product_title: Tommee Tippee Closer to Nature Anti-Colic Bottle
review_headline: Before I go into what I dislike, a few nice features are
review_body:
We bought these on a whim, as I am currently using the standard 5oz. Tommie Tippee bottles for my son and need some more bottles to send with him to daycare. I am exclusively pumping and feeding breastmilk via these bottles. I do have to supplement with formula occasionally. I have used this bottle twice thus far. Before I go into what I dislike, a few nice features are: Heat sensor along the internal 'anti-colic' device and the wide diameter nipple. This is the same nipple as seen in the standard bottle but I really like it as it mimics the breast well.

The problem I am having with this bottle is my son suckles hard and the nipple collapses on itself. This frustrates him (and me!). The nipple flow is faster than my '0' nipples and it is apparent when he can suck down 4 oz in no time. For those who are still breastfeeding, and have a slow let-down, this may cause an issue with your child. I was using faster flow nipples initially when I had to start formula and this caused an "instant gratification" issue with my babe. He was not happy to wait for my let down at the breast. Additionally, I tried to shake up some formula in the bottle without the colic device in place and it got everywhere. It would be nice if the company offered a cap with this type of bottle.

Overall, still happy with the company, but I will probably put these bottles aside until he is older. Coincidentally, the largest "spit up" I had with my son I a few weeks was after one of the feedings with this bottle. I certainly don't think it was directly causative and I haven't used the product enough to reliably comment on its 'anti-colic' properties.

The only thing that doesn't make it perfect is that the seat cushion is not as soft as I have expected, the waist support is not good enough, but if you put a pillow, it will be perfect.

I really recommend this item if you are looking for comfort and cost efficient glider and ottoman set. No one can beat this price!

review_headline: Not appropriate for a 22 pound child!
review_body: This seat is absolutely not appropriate for a child under two years old, regardless of of age and weight minimums Graco allows. This is a forward facing only seat, which is only safe until a baby is AT LEAST two years old according to the AAP and NHTSA. Just because the law in some states says a 12 month old can forward face does not mean it trumps the laws of physics. The bones in the vertebrate of a toddler does not fully ossify until 3-4, which is toddlers should be rear facing to the maximum height or weight of a convertible car seat. The nautilus is a great seat that passes the same safety testing as all other forward facing seats, but I urge Graco to join other major manufacturers who have raised their forward facing minimums to two years.

Example - when you push the button to turn on the screen (because it will go into a sleep mode when you have it unplugged from the wall), there is a noticeable lag time of a few seconds. review_headline: These work Perfect for little bellies!
review_body: These stackable reusable baby food containers are just what I needed. The first thing I look for on any plastic product is “BPA FREE.” That is a must and if you don’t know what I am talking about then you really need to look into. Never buy any plastic that doesn’t say BPA FREE. Now these baby food containers say spill proof and you better believe I am going to test them to their limit. We filled them with oatmeal. Oatmeal is thick so its great for testing “spill proof” containers. It has almost the same consistency as baby food but a little thicker. And should the container actually pop open, the thick oatmeal wont really spatter especially if its cold. So that’s my testing medium. Well I filled them all up, held them up, tossed them up in the air and let them fall. Test 1: no spills. Test 2: no spills. For test 3 I took one and threw it twice at a wall (outside of course) still no spill. Well they get an A+ for being spill proof. The portion is perfect for babies or snacks for school lunches like applesauce. After my oatmeal palooza I cleaned them out and they were really easy to clean. The container itself is durable and I can see myself using them over and over again. I am really glad that I tried this product. product_title: North States Quick-Fit Wire Mesh Gate
review_headline: Stops the robot, makes the cat hesitate
review_body:
Although we do not have children that we are trying to rein in, we do have a sprawling one level ranch house , two cats, and a robot vacuum cleaner. The cats are indoor cats, but one is allowed to play on the back deck every weekend when it is not raining. He often takes advantage of the momentary freedom and gets happy feet down the stairs and into and around the back yard. With the occasional stray cat to antagonize him and his occasional long distance forays, we were looking for something like this gate to cut off his exit and keep him on the deck. Similarly, although our robot vacuum comes with electronic walls, we sometimes want him to cover wider areas but necessarily have to limit him to a certain section of the house, or else he is liable to run out of power in a far flung, not often used room, making it hard to find him. We thought that if the cat gate could be easily and quickly moved, it would serve for this purpose as well.

This gate is all wood construction with plastic mesh, and it feels very solid and secure. Even when the robot runs into it at full speed, it doesn’t budge. It looks okay, not great, but most people who need things like this are not interested in a fashion statement, so much as keeping a pet or child safe. For those purposes, it looks, and is, effective. It works simply by extending the gate, then lifting the gate bar, sliding the plastic catch a little to tighten the bar, then pushing the bar down into place to secure the gate. If your opening is not exactly flat, like there’s a baseboard or something, you may end up with a crooked gate (see indoor photo, below), but if the surface level difference isn’t too egregious, the gate still closes up the opening. (Note in the photo how the gate spreads wider at the top than bottom. Also, the cat is stuffed and the robot electronic wall is at lower left.) During initial set up, reading the lame instructions was my only mistake, as they name parts of the gates by terms that don’t make sense and they don’t illustrate what they are talking about. But after one or two experimental tries, I had it figured out. I think most users will get the hang of it in no time.

As a robot limiter, the gate works great. It is wide enough to use in our foyer and halls, so we can cut off the distance the robot travels, but allow him to get to more areas of the house that need cleaning. Lately, we’ve been using this gate to cut off half the house at a time, then using the electronic walls to dictate the cleaning area. It is really great for this purpose. It’s also great for just keeping the robot in sections of joined rooms without closing doors (air flow issues) or using batteries (electronic wall issues).

As a cat limiter, however, it was less effective. While it did block the deck stairs, the cat eventually figured out that he could squeeze through the side railings, then easily step around the posts to the stairs. (Two more of these and we could completely cut the cat off, but with just one, it is only enough to make the cat have to think for a second until he finds his way down.) Thankfully, the quick fit design allows us to move the gate around and switch quickly from robot controller to cat confounder.

If you have something you need to block from accessing a room, whether is man, animal or machine, this gate is probably one of the best ways to do it. For the robot control alone, it is easily worth four stars, but throw in the cat retardant effect and the potential for other uses and it is easily worth a five star rating.n’t make sense and they don’t illustrate what they are talking about. review_headline: Requires 3/4" by 1 3/4" under cabinet to install these magnetic cabinet locks
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:7d8630cfd6154a7fdf804bfe95614e49]] I have to admit that I was a bit skeptic on how well these would work because of the magnetic way it opened and closed.I have a few cabinets that needed to be child proofed from my ever so curious toddler who is 2years old now.I have had these for over a month now and they work great.I have not had an issue with them so far.One thing to keep in mind is MAKE SURE YOU HAVE ENOUGH ROOM UNDER YOUR CABINETS to install these.For under the cabinet you need 1 3/4 of an inch by 3/4 of an inch to install the part that creates the \\"lock\\" action to these locks.I had a few that had that clearance so I had no issues with those until I used these on the hallway closet where I store my daughters arts & craft supplies and wanted them locked up.I did not have the clearance to install under the cabinet but luckily my previous tenant had installed a metal one that worked perfectly for locking onto the lock.It worked just as great and I was super happy it all worked out, so that is definitely something you want to keep in mind and check if you plan on getting these.
The part that installs on the backside of the cabinet door is about 1 1/2 by 1 1/2 inches.This part is where it contains the magnetic part that controls the unlocking and locking part of it.Check out my video I demonstrate how to use these and show you what you will be getting in this package.What is neat is it has a one and off latch that you press if you do not want to use the lock feature on it.This feature is great if you are going to be getting things in and out of it.You do not have to constantly use the key fob knob that comes with it.You get 4 latches that go under the cabinet and 4 corresponding pieces that go on the back of the cabinet door.One magnetic plastic covered disc that acts like a keyholder for your key fob knob.You only get one of these knobs to open all the cabinets with so make sure to put this somewhere you will always find it and out of reach of children.
The instrucitons are inside the paper in the packaging check out my video it is very thin and you may think there is no instructions.I almost skipped it because I could not find the instructions the paper is very thin so open it up and it will be there.They have these ruler guides for you to cut out and use as guides to install on your cabinets which are helpful.No screws are needed and no tools are needed, these are all installed using 3M strips that are pre installed on the pieces.So far I like them and they worked better than expected.They have not fell off nor has my toddler been able to get in the cabinets I installed these on and I have not had these malfunction on me either.My family comes over often and they like how neat these are.

review_headline: Never Lose a Sock in the Wash! -- Never Sort Them Again!
review_body:
Just adding more of these to the collection! Yeah, for me these are like 'designer' pins! I just bought some new socks! You'll see what I mean. I already purchased a set of 6 of [[ASIN:B00FB5AQPI Babies R Us Deco Diaper Pin]] and a set of 12 of these [[ASIN:B00G6AJYPK Sassy Deco Diaper Pins]] and before that, 6 more of a different design [[ASIN:B00H8N8YXC Deco Diaper Pins 6-pack]]. A while back, I found that these are very beautifully colored and/or decorated, much nicer in person than in the picture. These probably are also some of the strongest and most well-made pins I have owned. So, I've been buying more to replace some of the cheaper ones I've picked up over the years.

A few decades ago, I was living in a residence for a summer which had a housekeeper who took care of dinner, cleaning, and laundry. In explaining the rules of the residence, one of them was unlike any I have ever heard before. The housekeeper made it clear, \\"I don't sort socks! If you want them sorted, pin them together with Safety (Diaper) Pins.\\" So, in the next few days, I bought a bunch of these at the local supermarket and did as I was told. I found that pinning them at the bottom of the heel area made them easy to fold and put away.

Yes, I still use them! And, it's been over 25 years since I started. I never stopped pinning my socks together after I left the residence that year and assumed responsibility for doing my own wash once again. First of all, in all this time, I have never lost a sock! I might have lost a pair, but I never kept track of them that closely. I also learned something new that summer. I do not like to sort socks either! With this new knowledge, I was not going to go back to old ways. That would be quite stupid. What I thought might have been a cranky complaint, was actually a mouthful of wisdom.

I still have most of the pins I bought that summer. Every now and then I restock. Occasionally, I lose a pin or the plastic breaks for some reason or another. These, however, are constructed for the safety of babies. They are stainless steel and do not rust. When they close, they lock in a way that they must be deliberately opened. They are strong and can last through several decades of weekly washings. If you do the wash for a family, you can assign different colors (like these fancy ones) or one color like [[ASIN:9533223049 Stainless Steel Traditional Safety Pin]] or use [[ASIN:9533223065 Cloth Diaper Assorted Safety Pins)]] to each person so that you never have to figure out who belongs to which socks (another trick of the housekeeper). They are also a bargain when you consider the price.

review_headline: We tried using it as of 8 weeks as our baby had horrible reflux and could hold his head well

It is recommended as of 3 months so we only used it for a couple times while we were traveling as his regular chair wasn't with us. The tray option makes it great to keep baby in there once he starts being mobile. Currently my baby is 98 percentile both height and weight and almost 9 months and he is still using the gray insert in it, with extra room. The putty color is more of a beige/gray color, and not as brown as pictured in here.
I know this is not recommended and it specifically says not to, but we do use it in the bath without the tray. As long as the water is under the insert level, the chair stays put and it's a great in between a newborn bathtub and having him sit on his own. It makes daddy and baby bathing time much easier without mommy having to help!
We also got the toy for it, a lot of people complain it falls off, but I don't see how it wouldn't. It's done with suction cups, and you are meant to be able to take it off so that the tray can be used as a tray table later on. You can also feed the baby while sitting on the floor, which is helpful when you don't want to take the baby all the way to the kitchen or dining room.

product_title: The Piggyback Rider Standing Child Carrier - Basic Model
review_headline: Not an anti-gravity device and does not account for kids' attention span
review_body:
Like others have said, it's no anti-gravity device. Shoulders will hurt after 15-20 min and takes awhile to fit properly. The trick is to adjust it a little high so the top of the parent's head at about the child's chest level. This way they have room to lean forward a little and not tend to lean backwards instead. Another tip, the bar is metal, so make sure the kid has comfortable shoes on to withstand a hard piece of metal under their arch for an extended period. The kid will love getting on this thing but a lot of times they will want off fairly quickly too, so the safety harness becomes a hassle to take on/off.

Lately, we mostly use this thing to get our girl to class quickly. She's excited to get on and show off to her friends. No more waiting or negotiating for her to walk quickly to class. Jumps right on and is happy as can be the whole way there (at adult speed). Doesn't work for events or farmer markets. She wants off too often to check things out on her own. So it looks like a good product for getting your kid to/from BORING places where they are too lazy to walk. And maybe places where a higher vantage point benefits their viewing pleasure.

So, the product itself is pretty good. It would benefit from better load bearing design and a faster buckling system for the safety harness. Beyond that, everything else is your kid's fault (moving around, jumping up/down, wanting to get on/off, etc).

The baby's weight sits on your hips rather than in your back which makes this carrier a lot more comfortable than others. Easy to wear and put the baby in (except maybe for carrying in the back, I found it much easier when my husband helps to put the baby in). The baby also seems very comfortable and his position looks ergonomic. It is strong enough to keep him in this position and have his spine in a straight line. Compared to Baby K-tan for instance where I wasn't sure if he was in the right position because I found it much harder to set-up correctly. I haven't used the infant insert as my son was too big when we got it but we use the cushion from the infant insert to lift him up. He likes this carrier better than the original Ergobaby because he can see around and loves being in the front-looking position.
I also like this color combo, because it fits with everything. My husband also can use it (it's all easily adjustable) and it doesn't look feminine. The only suggestions I would have for Ergobaby is to create a carrying case. It has a lot of straps and it's not easy to keep nettly.

review_headline: Great for potty-training kids on long drives!
review_body:
We bought this for our potty-training kids to use on long drives through relatively remote/un-populated areas. It works great for that.
Pros:
The sides fold up and slide over the top of the seat, so it is a compact case, which I like better than some of the other travel potties. And it folds up and down easily.
The sides store a good amount of stuff. We put two small rolls of toilet paper (not new, but like 2/3rds gone) in one side and a dozen or so bags in the other. There's still lots of room for other stuff too.
It's pretty sturdy--it holds a 40 lb kid!
Regular gallon-sized ziploc bags fit the seat and they go on pretty easily. And I love that all I have to do is wipe down the seat with an antibacterial wipe, zip the bag, and we're done. There's not an entire seat to wash down.

Con:
The seat is flat. This enables it to have the cool design where it closes in on itself, but it means that there's the potential for your kid to miss because there's no front part to block it like on some other seats. This isn't enough of an issues to ever make me change seats though.

product_title: Graco Blossom 4-In-1 Seating System
review_body:
I really hate this high chair. I did sooo much research and this one was really well-rated. I really don't like anything about it, but here are my major issues with it:

1. There is a huge gap between the tray and my daughter - all of the food goes on to her lap. I have adjusted the seat as best I can but there's nothing I can do. Horrible design and so much food gets wasted. Also makes clean-up harder.
2. It's so hard to clean! The insert is useless and I took it off after about a month or so. I have to scrub the pad and still food just sticks. I would probably get a harder plastic chair if I could redo it.
3. The harness is difficult. It's 5 point, but you have to thread the top straps through the side straps into the main snap; it's hard to do with a squirmy kid. I also find it really dangerous, because the child can easily slip out while you're trying to snap the straps in place. I would've preferred a seat with a built-in tray.
4. Wheels - they don't really work. You really can't move this chair around. This isn't that big of a deal for me because the chair stays in the same spot, but if you need to move the chair frequently it'll get annoying.

Overall, it's a pricey high chair and I don't feel it's worth the price at all. I think next time around I'm going to buy a cheap Ikea high chair.

product_title: Silverette The Original Silver Nursing Cups - Soothing Sore Or Cracked Nipples with Silver
review_headline: These cups saved my nipples and nursing relationship. AMAZING.
review_body:
I got these about four weeks post-partum on the recommendation of my awesome IBCLC (International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant). She said they're big in Europe, and other Lactation Consultants she knew had been raving about them. They are pricy, but I was desperate -- my nipples were badly damaged from early latch issues, including several layers of tissue damage on one side (and missing tissue), bleeding wounds on both sides, plus persistent redness and soreness. Nursing and latching was going better, but my nipples just would not heal fast enough for me to not be in agony every time. I tried everything - Medihoney, Dr. Jack Newman's APNO by prescription, Earth Mama Angel Baby nipple butter, coconut oil, olive oil, exposing them to air, keeping them moist, saline rinses/soaks, sunlight, nipple shield (which promptly filled with blood when I tried using it). Nothing worked and I was almost ready to quit despite all the hard work we had done and the improvement in latching technique.
So. Desperate, I got these babies. And within hours my nipples had gone from bright red and painful looking to light pink and almost normal looking. Hours. I couldn't believe my eyes. I showed my husband and he agreed they looked like new nipples. The pain relief was also immediate though I was still not pain-free. But after a few days of wearing them, my nipples had made huge progress in healing. I never took them off after that, wore them 24/7 (and still do at 10 weeks postpartum), and my nipples healed almost completely. (I say almost because the one with the many layers of tissue damage had some permanent trauma damage that left me with vasospasms about half the time, so it still sometimes hurts...but nothing like before, obviously.) These Silverettes saved my nursing relationship. Ever since, I have recommended them to every nursing mom I know who is struggling in the early days. And with future babies, I will start wearing them 24/7 maybe even before the birth.
Some details:
For care, I wash them twice a day with baking soda paste. I wear them with a bamboo breast pad over them to catch leaks (and make the Madonna-nipple look less prominent). They do fill up a bit on the non-nursing side if you have a big letdown, so watch out for that (or purchase a Milkie milk saver). The rims do cut a little bit into your areola if they are not positioned just right or if the rim is on a Montgomery Gland (little bump on the areola). When this happens I just adjust them to be more comfortable. My nipples seem a bit dry sometimes wearing them, and maybe a bit greyish like the silver is changing their color. But I don't care about any of the inconveniences. These things save my life. You'll have to pry them from my cold, dead hands if you want me to stop wearing them!!!! They basically saved my nursing relationship with my baby.
That said, does anyone else who has worn them have tips on when you can stop wearing them, if ever? I've taken them off a couple of nights here and there when stomach sleeping, but otherwise I'm nervous to do so.me details:

product_title: myBaby SoundSpa Slumber Whale Projection and Noise Machine
review_body:
Bought this for my toddler when his more expensive projector/sound machine gave out after two years of use and abuse. It's an alright machine. The projector is a pretty low-quality with kitschy, dated illustrations and it's not nearly bright enough to use during daytime naps, but we turn it on at night and our kid likes to watch the pictures change while he falls asleep. It serves well as a nightlight too, and you can adjust the brightness with a knob on the side. So, it does the job and he's none the wiser, but the Munchkin Nursery Projector outperformed this machine in the projector department. The music is good - the sound quality is not bad and there are a variety of songs and nature sounds to choose from. I like the ocean sounds, but my toddler fiddles with the settings after I leave the room and usually chooses the lullaby. I find the lowest sound setting to be still a little loud - that's odd to me: usually anything that allows volume adjustment starts at 0, but this doesn't. Again, though, the kid doesn't mind, so I don't either.

Conclusion: it's a passable projector/sound system. It's survived abuse at the hands of my child for several months now, so that's a win in my book. The Munchkin Nursery Projector is of a higher quality, but much more breakable - because of that fact, and because I have a child who doesn't stay in his bed after lights-out, I'd choose this one over the Munchkin for now.

review_headline: Easy assembly, nice looking bed, great for the price!
review_body: We moved my 2.5 year old into this so we can re purpose his crib for his new sister. It's a very nice looking bed (ours is espresso)  For the price it seems sturdy enough (I probably wouldn't bounce on it myself, but it seems fine for him so far). It's a great price for what you get and I recommend it for a transition to twin bed. I wasn't sure whether to go right to a twin to save money but he was so attached to his crib and apprehensive about the idea of a new bed that I thought we'd try a toddler bed. I was happy to find this one at a price point I won't feel so guilty moving him to a twin in the next year or so.  Assembly was also SUPER easy. We had between afternoon nap time and bed time to take down the crib and put this one in it's place, and I was worried it would take forever like some furniture does (I'm looking at you IKEA!). It took my husband maybe 30m to put together, and my son liked "helping" put the bottom slats on. Not frustrating or time consuming at all!  Regular crib sheets fit fine on here, which is nice because after picking out a new toddler set to get him excited, my son begged for his old bedding back for familiarity!  1 year+  later review: My just turned 4 year old is still in this bed! I think we will move him when his baby sister moves out of her crib sometime in the next year or so, but so far this is still going strong. I think most people move their kids out of toddler beds sooner, but he seems to like the small space, and he's not too long for it yet! I suspect we will be able to use it for his sister. This was excellent value for the price especially!

product_title: Bubzi Co Baby Nasal Aspirator for Sinus Congestion Relief, Reusable Booger Snot Sucker for Smart Moms, Bonus Storage Case,Premium Mucus Extractor for Cold & Flu,Gentle Nose Cleaner Suction Infants
review_headline: Would not recommend if you cannot deal with ingesting your child's snot  on occassion- yes, even with tissue in the receptacle
review_body: I purchased this and a Nose Frida because I was truly torn when I read the reviews for both. If you are like me and it drives you nuts when people give you all the details of a story , then the main point at the end: I am returning this product for a refund and keeping the Nose Frida because despite placing tissue in the receptacle, I have orally ingested snot, not once, not twice, but thrice. I just can't stomach that anymore. I love my kid, but that really crosses the line into the grotesque for me. If it was an emergency type of situation, yes, I would orally ingest my child's snot, so stop judging me! Pros of the Bubzi as compared to the Nose Frida:  The Bubzi is a much smaller contraption, so it is much easier to hold and manipulate while single-handedly battling the anti-snot sucking toddler fury - particularly if you have small hands like me.  Also, it is easier to clean because it is smaller. I feel like I need a small tube brush to get the Nose Frida completely clean. Another Pro: Because this unit is smaller than the Nose Frida, it has less "dead space," and you need less lung power to suck snot. Pro: it had a cute, compact handy little carrying case that made it super portable. Pro: It got a good amount of snot out, but not quite as much as the Nose Frida (probably because there is less space for snot to accumulate). Con: Playing snot roulette - even with the tissue you just never know when snot is going to skedaddle up the tube and into your mouth. I just don't need that kind of grotesque mystery in my life. Con: Because it is so small and the receptacle is semi-opaque, it is difficult to gauge the amount of snot that is accumulating in the container, which increases the likelihood of you sucking snot into your mouth. The Nose Frida is bigger and is clear, so you can readily see how much snot is coming out and the tube is long and has a filter, so the likelihood of sucking up snot is nil, unless you have lung inhalation capacity on par with a Dyson vacuum, which I'm sure couldn't be good for your child's nasal cavity. So, with that said, I hope this review helps those who are on the fence about either product. Cheers and happy snot sucking!

product_title: Best Bottom Diaper Insert- Doubler 2 Pack
review_headline: Great doubler for a quality diaper!
review_body: We've been using Best Bottoms diapers exclusively since our daughter outgrew newborn diapers (over 3 months) and have had a great experience.  When fitted correctly, we did not have any leakage or blowout issues until she started sleeping through the night. We purchased these micro-doublers for night time use and haven't had a wet bed since.  I was a little apprehensive about adding more bulk to the diapers since they are a little bulky as it (not unreasonably so, just bigger than a disposable), but found that the doublers add a great deal of absorbancy with very little added size.  As I wash my diapers every other day, I purchased 4 doublers( two small and two medium) so that we would have back-up.  We have the diaper on the smallest size right now, so the small doublers are the ones that fit best, but I use the medium doublers with my small stay dry inserts and have had no issues.  I simply snap the doubler to the insert and fold the little bit of excess under when I snap them into the shell.  I intend to buy two larges and do the same when she outgrows the small inserts. I have not tried using a smaller size doubler on larger insert, but plan to when she is using the large inserts.  Instead of paying for 12 doublers, I will only have to buy a total of 6 (2 small, 2 medium and 2 large) between now and the time she potty trains. I have and will continue to recommend this product to my friends who are interested in going with cloth diapers.

review_body: Terrible bottle brush!  I bought this following my first year with an Oxo Tot Bottle Brush.  That brush last forever and was really good at cleaning the bottles. I liked the spongy top to the main part of the brush, however the bristles below it are so sparse and stiff that I find they don't clean the bottles at all.  The top piece is a plastic covered metal which completely rusted out within 2-3 months of use.  I expected to get a lot longer use out of this brush and was severely disappointed in its effectiveness to clean.  I really recommend going for a more expensive bottle brush, like the Oxo Tot Bottle Brush. We have enough stressors as Moms and Dads.  We don't want to agonize over cleaning the bottles.  We want to clean them quick, effectively and move on!  We also don't want to be shopping for bottle brushes every 2-3 months.

product_title: Graco My Ride 65 LX Convertible Car Seat, Coda
review_headline: first time mom happy with this decision
review_body: **review edit: 1-31-16    We have now had this car seat for over 6 months  and have had the chance for plenty of use in it.  Our baby seems most comfortable . We have had to remove the seat several times between are multiple cars and installation between each car happens without any problems of course after the proper adjustments made to seating and such. Also adjusting the straps and lap belts easy.    Original post:  I'm a first time mom - baby is almost one & I'm 8 and half months pregnant with number 2 - so the last few weeks I've been researching all the best top rated brands of car seats and finally chose graco's my ride 65 LX. The seat arrived promptly and installation was a breeze  (this is what I was dreading the most.).  We have a 2007 Honda CRV and it took the husband and I like 20 minutes to install. We installed it forward facing. Our Honda's seat needed to be reclined just the slightest along with the head rest needed to be notched up. I would just advise before installing in car be sure to adjust straps to babies size. We forgot and had to remove and do it again  (even then we said wow, this is so easy to get set up & installed) and the adjusting to straps was easy. there are clear Instructions to follow printed on the car seat itself and of course In manual. We used the latch and also looped seat belt thru. Extra protection we figured. The delivery was amazingly fast we only got it a few days ago and baby  has only been in  it twice, but I have to say he seems really comfy not squished and even fell asleep in it and his head was fine didn't slump forward like some other reviews  advised. I apologize for the long run review but like I said, I've been researching a lot and was left with a lot of questions that put crazy skeptic thoughts in my head. (Mom brain.... ugh!) I'm really glad I bought this graco and if anything changes I'll  update since baby had only had 2 short trips in it.

product_title: Munchkin Soft-Tip Infant Spoon, 6 Count
review_headline: Creates Less Than Ideal Messes, Not Great in Dishwasher
review_body:
I can't say these are the best spoons. From what I've experienced with my early eater, they are somewhat difficult for younger babies to get used to. The spoon part is a bit too deep, so they can't get the food out of the spoon unless you start with a pretty big spoonful, which can get pretty messy pretty quickly! When we first started on solids/purees this was actually helpful for us because she never had too much in her mouth from each spoonful. However, as she quickly learned to eat from a spoon, she became very frustrated unless the spoonfuls were large enough for her to get an adequate amount from each scoop. It really created more mess than anything else! We have other baby spoons (our favorites are the gerber graduates spoons!), and we don't experience this issue with the others.

These spoons are intended to be dishwasher safe. We feed our daughter solids once or twice a day and have been for the past three months. We rotate through all the spoons, and we do wash them in the dishwasher. After only three months of rotated light use, the colors have begun to fade off many of the spoons. They are starting to look old after only a few months!

On the plus side, the colors are fun and eye-catching for little ones. They are easy to grip for both parents and kids. But overall, not recommended!

Unfortunately for me we have two cameras for this unit so it would be quite expensive to replace with a different brand. I would 100 % advise you not to buy this unit. Moving forward I will only buy something with a replaceable battery. I have an AngelCare monitor with replaceable/rechargeable batteries. product_title: Infantino Flip Advanced 4-in-1 Convertible Carrier, Light Grey
review_headline: Fantastic carrier, great price, and baby loves it!
review_body: We've been using the moby since baby was born, but it's getting too hot to use for long in the summer, and I wanted something easier and faster to use for an upcoming flight. I was looking at the ergo 360, but was having trouble swallowing the price tag. I looked at these online, but just couldn't decide. I checked them out in store at Walmart, and loved it! I tried it on in the store to see if it would be comfortable, and ended up putting baby in it and buying the empty box as I wore it out of the store. It fits me very well (5'5", size 12ish). I can put it on and get baby in by myself (the trick is to fast the top back buckle and slip it over your head), and baby feels secure and comfortable. So far I've used it twice in the 2 days we've had it, and both times baby fell asleep. It's much more breathable than the Moby and has good air flow. Baby is currently 3 months old and about 11 lbs, and this works great for her facing in with the narrow seat (her legs are in the correct M shape). I don't think she would have been able to use it much earlier, based on where her head is in the carrier, so I think much younger than 3 months may have to wait a bit. I'm so glad I checked this out before spending $100+ more on the Ergo 360.

product_title: Ingenuity Moonlight Rocking Sleeper Deluxe- Seneca
review_body: This sleeper is a great outfit to use around the house and especially perfect for travel. We have a full-sized crib in our bedroom, but my wife does a lot of sewing at home and now she can have our new son resting comfortably and safely nearby as she sews. Then it is not hard to move it to the kitchen if she is working in there. The way this folds up, it is still somewhat wide but quite flat, perfect for stowing in the back of our mini-van without consuming much space.    The vibrator gadget that clips on the side rail may be helpful for soothing your baby, like the light/sound/dangling toy gadget that mounts to the other rail. I'm not super enthused about more gadgets that need batteries, but there are times when it is worth trying anything to get a baby to quiet down and sleep. Both are easily removed for transport. The battery requirement of three \\"AA\\" cells currently stated in the product description here is incorrect. The vibrator uses one \\"C\\" cell, and the sound thing uses three \\"AAA\\" cells.    The rocking aspect of this sleeper is just hand-powered rocking. Stops at the ends of the rockers limit the rocking motion very conservatively.    The sleeper is designed for babies from newborn to about 5 months of age. It should not be used once the baby starts to get to the crawling stage, for safety reasons. It must be sturdy enough; our 2.5 year old just had to get in it and try it out too, and it held her without damage.    I personally would prefer to give up one or both of the gadgets and pay a lower price for the basic sleeper, but overall I think this is a very good product.

I have it on the gentle bird sound for waking up though, so maybe if I made it on the rooster mode it would wake her up. But truth be told, I don't mind if she sleeps in a little bit. So that's why it doesn't concern me right now. But when she does wake up and sees it is morning, she just gets up and puts her clothes on and goes to the potty without even being asked.
Totally new child I have.

product_title: HappyEndingsTM 5 Layer Charcoal Bamboo Inserts for Cloth Diapers
review_body:
Of the cloth diaper inserts we have tried, these are my favorites. We have used bumGenius microfiber and Alva Baby inserts, as well as Green Mountain Diaper workhorse fitted diapers. These inserts are very absorbent and they do not take a very long time to dry. I use them in pocket diapers as well as in covers by themselves. My favorite combination right now is one of these inserts in a Thirsties Duo Wrap. They are stay dry, so I do not have to worry about them being right up against my toddler's skin.

One thing which may be considered a con to some is that these are thick. However, I find they are thinner than using a prefold as an insert. Also, in the past, I have noticed our inserts have lost their absorption capabilities and needed to be washed/rinsed several extra times. This may be due to the hard water we have in combination with our front loading washing machine. Last week, I soaked our inserts overnight with Rock n Green Hard Core Concentrate and then washed them without adding detergent. This definitely helped and I plan to repeat the process to regain maximum absorption.

Mostly I use these inserts during the daytime. At night, we use Huggies Overnights. So far, we have not had any leaks with those. When we have tried the HappyEndings inserts, even doubled, we have had leaks or a baby waking at night due to wetness. In all fairness, though, we have tried several brands of disposables at night with limited success.

Overall, I am very happy with these inserts and plan to order more. I will also be ordering the newborn size available through Amazon soon.

product_title: Tiny Love Soothe 'n Groove Mobile
review_headline: Wonderful mobile - twirling colorful animals and a wide choice of music
review_body:
I bought this mobile for my grandson when he was only two months old - a mere two weeks after he had life-saving heart surgery. His parents had another Tiny Love mobile at their house and I was going to watch him during the weekdays while he recovered and they had to work. Little did any of us know how long his recovery would take (he had breathing and eating issues because of the underlying cause.) I was pleased to have him with me for many months and I still watch him several days a week now that he is a big boy of 20 months and recovered fully.

This mobile was really a life-saver for me. Because of his many issues, I had to watch him pretty much like a hawk. I still wanted to engage him during period when he had to lie down and this was the perfect way to do so. He loved watching the characters turn around and around and glide up and down (sometimes twisting as they went.) The music is so soothing, too. It can be bright and cheerful or even mimic that of a mother's heart beat. He could sometimes be still under it for up to 20 minutes - which was a real break for me and a fun time for him.

I kept it in his crib until he could reach up and grab the animals. Then, sadly, I had to remove the twirling portion. To this day, though, I still have the music box in his crib. When he wakes up from nap, the first thing he does is go turn the music on and then starts dancing to it. I can always hear it through the monitors and I know that he is awake and it is time for me to pick him up.

The batteries last a really long time. I have never had to change mine. I know that I don't use it as much as it would be used at his own house, but I did use it multiple times a day for months and still several times a day on the days when he visits. When he is out of his crib and into his toddler bed full time, I plan to move the toy to being a hand-held music box for him to carry around.

Honestly, for the amount of money spent, I think it is the purchase that I have made that has provided the most and longest return. I'm hoping for more little ones to come as I loved seeing the animals twirl about. It really speaks to the durability of the mobile that I am sure that it will still be in good working order in the future. I highly recommend this mobile as well as other toys by this manufacturer.have made that has provided the most and longest return. I'm hoping for more little ones to come as I loved seeing the animals twirl about. It really speaks to the durability of the mobile that I am sure that it will still be in good working order in the future. I highly recommend this mobile as well as other toys by this manufacturer.

product_title: Philips AVENT Double Electric Comfort Breast Pump
review_headline: The search ends here...this is breast pump you are looking for (unless you need one that can run on battery power!)
review_body:
In short, I love it. There's been so much good stuff written about this product, that I kind of thought it would be best to use my review to take a different tack and handily summarize everything I love about it in an easy-to-read list (and to also point out a few potential drawbacks that prospective buyers should keep in mind). Without further ado:

PROS:
--The 2015 version adds a large size cushion
--Nice compatibility with AVENT bottles; they will all work with this product (even older ones)
--Very nice travel bag included (I believe this is included in the 2014 version as well, but that was the first year of it)
--Milk won't back up into the tubing thanks to a well-designed barrier system
--Relatively quiet although arguably a bit louder than older models
--You really can travel around the world with this thing: it works with 100V - 240V (you'd have to buy the appropriate adapter for non-US outlets but it will support it)
--2-Year warranty
--Very, very comfortable to use and lightweight, compact design
--Reasonably priced

CONS:
--You HAVE to use AVENT bottles; it's made specifically for them (but at least older AVENT bottles will work with it); no pumping directly into a bag.
--Even though there are 3 suction setting, the product seemingly would benefit from a wider range to be more accommodating to personal preferences of the women using it. I am totally fine with the settings available; however, I could see why some might complain about this.
--No battery, so no outdoor usage. To me, that's the biggest drawback.

product_title: Summer Infant Extra Camera for Sharp Sight High Definition Video Baby Monitor (29340)
review_headline: Too loud. Too bright. Awful when you're trying to sleep. But great for day time monitoring.
review_body:
We've used 4 low-resolution baby monitors and felt high-definition was overkill, but certainly wouldn't turn it down. Similarly, pan and tilt is overrated, but are welcome features.

At first, there was a lot to love. The monitor was large. The display was crisp and highly visible. We really like not having a flip-up antenna. Even without the external antenna, signal was strong and seldom dropped. The stand doubles as a handy pocket clip, which none of our other monitors had. The stand uses friction retention, so it can be adjusted to any angle you'd like, but eventually the retention will wear out and there's no way to retention it. By then, hopefully, your Baby has outgrown the need for a monitor. The noise-meter is highly visible and colored for easy identification. The talk feature is underrated. It's so handy to be able to soothe Baby remotely. There is a very short delay in the feed, shorter than most. However, the delay in the pan & tilt was pronounced. This makes it somewhat challenging to use precisely. You have to click a direction and wait for the motion, then click again, etc. Not a big deal, but something to note. Also, another minor nuisance is the unintuitive directional buttons. Look closely at the image and you'll see the arrows are stacked to the right rather than a cross. Typically, once you've gotten the camera angle where you want it, you never touch those again, so it's really a trivial issue, but worth noting.

The real deal-breakers were the overly sensitive microphone and brightness of the screen. Even though the camera is in the second floor nursery, it will pick up noises from all over the house to the point where I can clearly make out conversations in the kitchen and family room on the first floor. On top of that, even when the volume is adjusted to minimum, it's too loud. The general hiss of ambient noise is distracting when we're going to sleep, but the sound of Baby rustling her blankets when she moves is loud enough to actually wake us. We're not light sleepers. So some nights, we turned the volume off, which defeats the purpose of a nighttime baby monitor. Likewise, the brightness of the screen at minimum is way too bright. It's brighter than a night light. It's so bright, we sleep facing away from it. No exaggeration. We put up with it as long as we could, but after 2 weeks of poor sleep, I swapped it out for one of our other monitors.

However, there's hope. This is not a bad tool, it just doesn't suit us as a nighttime baby monitor. So don't use it at nighttime, use it in the day time. The advantage of high definition is largely lost in darkness because the picture i black and white. It really shines in the day when the colors are visible. You can see a lot of detail. If your child is old enough to play with limited supervision, perhaps you can use this camera to keep an eye on them without hovering. Or use this when Baby is napping. You can do whatever you need to do with the monitor clipped to your hip, and you can be certain you won't miss the sound of your baby crying.

product_title: Safety 1st Heavenly Dreams Stars a Plenty Baby Mattress
review_headline: Looks & feels like a great mattress
review_body:
I opened the package when it arrived and was extremely surprised by how substantial this crib mattress felt. I read the great reviews and figured it must be pretty good to get all those reviews, so I was expecting a good mattress, still when my husband and I opened the box I was pleased to find a thick mattress that looks like a REAL mattress, not just a piece of foam. I said, "Wow, you can see how this mattress will work with our crib to be a toddler bed when the baby is older!" I felt so pleased, because we got this at such an affordable price, and it will do double duty with our convertible crib, so we can use it for the next few years to come. I can easily see our tiny baby, growing into a toddler and still sleeping on this mattress at 4 years old. The reviews said it stood up to years of use, and it certainly looks solid. So I was very happy with my purchase. Also, it feels like it would be comfortable to sleep on, yet it's safely firm (a baby mattress must be firm, not too soft, to reduce risk of SIDS). I also like the waterproof covering which saved me more money (I was going to purchase a separate mattress cover as you usually have to, to protect the mattress from stains due to the likelihood of spills). So, so far so good, but I'll update my review after our baby arrives and sleeps in it!
PS - update, we put our crib together (it was a Stork craft model) and the mattress is a perfect, snug fit, just like the other reviewers said it was, so we feel very good about this mattress, no worries about gaps.

review_headline: Great umbrella stroller, easy to fold, sturdy, lightweight

The Summer Infant 3D lite stroller is a great umbrella stroller for a family on-the-go. The stroller is very light and easy to open and close. We took the stroller to a theme park for two days. Even though it is an umbrella stroller, it is remarkably sturdy and very easy to maneuver. Both our 2 year old and 8 month old sat in it and were very comfortable. They both liked the recline feature - there are three positions. The only thing that we didn't like about the stroller is that you need both hands to recline the seat. You need to press tabs on both sides in order to recline the seat, if your baby is sitting or sleeping in the stroller you need to make sure their weight is not on the seat before reclining - since you are using both hands you can't control how fast the seat will go back when you press the buttons.

Our 2 year old was able to use the footrest to climb in and out of it easily. I was even able to rest my purse and bag on the handles without it tipping over. We especially love the large storage space below as well as the little pocket behind the seat to put a phone or keys. The sunshade canopy is large and covers baby well.

The Summer Infant 3D lite stroller is the best umbrella stroller we've tried. The stroller has kept up with our active lifestyle and easily travels to the park or theme park. Our favorite things about this stroller is the lightweight frame, easy to maneuver, fast fold/carrying strap, large storage space and recline feature.

These are wonderful for any mom who is constantly on the go or even if you have a babysitter for a night that you can pre-fill these dispensers with formula and snacks so they know exactly what to feed the kids. I can't speak for the 30AA end of the spectrum, but my wife was (professionally) sized at 36GG and this actually fit, though barely.

The velcro adjustment strap that allows for such a wide range in sizes is STRONG! 2 months straight of multiple daily uses and the velcro is still holding great, though fabric in other places is starting to tear (again, while the s-l size does fit, the fabric is being put through the paces...).

review_body:
I love this mattress protector. We own this and the full size crib cover from American Baby and they are both great. I wanted something with an organic top layer to lesson any chemical fumes; the backing is polyurethane, I believe, but anything waterproof is going to have a non-organic substance. At least the surfaces closest to baby are organic. This is soft, with just enough padding to make it comfortable but still plenty safe for baby, especially with a fitted sheet on top. It easily fits both on our mini-crib mattress and our longer Graco pack-n-play mattress.

I've been washing it for years and drying it on LOW heat with no problems. It often takes two drying cycles, but it has never melted or shrunk. Make sure it has spun well in the washer and that there are no puddles of water trapped in the corners before you stick it in the dryer. The waterproofing has kept our mattress safe through all diaper leaks, but isn't loud or crinkly.

product_title: Munchkin LATCH Transition Cup, 4 Ounce
review_body:
I’m a new mom without a bunch of money so it’s important to me to know I’m getting good products for my son that will not only work but be worth the money. This sippy cup is both! It’s really easy to clean—it comes apart nicely and cleans great on the top shelf of the dishwasher. The handles are big enough for him to easily grip them but not so big they’re unwieldy for him or too widely spaced that it’s an effort for him to keep a grip on them. They’re just the right size and height. It’s also a stubby cup so it doesn’t take up a ton of space in the diaper bag.

But the BIG thing about this is the nipple/sippy cup top. It’s amazing. My son still isn’t sitting so he likes to lay on his activity mat with his head on a pillow and a bottle. I was worried transitioning him to a sippy cup would result in lots of mess and discomfort for my toothless tot. Not so! He’s able to hold this thing upside down and shake it and it doesn’t leak but he gets a good, even flow when he drinks from it. It’s made with soft, clear silicone so it’s great for sore gums and little teeth but also provides a perfect transition for bottle to sippy cup. It also features an ingenious vent or valve in the bottom that creates an even flow of liquid when he drinks but doesn’t leak. AT ALL!

My son is on cereal because formula isn’t enough anymore and it handles oatmeal and rice products just fine without getting clogged.

I would recommend you get a small nipple brush to clean out the valve and mouthpiece if you use a dishwasher because they are so watertight that they don’t drain but that’s a good thing! You know they’re not going to leak. I can’t recommend this highly enough!

review_headline: this crib is excellent. The assembly wasn't too hard
review_body: For the money, this crib is excellent. The assembly wasn't too hard, it is solid and really looks way more expensive than it is. The color is very nice if you like the dark stained wood look. It is a darker shade than the picture here seems to show. Our 6 month old (he is about 15lbs and 20 inches tall) outgrew his bassinet and this crib is perfect. The ONLY negative thing I found is that the finish scratches very easily and will not hold up well to normal use unless you are really careful. I only wish I knew of a non-toxic clear coat spray to coat the rails with because they will see the most use. I disagree with many of the reviews about the stock plastic coated 1 1/2" mattress. It is the appropriate thickness for a smaller baby and is firm, but not hard. If you read anything about SIDS, you'll know you don't WANT a thick, plush soft mattress. It breathes fine when covered with a mattress pad and sheets and our baby sleeps fine on it. Others here didn't like the MDF board that supports the mattress--I think it's fine. It is not designed to hold a tremendous amount of weight and it has a cross member in the center that makes pretty strong -- *within reason* -- no, it will not bear the weight of an older child jumping in it or a sleepy parent falling into it. I took a picture of the under side.

product_title: Premium Double Breast Pump W/ Shoulder Tote - Essential For The Breastfeeding Mother - Electric Breastpump For Personal Use - Includes 4 Bottles, 4 Caps, 2 Tubes W/ Connection Valves, 6 Batteries, 2 Breast Shields Sizes (80mm, 76mm, 74mm)
review_headline: A good pump makes ALL the difference!
review_body:
I have always struggled with getting enough milk with a breast pump. I have a manual pump from Medela and a double electric pump from Evenflo. I've had the manual pump for about 10 years. It's actually my better working pump. It has suction and I am able to control the pressure myself. The one from Evenflo I got used (but it was only used a few times). I know, I know. Gross. I took it apart and sterilized it, but found out later that it could still have contaminates in it. I only used it for a few months. Even after buying new parts it would lose suction and was useless.

I was never able to get more than 1 or 2 ounces of milk a day. It was very depressing and I was never able to store much milk, since it would take a week to get a days worth of milk for my baby. It is always said that you can NOT compare your amount you pump to the amount you're feeding your baby. It is still a little worrisome when your body won't respond to a pump. Is my body doing enough? My babies are not those fat, chunky babies. I have little, skinny kids. They look like my brother and I did. Still, I always wonder.

I recently had the exciting opportunity to review a brand new breast pump. My most exciting mommy day recently was when UPS dropped off my Natures Bond Premium Double Electric Breast Pump. I was so excited!

I immediately pulled it all out and took and inventory. I checked it over and was so thrilled to see what all it included.

Features & Benefits:• Personal-use electric breast pump

• Designed with 2 pumping modes

• Airlock design helps protect breast milk and baby from bacteria, mold and viruses while pumping

• Capable of single and double pumping

• Lightweight and portable for added convenience

• BPA-free

• AC Power Adapter

• Kit comes equipped with shoulder tote bag and milk storage cooler bag

• Includes 4 milk collection bottles with lock-tight sealing lids, 2 tubes with connection valves, 4 caps, 6 batteries and 2 of each of the following breast shield sizes: 80mm, 76mm and 74mm

I took all the tubes, bottles, caps, and breast shields and sterilized them in water I had boiled. I then set them to the side to dry completely. After that, I put it all in the tote bag and gave it a try.

I discovered something amazing. A good pump makes ALL the difference! I went from getting 1 ounce to actually pumping 6 ounces in one sitting!!! I started with the let down mode. It made tiny little sucks to get the milk in. I then pushed the button and it changed to the pumping mode. I was able to control the suction easily with the push of a button. The light tells me what suction setting it's on. It's very quiet compared to my old electric pump. It makes the humming and pumping noise, but it's not loud and doesn't disturb my family. My baby guy also becomes obsessed with it. He loves it and comes over to touch it as it has a vibration that he seems to be obsessed with. Ha Ha Ha. Silly guy. My old pump he hated and always tried to swat it away.

The Natures Bond pump also has the ability to use batteries (6 AA), which lasted me a couple long pumping sessions, or you can use the AC power adapter if you have a close power source. The lights on the pump will also change colors according to the battery power. Green is a full battery. Yellow is warning you that the batteries are getting low. I didn't let it get past yellow, because I could tell the suction was lower and I didn't want to risk stressing the pump.

This is a brand I hadn't heard of before, but after using Natures Bond, I will definitely recommend them to my friends and followers. I am so happy that I am now able to pump and store my milk. This is such a blessing to me, and it has really boosted my confidence in my body's ability to make milk and nourish my baby.

A few breastfeeding tips:
•Drink enough water. You want to make sure you are staying hydrated or your milk supply will go down.
•Eat enough calories. This would be between 2,000 and 2,500 calories per day for a breastfeeding woman.
•Eat healthy foods. Make sure you are getting the proper nutrition. This will help keep your and your baby healthy.
•Get enough rest. Being tired or under a lot of stress can cause your milk supply to suffer. Your physical and mental state can make a big difference in your milk supply. Try to get rest when you can. A mother never seems to get enough, but if you are able to catch a nap here and there, that will really help.
•Eat foods that help your milk supply. Foods like oatmeal, Red Raspberry Leaf tea, Mother's Milk tea, brewers yeast, fenugreek, lactation cookies (yum!), garlic, carrots, nuts (Cashews, almonds, and macadamia nuts), fennel, green (unripe) papaya, sesame seeds, ginger, and (if your a natural minded mom that's up for something super adventurous) placenta capsules (warning - graphic content).

review_body:
I so wanted to love this and in a lot of ways, I do. I just wish it were a little bit refined, which is why I’m giving it one less star. I will say, it’s been really handy for our family.

I received it as a gift and while a wipe warmer seemed like a gimmick, I ended up with a newborn that would have a complete meltdown the second his bottom hit air!! Enter the wipe warmer. I’d heard these things were a waste of money because they dried out wipes and turned them a weird yellow color. Not so the mist warmer from Munchkin.

It’s such a brilliant idea and it does work really nicely. It has some great features like the power cord that separates so when your darling child kicks the wipe warmer off the changing table or you get a stuck wipe in the opening, it won’t get ripped out of the wall. It also makes it portable, which is really handy.

The mister works great. My wipes have come out nicely warm, my son and his bottom are happy and they’re still damp with no dried out patches or weird colors so it definitely works.

However, the latch on mine doesn’t always want to snap back in place so it pops back open again. The plastic is a bit too soft I have to make a point of popping it back and checking it’s latched. That sounds like a small thing but when it’s 3am, you have a fussy baby that you’re changing in the dark because you don’t want to wake him properly and you have to mess with a latch that won’t stick, it gets old. If you don’t bother to check, your wipes dry out, which defeats the object.

I also love the misting function and it does keep wipes moist but it also dilutes the cleaning product on the wipes. I use the Pampers Sensitive wipes and I like them because the cleaning product moisturizes while you’re wiping so they drift across baby’s bottom. This warmer takes some of the product off and warms the wipes to the point that they get soft and scratchy (I guess they’re made with plastic so it stretches). The wipes just seem to lose their integrity. This may be different with a more paper-based wipe like Huggies wipes.

All in all, it’s been great and I use this thing every day. It’s definitely better than I had expected and I can’t imagine changing my little fuss-pot in the middle of the night without it. Seriously. He HATES cold diapers. I just wasn’t as floored by it overall as I had hoped. Munchkin products are usually really well developed and I felt the latch issues let it down. If you need a wipe warmer though, it’s definitely a must-have.

product_title: Keekaroo Height Right Highchair with Insert & Tray - Chocolate - Mahogany Base
review_body:
We bought this chair for our first and are still using it now that she is almost three! When we first used it to start feeding her solids she was too small to fit comfortably in it. We put a pillow behind her to make her fit more snugly and also to keep her from banging her head on the back head rest as she liked to get in and start flailing around. I wish we would have bought the infant insert as I think that would have solved the problem. As she grew, I found the tray very convenient and easy to pull in and out of the chair. This was especially helpful as she started feeding herself and making big messes on the tray. I also liked that the plastic cover on the tray pops off for even more convenient cleaning.

But the thing I love most about this chair is how it grows with baby. We still use it now as her "big girl" chair with the tray removed. We pull her right up to the table so she is at the perfect height. We have adjusted the foot rest and seat a few times as she grows and it's really simple to get the perfect fit.

Now that our second is getting close to starting solids, we will be buying another of these chairs but with the infant insert this time. I gave it only four stars because you really do need the infant insert for smaller babies or your child won't fit in the chair as is. This is a great chair overall that will be used for years as your child grows.

product_title: Munchkin Latch Spinning Drying Rack
review_headline: Best Baby Purchase in a Long Time!
review_body:
I never write reviews, but I love this product so much I took to Facebook about it. While surfing Amazon tonight, I saw this and felt compelled to weigh in.
When our daughter graduated from bottles to sippy cups, we had to change drying racks. I bought 5 different namebrands and took them home to compare. This one was the obvious choice with the other contenders falling way short. Now here's what I love about it:
1) The arms fold down for storage but are very solid when clicked into their upright position. They do not wobble like other brands and you don't have to assemble them yourself, as they are already connected.
2) Both levels rotate like a lazy susan, which is very convenient when you're washing more than 4 bottles/cups at once.
3) The base was very thoughtfully designed. It has 2 cutouts on the sides so you can slide your fingers underneath to easily pick it up when cleaning the countertops. It is concave so that dripping water rolls to one side, through a drain hole, and into a collection receptacle under the base.
4) The receptacle has a little tray that can easily be pulled out and emptied. If you have an undermount sink, you can insert the tray backwards and a tilted lip protrudes about 2 inches so the water drains directly into your sink.
4) The upper level is my favorite because it has so many neat features that multiply it's functionality. A) We put the sippy cups on the lower level and the lids hang perfectly balanced on the shorter upper arms. B) We also dry the infant medicine syringes (taken apart) on these upper arms. C) In between each upper arm is a slot to hang nipples or pacifiers, with each having 3 graduated holes to accommodate various sizes. D) The drain holes are shaped like slits and we discovered they are perfect for drying our steak knives that we hand wash. E) Surrounding the center cup are 8 round holes that work great for drying the Tervis style hard plastic straws. F) The center cup is the icing on the cake. It has drain holes in the bottom and we use it for our daughters forks and spoons. It basically holds anything that won't fit in any of the other places mentioned above. G) And in case you were wondering, the upper level can adjust to 3 height settings if vertical space is an issue.
I have not used the Munchkin Latch system but it looks like this drying rack was specifically designed for those bottles. As you can see, we have enjoyed this dryong rack ever since I took it out of the box. I can only imagine that it would be even more perfect if we were using it with the Latch system it was designed for.
Please know that this is a very sturdy, solid rack. It is made of high quality hard plastic and the turntables rotate freely. Let me conclude by saying that I do not buy inferior, flimsy products. I am very detail oriented and very picky. If find that a product has an annoying feature I will usually replace it (we went through 6 bottle brushes before finding one that was adequate, but even that one could be improved). I want the best of the best and I don't mind paying a premium for it. That being said, this rack is surprisingly very economically priced. Two of the others I considered were priced a good bit higher. If I could give this product an extra star, I would. Great job as usual Munchkin!

review_headline: Mold issue! Beware, do not buy!
review_body: I purchased two of these for my kids. Within a month or so I started noticing discoloration on a bottom corner. I didn't think much of it as it just looked like a small water stain. In the next few weeks the stain gradually grew bigger and turned black. Eeeeek. Black mold on the lunch bag? I called the manufacturer and told the call center rep that I had mold on my lunch bags. I also told her that I cleaned it according to manufacturer instructions. The lady was very friendly and told me, that if anything spilled or if you had lots of condensed water on a cold drinking bottle, the liquid would/could enter through the inside seams and ends up trapped between the silver inner liner and the laminated canvas outer shell. The laminated outer shell prevents the spill from drying which results in mold in between the layers. She also mentioned that this was not dangerous for the kids (yeah right) but she offered to replace both of my children's lunch sacks for free. I was told to be more careful with the replacements and to always make sure to put a few layers of paper towel in the bottom to help absorb possible spills and prevent moisture from getting into the stitching again. I received my new lunch sacks and did EXACTLY as I was told. I wiped the bag with a damp wet cloth if something spilled and replaced my paper towel liner daily! It's been two month now and again I'm am starting to see the mold spread in between the layers on both kids lunch sacks. This is ridiculous. This is disgusting, this is not made for children, this is unsanitary and most of all this is a complete waste of money

product_title: Kidco Anti-Tip TV Strap (2)
review_body: Could have been 5 stars except that the bolts did not fit my Samsung UN48H6350 TV that I purchased from Amazon. The bolts were the right type (M8) but too short, meaning I had to make a trip to the hardware store. Also the plastic ends that attach to the wooden furniture were installed on the straps the wrong way,  I had to take them off and rotate them so they would go flush against the wood and match the photo of the installed product.  For anyone who has the same TV, the M8 bolts need to be 26mm (approx 1 inch) long.  The ones that come with the product are only about 13mm (1/2 inch) long.  For mounting to the wooden furniture, if its "hardwood" you should drill holes, otherwise it will be very hard to screw the screws in by hand.  I used a 5/64 drill bit but check the diameter of the screws they give you first.  Other than all that, looks like a good product.

product_category:
BEST.STROLLER.EVER.

I have four kids. I have had every stroller known to man. This stroller is amazing. I have an SUV with almost no trunk space. I can grocery shop AND have a stroller in the back - a miracle!

I have travelled everywhere with this stroller. It has carried my 7 (yes, 7 lol) and 5.5 year old through Disneyland when they were exhausted and too tired at the end of the day.

It has gone along the cobbled streets of Paris with no problem. It has come on the plane with us. You name it, it has been there and has handled each situation like a boss.

The fact that you can put an infant car seat directly onto the seat and just clip a strap overtop is beyond convenient. You won't find an easier stroller to open AND put a baby into, anywhere.

Yes, we had the front wheel issue. We had the replacement kit sent. I lost it, but used zap straps in black. Works perfectly! Yes the sun shade is not so great, but oh well - that is why you buy the sun canopy & rain kit. This is NOT supposed to be your "main stroller" people. It is a handy, leave in the car, or whenever you need convenient stroller. If you want perfection, don't look for it in an "umbrella" stroller.

Considering many other strollers on the market, there really is very VERY little to complain about. Yes the parking break gets scratched on the curb when you try to go down it. Oh well. It's meant to be used and scratched and loved.

Anyway if you're on the fence, don't be. Coming from a LOT of experience, this stroller is the absolute best invention by far for "umbrella" strollers. I am buying one right now for a friend. I will be buying these for any friend who has a baby on the way. I LOVE me some Nano buggy!

review_headline: If you haven't bought one of these yet, you should!!!
review_body: I ordered this necklace as a second option because the first one I ordered didn't match the description.  The picture that is listed for this necklace is EXACTLY how it is presented in person.  It came in a nice little box in a nice giftable mesh back along with a certificate of authenticity and a business card.  What stood out to me even more than the necklace itself, is the fact that the company provides a business card.  This is so important to me because when I like a product from a company, I want to buy more from them.  This allows me to easily shop their store and their products.  The necklace is about 12.5-13" long.  The stones are unpolished and vary is shape and size.  The beads are knotted individually and there is a twist clasp that can easily break away should it get snagged on something. In comparison to other necklaces that I have seen, these beads are a little smaller, but just as powerful.  It doesn't look so bulky as others do. When the necklace is warmed in the sun to "charge" it, you can smell a slight sap smell.  This is reassuring to me that this necklace is, in fact, real raw baltic amber.  For anyone who has never used an amber necklace for their teething infant/toddler, you should really try these.  I wasn't sure about them when I first had my daughter, but I will never go without one of these again.

review_headline: Overall good but has few minor annoyances!
review_body:
Car seats are awful to shop for, they just are. This is my third one to buy for my three year old over the years, and I keep finding it difficult to get all the features I want in one seat. I honestly just gave up and settled on this one. It's not super expensive, has all the requirements for safety and will make do. The features I want in a car seat, and I'm sure I'm not alone, are: 1) Be as lightweight as possible 2)Not be black or a dark color and 3) Not look like a cheap hotel lobby chair.

Obviously, my first concern is safety and the comfort of my kid. All car seats must meet the same regulations for safety so I don't even really bother researching all that at this point. I just want a seat that isn't a huge, heavy monster to drag through an airport, one that isn't solid black which becomes molten lava in a hot car and one that doesn't look embarrassing. This was the closest I could find. And it's still way off. I went to a few stores to compare different ones before deciding. Some of these convertible car seats weigh close to 30lbs! This one is 21 lbs, so it's not the worst offender. Now that my girl is almost 4, the little kid padding is not needed and it revealed a light grey fabric which won't scorch her like all the solid black seats. Only problem, and it's hard to see in the main photo, is this seat has black arm rests with a rubbery coating on them. They get so hot that she flinches when crawling up into the seat and I have to help guide her over it. I'm now here to buy dark window tint for that back window, hoping it will help. We live in LA so it's a year-round issue. WHY MUST THEY MAKE CAR SEATS BLACK?!?! I get that it hides stains, but I'd honestly rather have stains than a sweltering, burnt kid!

The last seats I had were Combi Coccoro and they came in solid lime green and solid light orange. They were the cutest car seats and only weighed 11lbs. She never complained that they were hot. The stains were not noticeable, were easily washable and all was fine. Those seats spoiled me, but alas, she outgrew them and their replacement is nowhere to be found. I was prepared to spend a ton of money, but nothing fit my needs. I settled on this and so far, here are my complaints: The pads on the straps are scratchy and cheap, they seem to irritate her neck. The pad around the crotch buckle keeps slipping off and is HUGE and clumsy to get in place to buckle up each time. I'm ready to just take it off or find a replacement. Again, the black arm rests get really, really hot. The designers got really close to a smart decision with all the pale, silvery fabric but then decided to throw in a section of black fabric on the lower back of the seat just so your little one can get nice and sweaty on their back.

Things I do like: The price is great, it is easy to adjust the head rest as your child grows, the seat feels well padded and my kid tells me it's comfortable, it has a slight reclining ability. Otherwise, it's like all other car seats: It has the latch system, can use the seat belt, has side impact cushions, 5 point harness, extensive height and weigh limits, etc. Also, it looked the least like a giant La-Z-Boy chair with a more sporty and sleek look. product_title: Piyo Piyo Baby Nail Scissors
review_headline: From my very first use, easier than clippers...
review_body:
I had read that scissors were safer than clippers for babies. I was skeptical because I had never heard of nail scissors.

After having a baby, I tried using clippers once. No blood, but I was terrified of accidentally clipping those tiny fingers (even on a sleeping baby!). It was hard for me to see what I was doing. The edges were rough, and it was hard to file the paper thin nails. I ordered these because they were inexpensive and had good reviews. I figured I might as well try them.

These are AMAZING. One of my favorite unexpected products. I give/recommend them to friends that are pregnant for the first time now.

Pros:
1. Easy to see exactly where you're cutting.
2. Curved a little, so easy to cut a good shape.
3. So easy to use. Way easier for me to use than clippers. I was surprised that they didn't require a learning curve. I didn't feel nervous about accidentally cutting my baby. I'm sure it could still happen, but I think it would be much, much harder.
4. They cut extremely smoothly. Even after a year of using them, I never need a file.
5. The toddler likes watching me use them. I just count the fingernails out loud as I'm cutting them, and the toddler patiently watches with almost no squirming.

Cons:
1. Just like clippers, it is possible to cut too close to the skin (i.e. to cut off too much nail). So that's not really a con, but something to watch out for. I think these are easier to use than clippers though, because you can see exactly where you're cutting.
2. Maybe it's just the circles I am in, but I don't know why baby nail scissors aren't more well known!
