product_title: OXO Tot Sprout Chair,Walnut
review_headline: Do not buy this. You can't get it clean. Ever. And then it stinks.
review_body:
There are so many things wrong with this seat. I'll do an overview of good and bad.

Good: The only good thing is that it looks nice.

Bad: 1. There is fabric under the seat cushions. FABRIC. Clearly a person with children did not design this chair. You have to take the cushions off every time and soap up and clean the fabric that has soaked up all the spilled milk and yogurt and captured all the crumbs from little hands that work their way easily in between the plastic and the back of the cushion...that is fabric. Did I mention that? And if you wanted to forgo the cushions to save yourself some cleaning time you can't really do that because of the next item in the list...it would make the chair incredibly uncomfortable unless the child was fully clothed in a fabric that didn't stick.
2. The awesome fabric on the back of the cushions sticks to the plastic chair with VELCRO??? Which after a few months stops working because it is so incredibly filled with bits of food that stink and pieces of sponge from your worthless attempts to clean out the stinky food.
3. Do not attempt to rinse off the tray. Even when the edges where the two pieces of plastic meet are filled with guacamole. Do not attempt to wash it. Why? Because It will fill with water and slowly drip out this water which somehow also becomes stinky (I'm assuming there is mold growing in there but I'm too afraid to unscrew all the tiny screws to find out) all over the floor and your child next time you go to use the tray.
4. The center strap and buckle are not removeable. So you cannot wash them. And the little buckle is forever filled with food. That you cannot clean out...and it stinks. Along with the strap...which has also soaked up said milk and yogurt and tuna juice or whatever else.
5. There are a remarkable number of nooks and crannies in this chair. It's as if they designed it to trap babies arms between the seat and arm rests, plus the places where the plastic meet the wood on the side are always filled with crumbs.

Ok I could go on but I've picked the top 5 annoying things about this chair. I am not a dirty person and I am not a clean freak either. Just a mom with a normal messy kid who is doing her best to keep things clean enough that they don't stink. This is quite impossible with this chair. Save your money and get the cheap $30 all plastic high chair from ikea...it doesn't look as good as this chair but it is so practical and easy to clean it's a way better choice.
I have twins on the way so I'm going to consign this chair and get three ikea chairs! Looking forward to this...well, sort of.

product_title: Baby Brezza Formula Pro One Step Food Maker
review_body:
I'll first say that, after 3 months with the Formula Pro and our new baby, we LOVE our machine. Solely because of the nature of formula, the machine is somewhat high maintenance. I'll leave you with a few bullet points that will ensure you love your machine as much as we do. The purpose that this machine fit's for us is the middle of the night feedings as well as feedings where our little one is screaming for his food and has ran out of patience. It's worth it's weight in gold at that point.

I've done some testing and found the water that the machine dispenses to be very accurate. The temp in the tank measures right around 100F via an infrared thermometer. By the time it mixes with the powder it's down around 94 degrees. We've run 4 types of formula in our machine until we found what best suits our baby: Enfamil Newborn, Enfamil Gentlease, Gerber Good Start Soothe, and finally Similac Total Comfort. Be aware that the Gentlease, and Total Comfort by Similac are pretty nasty when they sit wet after a while. the Newborn and Good Start Soothe were a little easier to clean. I'll include a couple points on that in the bullet points. Let's just get on with the bullet points shall we...

•READ THE INSTRUCTION MANUAL!!! I'll supplement a few things that I found to work better than what the instructions say though...
•Use distilled water or a variant only. We use nursery water. Using anything else will contaminate the water system of the machine. You want to keep this clean!
•CLEAN CLEAN CLEAN! Clean both pieces of the funnel daily, at least. I clean the round powder dispenser opening every 2-3 day's at the longest. This part get's nasty quick depending on the brand powder you use. I disassemble and clean the container as well as the measuring bits contained inside. I use warm water running from the faucet and dish soap. I do not put any parts in the washing machine mainly for the sake of making the cleaning process quicker and making theprocess more thorough by doing it by hand.
•Make sure the parts are completely dry before assembling and adding formula powder to the hopper. You know what happens when water and formula powder meet.
•The manual show's an illustration of wiping a towel in circles around the dispenser hole above the funnel. Forget that. Especially with the Gentlease and Similac Total Comfort, the stuff that powder leaves behind after several uses is nasty! I have a plastic scraping tool to remove the NASTY sludge from around the round opening. I remove the entire hopper from the machine, just lift straight up. When you leave the top on the measuring parts are held down so you can push up on the measuring disk through the round opening without misaligning things. I've never had an issue plopping it right back down. THIS PART IS IMPORTANT: If you do not keep the round powder dispenser opening clean your powder measuring will become more and more inaccurate. This means your formula will not have the right portions and your baby will get sick! The hole get's smaller and smaller. With a plastic scraper you can clean this round opening by scraping the sludge out following up with a DRY paper towel or something to remove the rest of the residue. DO NOT USE a wet cloth as it will introduce water to that area which will seep up into the powder and make a nasty mess around the opening. Using a small plastic scraper will keep this process dry and allow you to clean this round opening without disassembling the whole thing.
•When I clean the powder hopper I dump the powder inside back into a formula container so I don't waste any. After cleaning and drying the parts I pour this powder back in as well as topping it off with new powder.
•It doesn't really say anywhere in the manual, but leave the machine on all the time. I didn't know if the machine is designed to be turned on and off between uses but it's designed to be left on. The water will be thermostatically kept at the proper temp and ready for your convenience when you need it.
•The powder and water mix pretty well in the funnel as it is dumped into the bottle. I don't totally trust that it is full mixed so I either slosh the bottle back and forth as I'm walking to my feeding area of choice to ensure the formula is mixed completely. Don't just take the bottle from under your machine and assume it's TOTALLY mixed. Baby Brezza will say it is but I still don't trust it. It does a WAYYY better job than manually making bottles. That requires quite a bit of shaking to get it mixed together. The Formula Pro does a good job mixing but, I think, needs at least a few turning upside down, rightside up, upside down, rightside up, upside down, rightside up before introducing to your baby.
•It's $100 at Sam's club! (This may be your favorite bullet point...)
•When cleaning the water tank, obviously do not put it in the dishwasher. Like I said, I don't put ANY of the parts of this machine into a dishwasher. First turn the machine off. The water tank lifts straight up off the base.The heating element power, temperature sensor, and water quantity float electronics are connected via tabs and slots under the tank. Water should be kept away from this area. Make sure it stay's dry. Don't go nuts with a brush or something in the tank as the water quantity float is pretty important and isn't made for abuse. I've found that a little bit of mold likes to start to grow in the plastic seams area's right near the clear rubber water return nozzle. It make's a 90 degree turn at the top of the tank and spits water back into the tank while it's making your bottle. With the water being heated constantly, there is evaporation going on constantly which add's a lot of moisture to that area as well as under the tank cover. Keep this area around the water return spout clean of mold!
•If you want to make an odd number of ounces you'll have to round up an ounce, mix it, then pour an ounce out and put it in the fridge. Use the formula within 24 hours of mixing it... Just like when you make it manually. One scoop of powder makes 2 ounces of formula. I don't know why this is a complaint about this machine as it's an issue when making the bottle manually with the included scoops as well...
•Use the measuring settings included in your box. There are 2 styles of measuring wheels for the Formula Pro. If you go to the Baby Brezza website searching for updated settings you may find ones that are drastically different than what your included documentation say's. I called on this issue and was informed that the settings I found are for a different style of measuring wheel and was told to use the settings included with my unit. All powder's compact differently in the measuring wheel and Baby Brezza has done countless R&D on what setting dispenses the right amount of powder. Trust their R&D.
•Make sure there is sufficient water and powder in your machine before making the bottle. If the water quantity float
I may have a few more points but these are the important ones that I can think of. We would definitely buy it again! It must be kept CLEAN CLEAN CLEAN but it works exactly as it was designed and is a great thing to have around the house.

Just at the end of writing this review at 11:30PM, our son decided he want's the cluster feed tonight 2 hours after eating last. I put a little bit of cereal into a bottle, put it under the Formula Pro, pushed a button and a few seconds later a warm bottle was ready for my baby boy. When walking it to him I shook it up a little since it has cereal in it and I knew he was getting the correct proportions and that it was properly mixed up. Sure beats waiting to warm a bottle, dealing with that stupid scoop. and shaking like mad to get it mixed up!

product_title: Evenflo Titan Convertible Car Seat
review_headline: Beware: This model only goes up to 50 lbs forward-facing.
review_body:
I usually hate when people rate an item without having used it yet, but I wanted to post this as a warning so that others don't make the same mistake that I almost did. I found the Evenflo Titan on a certain big box store website (starts with a W) and when I added it to my Amazon wishlist, it automatically said it found a match. I ended up ordering the one from Amazon because I liked the color of it. For some reason, shortly after I ordered it, I went back and read through the description and discovered that this seat only goes up to 50 lbs forward-facing, whereas the seat at the other store goes up to 65 lbs, and if you look at the pictures, they do look slightly different. I immediately cancelled my Amazon order and will be buying the seat at the store because I specifically chose the seat for that weight range.

I'm sure it's probably not an easy thing for Amazon to do, but it should not tell you something is a match if it really isn't a match. Evenflo Titan Convertible Car Seat, Tatum is NOT a match to Evenflo Titan Convertible Car Seat, Atlantis (or Ciara)

Don't get me wrong, I love that Amazon tells you when they find a match and I think it's a great feature, but I feel like some people may assume it's the same seat when in fact it isn't, like I did. This could have ended up being a safety issue. I learned my lesson, though - always carefully read the descriptions even if it appears to be the same product.

product_title: Fisher-Price Precious Planet Healthy Care Booster (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

I have been looking at these boosters for a few months, but there are so many to choose from that I wanted to be able to sit down and read the reviews and find the best one. Fisher Price has multiple styles and then there were other boosters that looked good. I ended up going with this one, mostly because there was an “open box” deal that was hard to pass up. I am so mad at myself that I didn't get this sooner! Here’s why I love it (and a few things that could be a little better):

Likes:

-Convenient: I love how simple it is to use. It can be moved and adjusted very easily. My son now gets to join us at the table, rather than being off to the side. It’s made dinner time more enjoyable for all of us. We take it off and bring it to the grandparents and our friend’s house easily. The back folds down so it's smaller and can be carried by the straps. I am using the tray on it right now because he’s still too messy to use a plate at the table and would likely throw it on the ground. Eventually he’ll be ready for the booster without the tray, pulled right up to the table. I’m glad this is such a versatile system. I'm also excited to sell my high chair and have that extra space back.
-Strap adjustment: I was very worried it wouldn't fit in my chairs. I’m posting a picture to show our chairs, the seats are huge and the back of the chair is large. This fits easily with a few inches to spare. I take it to my neighbor’s house for game night so my son can sit at the table and watch us play domino's. It is easy to adjust it to fit their chairs as well.
-Cleaning: This is huge for me. I was so incredibly tired of washing the high chair pad and cleaning out the cracks. The tray comes of easily and just gets scrubbed off quickly and the seat gets a wipe down. There are little holes where the straps go into the seat that still is a tiny bit hard to clean out, but not a big deal. The seat belt straps come out easily and can be washed and the holes cleaned.
-Toys: This is toy tray is a nice bonus that most other boosters don’t have. My son plays with it for about 3-5 minutes at a time, just enough time to serve up food. The toys are difficult to clean though, so I try to keep food and dirty fingers away from it.

Dislikes:

-Toy tray removal: It’s supposed to come off easily, but the tab you stick your finger in is pretty shallow and there’s nothing in there to get any leverage off of to pry it off. I haven’t had to resort to using a knife or anything, but it could have definitely been designed with a tab to grip.
-Tray size: My other high chair has a very large tray that fans out, this one is very small in comparison. My son is in the stage where he likes to drop food off the side when he’s full, this booster makes that much easier for him. On the flip side, since it is smaller and he’s now my equal height, it’s so much easier to feed him. I don’t have to lean over at all.

The other benefit I've noticed is I’m sitting down for meals more with my son. I work 2 days a week, so him and I are home alone a lot together. With my other high chair on wheels I would pull it into the kitchen and feed him while I did other tasks. Now since it’s easier to sit at the table I find myself making us lunch and then sitting down to eat with him. I enjoy this time we spend together and it forces to me eat regular meals also. I definitely recommend this booster, it is easy to clean, pulls right up to the table and is very portable! review_headline: A Really Great Set Of Baby Spoons!!!
review_body:
*** NOTE: I received a free product sample in exchange for an honest review. ***

I would have really loved to have these spoons when my kids were learning to feed themselves. They were always chewing on "everything" and many times they locked down on the hard spoons we used and hurt themselves since they don't have much jaw control.

UB Baby's set of four baby spoons are perfect for feeding your little ones - or to let them learn to feed themselves! The spoons are made of food-grade silicon with a slightly harder plasitic interior shell to provide rigidity. The spoons are pretty large in diameter so its easy for your baby or toddler to hold tightly onto the spoon. They also have ridges on the spoon to keep it from slipping our of their hands when they invariably coat the spoon with food and saliva. The spoon's cup is deep enough to hold a decent amount of food (its about 1 inch long and 1/2 inch wide) without being too big that baby can't get the spoon in his/her mouth or too much food at once to choke him/her.

The 10 month old baby we "rented" to try out the product with had no problem grasping the spoon and manipulating it into her mouth. She didn't get much food in there, but she's just learning. Since the spoon is made of soft silicon, she loved just having it in her mouth to chew on when it wasn't meal time. Considering she was teething, she was constantly shoving stuff into her mouth and these spoons are certainly better than a dog toy or her fist or whatever else she decides looks "yummy".

Overall, I don't think I can more highly recommend UB Baby's Baby Spoon Set. They are perfect for parents and toddler alike.

product_title: BubbleBum Travel Car Booster Seat, Black
review_headline: Dangerous; kids can't rapidly escape the car as the Bubble Bum lassos them into the seat belt. Should come with Emergency Cutter
review_body: I believe this seat is Dangerous as it will prevent your child from being able to rapidly exit the car in case of an emergency. The Bumble Bum actually TIES your child to the seat belt with two red clips (one on each side of the seat). IF YOU USE THIS SEAT YOU MUST HAVE AN EMERGENCY SEAT BELT CUTTER ON HAND as there is no way to rapidly release the child from the seat or seat belt. Conversely your child will also have a difficult time threading both of the red clips on to the seat belt after buckling. If your car goes into the water or starts to catch fire, I believe it is extremely unlikely your kid will be able to free themselves from the seat; even if he/she unbuckles the seat belt,  the two red clips will still keep the child physically locked between the seat belt and the Bubble Bum seat.  The seat however does have at least one useful feature in that one can change the amount of air in the seat and thereby raise or lower the child in the seat to more safely match head rest height; this feature can be useful when using third row seat which often are notably smaller than the first and second row seats.

product_title: Generation Ⅰ Peek-a-view 720p (1280*720) HD “Wifi” Wireless Baby Monitor Camera for Iphone, Ipad, Android Phone or Pc Remote View
review_body:
This camera is way cheaper than similar ones, but there's a reason for that. It looks like someone made this company in their basement. The box, instructions, and app are all in broken English. It's readable but annoying.

Pros:
-very clear picture, even in night vision. People who have problems with that likely have a slow internet connection.
-very easy to set up with one major exception listed below.
-remote access from anywhere on your phone
-alarm setting allows you to use this like a security camera even taking pictures when movement is detected.
-mounting hardware included
-app is fairly easy to use

Cons
-haven't gotten the wifi to work. Still working on it using a computer program. I think it has the wifi disabled and you have to download this program that uses the IP address to switch it back on. I don't really understand it but my husband thinks he can fix it. However he's a software engineer so if you aren't tech savvy, the wifi will never work for you.
-the sensor that made it change from night to day just stopped working before I was finished setting it up. You can still manually change the setting but it won't automatically switch
-the directions are pretty useless except to give you the name of the app.
-I don't know what camera some other people are talking about, but you cannot remotely move the camera. You can zoom, but the quality is distorted
-it does not automatically adjust the focus to focus on wherever there is movement. You can adjust the focus manually on the front of the camera.
-requires plug in making it not so wireless

So basically you're paying for the app to be free and a high quality of picture. We were able to make it work for us, but if my husband can't get the wifi to work, we'll return ours. This is a "get what you pay for"situation. If you want something perfect, spend more money.

product_title: Safety 1st Incognito Kid Positioning Seat
review_body:
I am a shorter adult, and have always struggled to get seat belts to fit correctly. At 5'2 and just over 120 lbs, I'm just over the manufacturer's intended maximum user size, but the seat works quite well for me. It's pretty comfortable, does a great job of positioning the lap belt across my hips instead of my stomach, & does a decent job of keeping the shoulder belt off my neck.

My only real complaint is that the front portion of the seat is wide enough that it doesn't quite fit properly between the sloped sides of my car's seat. This can cause slippage from time to time...but not enough to be a deal breaker, merely an annoyance. And it wouldn't necessarily be an issue in other vehicles (for reference, I drive an '07 Hyundai Accent, which I think has fairly narrow seats). Also, the narrower back portion seemed uncomfortable at first. I have wide hips/big butt, so my hips are slightly wider than the seat, and the feel of my hips hanging over the edge took a couple weeks to get used to.

Overall, after 5 months of use I am very happy with my decision to get this booster. Driving is so much more comfortable, I can ride safely in almost any car, & I no longer have to deal with funny rashes from the seat belt rubbing against my skin.

product_title: Child to Cherish Handprints Tower Of Time Kit
review_headline: I like it for what it is
review_body:
I am stuck on giving this item either a 3 or 4 star review. I like it for what it is, it looks nice, and the plaster for the prints works good and stays nice, but the metal dents more easily than I expected and gets some rust on it. I purchased the multicolored stack and the all pink one. We have had these stacks now for around 4 years. We have two more prints to make, the 4 year old and the 5 year old.

Cons: Some of the discs have got rust spots around the edge of the lids after a couple of years. That alone is enough to put a big damper on the item because it is supposed to last for many years. Another smaller, yet disappointing issue is how some of the containers now have dents on them. It didn't take much for the dents to happen. Even though dents are not going to destroy the item and didn't effect the prints, it messes up the look of the item which was part of the reason we purchased the stacks for our daughters nursery.
the smallest problem is the paint is scratched a bit on some of the lids around where the next container rests on it. This is from the bottom of the metal container coming into contact with the lid it rests on.

Pros: The hand prints are protected and are still in good tact. The plaster looks good and was simple enough to make nice little hand prints following the instructions. The paint on the containers look very nice for the most part. I have not had any other issue with the paint coming off or chipping in the dented areas. Each container from age 1 to age 5 has a different animation containing the same bear. For example, the age 1 lid has a cute bear on it with one turtle nose to nose. The second container age 2 has the bear with two birds, and the third one has the bear with three cute snails. They are still cute. Also, even with the imperfections the stacks are a lovely sight from a small to large distance.

I would most likely give this 4 stars if it wasn't for the rust because I have not gotten it wet at all so I am not sure how I could have caused the rust to happen and I am not sure how to avoid further damage relating to the rust. Also, it is something that is going to eat away at the product more and more itself over the years. So it is a major disappointment.
The paint issue could have been avoided a little more if I wouldn't have moved them at all and wouldn't have let others or myself touch them to look at them to where they will be unstacked and then stacked again. This was not done often and the whole point is to have them stacked and to look at them from time to time.

The denting is the most understandable because tin dents so I was expecting that. It could have been avoided the most if none of them was ever accidentally dropped. Even though accidents are bound to happen and it was only twice this happened out of 4 years, the denting was my fault. The top two on the stack are the easiest to come off the stack so the top two are the ones with the most damage.

I do wish that Child to Cherish had replacement lids since the most damage is on the lids. If it wasn't for the rust then I would maybe buy another whole set of stacks to take the lids from to replace the ones that are damaged. That would be inconvenient and a waist since I would just be buying the sets for the lids, and would have no use for the new containers since my daughter is now 4 years old.

product_title: Summer Infant Extra Camera for Dual View Digital Color Video Baby Monitor (28980, 28980A)
review_headline: NO SOUND INDICATOR FOR LOW BATTERY/NO SIGNAL = DANGEROUS PRODUCT!
review_body:
I absolutely love this monitor except for that it has no audible sound indicator for low battery or signal. That lack of function could cause my child to die. What if I forget to plug it in at night because of that glass of wine or just because I forget sometimes? It will die without me knowing while I peacefully sleep. What if, as it gets older, the signal reach fades (as all seem to from my exp and reading reviews) and the signal starts getting lost at night while I sleep. I would never know without a sound, and baby could be screaming or worst strangling or choking on spit up or even die! Why would a BABY MONITOR company make something that doesn't wake you up to let you know it isn't working or is about to die? And why would they LIST THE FUNCTION in the product description? Borderline false advertising eh? I am sorry but displaying words on the screen does not mean it has an indicator!

This is a sad day for me to have to return this monitor and go back to Motorola. I even called Summer's customer service to make sure I wasn't wrong, but sadly confirmed there is no actual indicator sound. The customer service rep suggested I keep the monitor plugged in at night and had no suggestion for the lack of signal indicator. We originally had the Motorola MBP36 and I was okay with it. However, the signal strength started fading and the battery life, well it was always plugged in or dead, and then the sound went out after 2 years of owning. I opted to replace with Summer Infant Dual View for many reasons and was EXTREMELY HAPPY with it for the week we had it until I realized there was no low battery and no signal indicator, lies.

WHAT I LOVE:
-It is so cute! I love the shape and the chrome border and the sound light bar. It is pleasing to the eyes. I thought it looked cheesy in pics but it truly is beautiful in hand. As a women I love pretty things and this is pretty!
-It feels good, the plastic outer is smooth and feel like a quality material.
-The kick stand is totally adjustable to any angle and has a spring so it can be used as a belt clip too. I love this because it prevents the monitor from falling out of a sweater pocket (which is probably why the sound on my motorola went out). This is a very big one for me and the biggest reason why I am sad that I cannot use this product.
-The split screen is simple to use.
-Picture quality is somewhere between acceptable and clear, not perfect but very close and I was satisfied/happy. What do you expect for such a well priced split screen capable monitor?
-Great battery life! I think they claim 10 hours compared to Motorola's meesily 3.5 hours.
-Priced well compared to equivalent competitor products.

I DONT LIKE:
-No SOUND indicator for low battery and no signal. This effectively is just a dangerous product, Summer.
-Only sound on one screen when in split screen mode, you have to physically switch the selected screen to get audio from the other cameras. They recommend using the scan function at night (where the camera switches on screen to any other cameras every 8 seconds), however the whole reason I wanted a split screen was for night so I can peek for a split second at the monitor through the night and fall right back asleep. On the scan function I would have to stay awake for 8 second while waiting for the other screen to come up. Call me picky but hey, I like my sleep, who doesn't? The scan function should work on split screen mode too.
-The camera does not play music like the Motorola, doesn't affect me unless it was white noise. I never used the function but wish one of these companies would put white noise.
-The monitor does not display the temperature, not a big deal but Motorola does, however it was always wrong and showing in the 40s and 50s.

Lots of don't likes but I am still very sad to have to return the product. The only don't like that really mattered to me was the indicator.I really wish I could keep this monitor. Sad day. Summer please fix and add a sound indicator and I will GLADLY become a loyal customer again, as I am sure lots of others will too! But hurry please my kids are only small for so long ;)

product_title: Contours Bliss 4-in-1 Stroller System
review_body:
I love this stroller. My baby was born in December so we haven't been able to try it out as much. However, we have used the pram position EVERY DAY for her to nap downstairs and she sleeps soundly. She is now two months and is using the sitting up position very comfortably.

It is great that the car seat attachment is included! Some people are concerned about the fact that the car seat has to be strapped in. I was worried as well, but I have to say that it is super secure and I am not concerned when I take her out. When I began the search for a stroller I was very indecisive when it came to picking between this one or a travel system, more specifically the Britax Agile. I have to say I am very happy with my pick and with the fact that I don't have to carry the big stroller with me when I just want to use the car seat in it.

I also remember reading in a review that the fabric design in the inside of the canopy would catch the baby's attention. It really does (I have the yellow one). Especially when they are so young and tend to focus on one thing for hours.

The stroller is very light to pick up and very easy to fold. I wish it was a bit easier to unfold, but it's really not a big deal. I also wish I didn't have to take the seat off for folding.

Bottom line, it is not a luxury stroller like Uppababy or Stokke, but it does the job pretty nicely. You can't beat the fact that the seat converts into a pram as easily as it does. Two clicks and you have a whole different stroller.

product_title: Infant Optics DXR-8 Video Baby Monitor with Interchangeable Optical Lens
review_body: This camera does the job but there are a few downfalls. My biggest issue is that the charging cord is so loose that it constantly slips out and then the unit dies in the middle if the night. Also when it's dying it makes an extremely loud beeping noise. Every so often it will loose range and beep very loudly repeatedly. When I say loudly I mean "wake up the whole house loud". When you have a sleeping infant you'd do pretty much anything to keep them asleep and a baby product like this should have volume control for noises like that. Overall it does the job for now but I'm keeping an eye on the plug issue which it seems like could get worse after reading some of the other reviews.  UPDATE- Monitor is now 10 months old and I HATE it!!!! It cannot be used at all without being plugged in which pretty much defeats the purpose of having a rechargeable wireless unit. The connection point is faulty as others have mentioned. It's so loose it can no longer hold a charge at all. If it comes unplugged (which is does often because it's too loose) it makes it's horrid beeping noise that you can't turn off. It also beeps randomly in the middle if the night for lost signal. Super disappointed as I was hoping to use this for baby number 2. Going to contact Infant Optix because this is obviously a faulty product. I do not recommend it at all unless they fix the connection issue.  UPDATE (Son is now 1 year old)- I seriously hate this thing more than I can put into words. We have changed the power cord thinking that would solve the charging issue (per customer service). And it did...for 3 days. It now doesn't hold a charge and we have to keep adjusting it to make sure the cord stays in because it has to be exactly in the right spot or it beeps super loudly. The latest fun is that it sometimes just randomly turns off (even when plugged in and charging properly. Also, it has started catching a ton of white noise so even on the quietest setting it sounds like you are in a washingmachine. It is a major issue to not have a reliable monitor for your child. Please for the love of all that is holy DO NOT BUY THIS MONITOR!!!!

product_title: Avent 2-Pack Natural Bottles
review_body:
I recently purchased Avent Comfort Breast Pump and it included two natural bottles.
This is a good bottle over all, like it's older classic brother. There are major differences between the two

Pros
1. Less parts than classic brother, there is no adapter ring and the neck collar is much longer
2. Wider base which can easily have a baby go from breast to bottle with no problem
3. Sleek design which is easier to hold, similar to Tommy Tippiee brand bottles in the feel of the bottle when serving from
4. Vented nipple so less air is in baby's stomach
5. Sealing disc is interchangeable between natural and classic bottle sets/ Can be used to store breast-milk
6. Clearly marked measurements both ML and OZ ( oz side has half ounce markings )
7. Can be purchased in glass
8. Can be pumped into via adapters ( for ameda & medla brand pumps ) or if your using an advent pump
9. Easy to clean

Cons
1. More expensive than classic, bottle itself and nipple replacements
2. No 11oz bottle size, just 4oz and 9oz
3. Nipples, collars and tops can not be use interchangeably with it's older classic brother
4. Unlike it's older classic brother, this bottle can not be used interchangeably with trainer cup handles and spouts. There is a natural style trainer cup that can be used with natural nipples and spouts but that is a separate purchase, where as with classic you only need to buy the trainer cup handles/spouts and not a whole new bottle.

Overall the bottle is a good bottle. I don't have leakage issues, holds up well to repeated use, can be used with multiple children. Bottle can be pumped into. I haven't had this bottle for some time so I'm not sure how durable it is but based on my experience using the classic bottle I can safely assume that the bottle if used properly can last for years and be used with multiple children. While in use the nipple flexes around some, in a similar fashion to skin. Nipple is vented and bell shaped.to skin. Nipple is vented and bell shaped.

product_title: LectraLock - Baby Safety Electrical Outlet Cover - Duplex Style (single screw type) - Deep Cover
review_headline: Exactly what I needed to keep my toddler safe!
review_body:
The product arrived sooner than expected, always a plus, and it was exactly as it looks in the picture. It accommodates the large, thick plug & cord on my surge protector (blue lounge cablebox mini with small surge protector- which I bought as an alternative to the baby safe power strip cover due to poor reviews- which I am also satisfied with, although the cablebox is much larger than I'd expect from one described as "mini" . . Back to the LectraLock cover . . ) It was very easy to install: Just remove the original plate from your outlet and screw this one it. Done. With my adult hands I can easily remove the cover, whereas my toddlers little baby hands would have no such luck. So far, with occasional tugging of the cord, the plug has yet to come loose from the outlet :) I have no large chargers to plug in . . but the cover sticks out 2 3/4" & is 2 1/4" wide & 4" long (from top to bottom) the cord holes are about 1/2" x 1/2" So they fit rather large cords but are small enough to keep the kids out. I hope that helps!

*also, if you look at the picture you can see that the box is slightly smaller around the edges. The tapering starts at roughly 2 1/4" when measuring it's depth -so the tapered part is about 1/2" thick leaving the end of the box at about 1 3/4" x 3 1/2" Still loads of room for most appliances :)

product_title: Philips Avent Digital Video Baby Monitor with Night Vision
review_body:
Summary:
Cons:
-Easily loses signal (see pic for the screen I would see all the time)
-Expensive for low quality
-Doesn't keep a charge that long (and seems to continue to lose the charge even when turned off)

Pros:
-Picture is good enough to tell if his eyes are open
-Installs easily
-Clip/stand are helpful

I received this monitor as a gift and was really excited to have it. We started using the monitor immediately after bringing our son home from the hospital (Oct 2014). Initially we had him sleeping in his crib in his room just down the hall and would also put him there for naps. The camera was installed on the wall overlooking the crib (following the instructions).

We live in a 3 story home with the bedrooms on the top floor. However, our house is not particularly large and it is well within the size limits that the monitor states it can work within. The day after bringing our son home, we had the monitor on the main floor (2nd flr) with our son in his room (3rd flr) and the signal kept going in and out - mostly out. This was a huge problem given this was the only monitor we had in order to hear him cry/awake. I immediately ordered from Amazon the Vtech sound only monitor which has yet to fail (next day delivery so we didn't have to deal with this failing Philips monitor). Even as I type this review in my bedroom, down the hall from his room, the monitor has lost its signal and I've had to simply turn it off to stop it from beeping.

My recommendation is to get a good sound only monitor that will always work and find a different video monitor as a nice to have. We always use the VTech one and will sometimes use this Philips one in addition to the VTech if we feel like seeing the video (but we never use it by itself).

product_title: Munchkin Auto Close Designer Baby Gate, Dark Wood/Silver
review_body:
Since my oldest was born, I have had baby gates. First, for the babies. Then, for the dogs. I have had all types of baby gates. My favorites sport doors that swing open and shut.

The Munchkin wooden baby gate qualifies as one of the best. It's similar to another brand I have made of metal. Munchkin is shorter and made of wooden slats for the door (metal for the side rails). It offers a more secure latching mechanism, but dog owners beware. A larger dog will be able to jump it.

This gate won't budge, if you drill screws into the door jamb. I don't need to do anything permanent like that. I just let it press directly against the wood, which is secure enough to keep my cocker spaniel away from the cat's food bowl.

When it comes to style and security, Munchkin wins hands down. Little children won't have the strength and dexterity to open it (lift, pull or push open while simultaneously depressing the latch button). Adults can do it with ease. I love how it will stay open if I push it all the way out, but it swings shut if I give it a nudge.

I am forever a fan of baby gates with doors. Never will I force myself to step over a gate again. Doors with fashion sense, that's even better.

review_headline: Overall GREAT.  Few nit picky complaints (detailed in full review)
review_body: Overall these are great!  I had to reposition them several times while applying on the wall (spacing issues) and they appear to be sticking great still. product_title: Ameda Purely Yours Ultra Breast Pump
review_headline: Work reasonably well at first, but broke down after moderate use
review_body:
In 2011, I purchased a Purely Yours Ultra double electric pump. I was happy with its performance under moderate use (probably a few times a week for 6 or 7 months, basically enough to supply spare milk for short times away from the baby). After I was finished nursing I cleaned all the parts and stored everything in its carrying bag in a dry place.

I have since brought out the pump for my second child. I replaced the valves, diaphragms, and tubing, and it worked okay for several months, but not as well as I had remembered. The speed adjustment seemed somewhat limited. And then recently, it started to loose suction intermittently. I tried replacing the valves again, but it did not help. After troubleshooting with a very nice customer service representative, we determined it is likely the pump itself that is failing. It is out of warranty, so there is simply nothing to be done.

With not much to lose, and curious to understand what went wrong, I opened up the pump case and found that the clear housing around the pump piston had become cracked around its base; the cracking is extensive enough that the clips are actually falling off. When the piston engages, the housing lifts slightly, and this is enough to loose suction.

This pump was never dropped, it was always stored carefully, and I always treated it with the best care.

I am extremely disappointed. This is an expensive pump marketed to women who plan to pump a significant amount. It is a shame that the design is so poor that the plastic fractured and failed under moderate use. This pump was used for less than a year and not even used extensively. And now I am faced with having to purchase another pump system because I am still in need of one.

I cannot convey how let down I am by the quality of this product.

product_title: Itzbeen Pocket Nanny Baby Care Timer
review_body:
This is a GREAT item to put on a baby registry, get a new parent, or to treat yourself (if no one ends up getting it for you).

I really do love this. My daughter is only a week old and it's been a lifesaver for having both mom AND dad play an active role in nighttime caretaking. I have the equipment to feed her (ehhem), so I'm clicking that button and instantly communicating--when daddy comes in to change her and lay her down or take the next shift--how long it's been since the feeding started. Likewise, I know how long since she's fallen asleep and when her last dirty and wet diaper was (we use the diaper button for "dirty" diapers, and the extra button for wet only). When he wakes me up to feed her again it only takes a moment of orientation to figure out exactly who did what and when.

It's like writing electronic post-it notes to each other. Not that we don't talk, but when you're stumbling through that first week on no sleep it's REALLY surprisingly hard to remember that your last feeding started at, say, 4 a.m. instead of 3:30 or 4:30 or whatever. It's much easier than what we had to do at the hospital (charting everything...sometimes forgetting when we started because by the time feeding had begun, I no longer had a free two hands to get the clipboard and he was sleeping and then I couldn't remember when I started by the time I was done).

As others have mentioned, I think a diaper number count might be useful for the first week or so, but I don't really miss it. By timing the frequency you figure out pretty quickly when you're okay and when you need to be concerned (even without an exact count). Oh, and when you need to brace yourselves (no dirty diaper in 12 hours? Have an extra wipe or two ready!).

product_title: Medela Pump In Style Advanced Breast Pump
review_body:
I'll let my wife write this review.

I'm very satisfied with this pump. It has been basically my best friend for over a year all together so far. We are on our 3rd child with the same pump. I pump basically every 3.5 hours for about 15 minutes every time. I went for 7 months with our 2nd child and so far I'm up to 8 months with our 3rd child and so far the pump is still doing good.
It came in a nice little bag so it's easy to carry and pump on the go. It's also a nice size. I was expecting something bigger and bulky but to my surprise the whole bag and everything is about the same size as the average diaper bag, might be even a little smaller.
It does come with a battery pack so you can pump on the go which is nice and convenient. But it does take 8 double A batteries and they don't seem to last very long so I do wish it came with a charger for the car instead of a battery pack. But either way it's still nice and convenient.
My regular wall charger lasted about a year before it broke and the metal prongs that go into the outlet started sliding inside the charger. I read online if I contacted Medela they would send out a new one free if charge but I couldn't ever get through to the Medela customer service so I just ended up ordering a replacement charger off here which worked better than the original
The instruction manual that came with the pump was easy to read and understand and I referred to it often when it came to cleaning it.
It's also easy to clean by popping off the face plate and giving it a good wipe.
Has a good range of power for suction. The 2 phase feature is amazing to get the milk to let down.
I was a little intimidated by the price but after using it for long and it still operating like new I know the price was well worth it.
I have recommended this same pump to several people and would definitely purchase another one if needed.

product_title: Graco Head Wise 70 Car Seat with Safety Surround Protection
review_headline: Happy with the features and ease of installation
review_body:
It's been two days since my son went for his first ride in this car seat, and since I know how hard it is figure out if a car seat will work for you in the real world, I thought I'd help others out by writing a review.

First of all is the installation itself. This car seat is installed rear-facing in an Accord, so keep that in mind when you read my comments below. I'm quite pleased with the ease of installation because I, all of 5'4 tall, was able to install it securely by myself with the Latch belt. I'm also happy because it takes up about an inch less space front-to-back than his infant seat. If you're having trouble installing it, I recommend peeling away the fabric on the cupholder side of the car seat and moving the Latch belt adjuster through the hole that it passes through. This allows you to pull up toward you to tighten, instead of out and away from you. You'll be able to pull it much tighter that way.

Other positives about this seat include the extra padding on the head rest, which makes a nice comfy pillow for the kid. I haven't been in a crash with it and hope not to, so I can't comment on its purported side-impact features. We also like the suede-like texture of the fabric. It's much nicer than the scratchy nylon that you see on a lot of other car seats. It sits tall so that kids can see what's going on out the back windows. For us, that prevents a lot of fussing.

Now for some negatives. If you don't use the infant body pillow, the seat pad has very minimal cushioning. I also find the harness difficult to tighten completely because the harness adjustment is so close to the seat back, leaving very little room to pull it. I've found that it's easier if you place the chest clip very low, close to the buckle, tighten it, then move the chest clip up to its proper position. The chest clip can also be hard to unbuckle since it requires a strong pinch grip. It's easier to open if you pinch the top prong first, then the bottom.

I see a lot of questions asking about the date of manufacture. Ours is June 2013. I don't have a problem with that, but if you want to use it with more than one child, it could be an issue. The seat we received had the new updated buckle.

I hope that this review helps people out. For us, the positives, including the fact that this looks like it will fit our kid until he's ready for a booster, greatly outweigh the negatives and we're happy with this purchase.

review_headline: Our second choice was this one - and we are extremely pleased with the reclining levels
review_body:
As I am sure every parent does, I researched a lot about car seats. And, at first, bought a reputed brand from a very reputed wholesale dealer. The problem ? The seat had just two recline levels, and in my Toyota Avalon backseat, that seat did not give enough back recline. When set up with rear facing option, the seat was too upright. Not only was the baby uncomfortable, but when she slept, her head would bob down towards her chest - which is extremely dangerous !!!!!

Our second choice was this one - and we are extremely pleased with the reclining levels. The baby and the parents feel much more comfortable with this seat! :)

Beyond re-enforcing what every other review seems to say:
* It is extremely easy to fix.
* The level indicator is a delightful feature
* The fabric looks and feels far more better than many other seats that we saw.

Beyond all these - the baby's posture seems to be the correct one. And that's what matters, I guess !

I guess it is a little bulky. In an Avalon, it didn't seem to matter, but i am sure in smaller cars, that could be an issue to think about. Space, but, is a small compromise to overall safety and comfort. And also, we don't plan to move these between cars, or even to carry this with us when we travel.

Few thoughts:
I know there are many things to think about - but IMHO, please do not make any compromise when it comes to the safety and comfort of your little one. I am NOT recommending this brand over any other - that's your choice. Just voicing out my opinion that when you select a car seat, please do not put space, bulk, weight or any such parameter over your overall safety of your child. Ensure that her/ his posture is the correct one, and everything about the seat is of highest quality. that's all.

review_headline: Overall very good stroller, with some flaws (bumpy ride in very urban setting)
review_body:
My wife and I have owned this stroller for 6 months and we are overall satisfied with it, though it does have some drawbacks, especially if you are in an urban setting with uneven/bumpy streets/sidewalks.

Pros:
- Great basket. I can't say how much it holds and how useful it is for us in our urban setting.
- Light for its class and compact for getting around in small spaces.
- Very functional: Folds pretty easily, different seat settings / angles are great.
- Baby likes it and has always seemed comfortable in it through his first 6 months (we used it with the UB bassinet, the UB infant insert, and now with the standard seat).

Cons:
- Bumpy ride on bumpy/uneven sidewalks/streets. We live in New York City and our area has older streets and it just does not have big enough wheels or a suspension (I believe the 2015 version of the Cruz has bigger rear wheels, and the Vista has even bigger ones).
- Releasing the foot brake can be a little awkward. Applying the brake works well, but releasing the brake sometimes ends in it getting stuck and you have to turn it/go back to fully release it.
- Some flex in the build. If you shake it from side to side, you will notice some flex. It's not going to break or fall apart, but it just doesn't feel like a totally high end "solid" build.

product_title: Regalo Extra Tall 2 in 1 Walk Through Safety Gate
review_body:
I have used this baby gate at the bottom of the stairs. As you see in the photos, the left side is bolted into the drywall and the right side is attached to the banister. I am happy with how it functions, but it did require some alterations to make it work well.

When you take it out of the box it says that you need to bolt it into a stud or else use drywall anchors. It does not come with any drywall anchors so I needed to get some of those. It also has instructions for mounting to a wall that has a baseboard, but my baseboard is extra deep at the bottom and it would not work with my baseboard if I wanted the verticle support to rest on the floor. I accounted for this by setting the vertical Rod on top of the bottom portion of the baseboard as you can see in the photo. The plastic pieces that act as support spacers in between the vertical rod and the drywall are only so big so I could not set it on the floor or else the vertical rod would be too far away from the wall. Because the vertical Rod was slightly elevated on the left side I also need to elevate on the right side next to the banister. I have used some of the scrap pieces to stack on the floor on the right under the vertical rod that is attached to the banister.

The width of the gate adjusts freely, too freely actually. It really helps to use slip ties to lock the gate to the proper width.

Lastly, the hinge was squeaky and stiff, and some wd40 helped a lot.

UPDATE: After a little over a year of heavy use, the gate ripped out of the wall and left big holes in the sheet rock. It's gave me a chance to learn to patch a wall.

product_title: KidCo G22 White Safeway Angle Mount
review_headline: Love Hate Relationship with an Inanimate Object
review_body:
Okay, do after reading the other reviews, I counted on a long installation time. Installation was moderately difficult, and I'm a guy who is used to installing stuff in the house. I actually had to walk away from this thing for a day.

First Impressions:
- I immediately saw the rust at the ends when I opened the box...the rust was visible thru the plastic wrap.
- This gate is WAY more complicated than it needs to be. I'm an engineer and holy crap was this thing impossibly difficult to install (assembly was cake)
- There are no measurements given for installing the ends (hinge and lock side), only a long strip of paper to help align screws and brackets from a fixed position (i.e. top of baseboard, etc.).....this is would have been easy had I needed that approach, however I installed it on the first step using a stairway gate installation kit from the same manufacturer (see respective review). So when you are an an angle with no fixed points, how is one supposed to align the end brackets w/o any measurements? ---> I had to ghetto rig this thing first to get it aligned and then installed.
- The plastic brackets clamping the two metal pieces of the gate together are okay. They will NOT stand a toddler jumping/reefing on the gate. I reinforced the end rackets and the attachment pieces with wide/thick zip ties. They are clear/off white so they don't look so bad.
- The white powder coating was peeling in some areas. Very annoying and difficult to hide. Likely some contaminants not removed before processing.

Installation Tips:
1.) My recommendation is to NOT install this gate at the top of a stair. This is positively dangerous with this gate. If you have a toddler that can climb onto the gate, there is a slight probability that the gate could collapse at the aforementioned joining brackets leading to failure and a fall down the stairs. Also, the end brackets on the gate and what the gate attaches to are plastic which could break fail leading to the same result.

2.) This is a great gate for bottom of the stair installation at an angle, specifically why we bought it. You will need a level, some ingenuity and a LOT of patience with this gate.

3.) If using the stairway installation kit, I recommend attaching both hinges onto the plastic brackets for more stability (see pics). The small flimsy wood screws will fail eventually.

4.) Zip ties are your friend for securing up various aspects of this gate (see pics)

product_title: Ikea's ANTILOP Highchair with safety belt, white, silver color and ANTILOP Highchair  white
review_headline: I have been using this highchair for 1.5 years...
review_body:
We have twins and have been using this IKEA highchair for 1.5 years now, and here is what I have learned.

If you buy it at IKEA you have to buy the tray and the padding separately, but all said and done I think it was $30 per set-up (highchair, tray and padding). I did not buy this highchair from this particular seller, so I am going to review the highchair and not the seller or the seller's price.

I really like the Antilop. It is neutral colored, it doesn't take up a lot of space (or visual space if you know what I mean) - basically it blends, which is good in our smaller kitchen.

It is also really easy to clean. Sometimes I just lift the chair up and pour all the cherrios right into the sink. Or there was one particularly messy time I took the chair right outside and hosed it off! Cleaning this chair is easy!

Also, because it is light, I will carry it outside for bbqs - or carry it wherever we are eating - it is highly transportable. In fact we have been using the chair without the tray and pushing it right up to our dining room table - it is the perfect height for the kids to sit with us for family dinners.

One thing to note, it is NOT easy to take off the tray, you basically have to use some strength and yank the thing off from the front corner. (Put your hands on opposing corners, brace the back corner and yank up the front corner.) You feel like you a breaking it, but you aren't. Because of this, I leave the tray on always and only take it off for serious cleanings and/or when we bring the chair right up to the dining table for a family dinner. I never take the tray off when the kids are sitting in the high chair. Therefore you are not relying on the tray to keep your kids from standing up - instead you are relying on the straps. So make sure the chair you choose has straps and as the kids get older, that you use them (because without the straps my kids will stand up in this chair - luckily they have never fallen).

My kids are now 2 and are 95% for height and 75% for weight and they are still very comfortable in this chair (we no longer use the padding) with plenty of room for more growing.

I have been very happy with this chair and would recommend it!5% for height and 75% for weight and they are still very comfortable in this chair (we no longer use the padding) with plenty of room for more growing. I have been very happy with this chair and would recommend it!

review_headline: Only practical for small busted ladies
review_body: This is a great idea in theory, but in practice is beyond awkward if you have anything larger than a B cup.  The Freemie cups themselves are a full B-cup.... The only way I could use these was to wear my Medela sleep bra underneath my Hot Milk bra, as no bra that can fit an additional two cup sizes is going to be supportive enough for business wear once you're not pumping... Now having these in, my bust came out a literal 8 inches from my chest, and being that I'm quite small, totally eliminated any chance of me being able to hold my baby while they were in.  They also pretty much eliminate any possibility of being able to do compressions or massage while pumping, so you just have to pump for an abnormally long time to make sure you're properly emptied.  You're also not going to know how much milk you've collected until you pour it into another container.  The connector for the Medela pumps is precarious at best.... it's just a plastic spike that you ram into the two tubes and is very easy to accidentally pull out.  I also found the cups to be extremely difficult to snap together.... All in all, I wish I had passed on these.

review_headline: Baby and mommy both LOVE this swing!!
review_body:
I have to admit that I was on the fence about purchasing this swing. I registered for this and the Snugabunny bouncer and I received the bouncer as a gift at my baby shower. I never received the swing and thought I didn't really need a swing AND a bouncer...especially when the swing is so pricey. I've heard that some babies don't even like swings and that they grow out of them fast. All this convinced me that a swing was not necessary. About a month after our baby girl was born we finally finished her nursery and then I had a dilemma. I had been using the bouncer a lot in the living room where she and I were sleeping and spending most of the day and I couldn't decide if I wanted to have the bouncer downstairs in the living room or upstairs in her nursery. I had been given some amazon gift cards after the baby was born to buy something for the baby and myself. I considered just buying a second bouncer since the baby seemed to like it so much...but then I saw that the swing was still there on my registry. I had enough gift cards to cover the purchase so I made the leap and bought the swing. I figured if she didn't like it then I could return it and get the bouncer instead.

Let me just say...this swing was worth every penny and more. Even if it only worked for one day (which isn't the case...it's still going strong) I feel like I would have gotten my money's worth out of this. My baby girl LOVES it. She naps in it all the time but the best part is that I can set her down in it when my arms start to get tired and get at least a few minutes of rest...or 15 minutes to eat...or 30 minutes to get something else done. Sometimes when she's crying and all she wants is to be held or carried and I can't hold her any more (I have health issues) then I can set her in the swing and she calms down.

She's two months old now and she still loves the swing. She loves the mirror above her and will sit and look at the baby in the mirror, make faces at her, etc for several minutes. We use the nature sounds on the swing and she seems to like that more than the music. The first time she fell asleep in the swing it was swinging front to back...but ever since that first time she seems to prefer the side to side swinging. It's nice that there is the option to change it up though. She's not yet paying much attention to the birds on the swing...which is funny because she loves the ones on the bouncer...but I think it's because she's so fascinated by the mirror. Awake and asleep...she spends about 2-3 hours in the swing a day total spread out throughout the day and I am one VERY happy mommy.

This swing has saved my arms and I definitely feel that it is worth the money. We should get several more months out of it but even if she grew out of it tomorrow I would feel like we got our money's worth out of it. I am SO happy with this swing and recommend it highly...especially if you have a baby who likes to be swayed or rocked. Our girl loves it!

UPDATE 3/28/15: Baby is 4 months old now and we still love this swing. We only use it once or twice a day...but it is a great item to have. Our baby girl does NOT take naps...but sometimes if we are VERY lucky she will take a short 30 minute nap in the swing. Most of the time she just quietly plays in there and makes faces at the baby in the mirror or jabbers at the mirror. Now that she's using her hands more she really like playing with the bunny that is attached to the seatbelt. Our girl is still less than 13 lbs so I think we still have a lot of time left to use this. Still thrilled with the purchase!

UPDATE 9/4/15: Baby girl is now 9.5 months old and we are still using the swing for nap times. She weighed in at 16lbs 5oz at her 9 month check up...she's such a little thing...so I expect we still have some time yet to use this. the swing works as good as ever and still is just like new. Our little girl still loves the mirror and when she wake up from her naps usually spends 10-15 minutes giggling, laughing, and smiling at herself in the mirror. I cannot recommend this swing enough and am so glad we bought it.

UPDATE 4/20/16: Baby girl is 17 months old now and still take naps in this swing. It is absolutely one of the best purchases we made. The swing still works like a dream.ling at herself in the mirror. I cannot recommend this swing enough and am so glad we bought it. UPDATE 4/20/16: Baby girl is 17 months old now and still take naps in this swing. It is absolutely one of the best purchases we made. The swing still works like a dream.

review_headline: This version is much better than new ComfortMe
review_body: Summer Infant is genius with the double zippers. I don't know why other companies don't do the same. It makes overnight diaper changes so much easier and no threading the zipper to deal with.    This (peek-a-boo Safari in medium)  must be an older or discontinued model, as it does not seem to be shown on Summer Infant's website. It appears to have been replaced with the ComfortMe, which has half sleeves and is more blanket-like in coverage). This older model is superior in quality (cotton fabric is slightly thicker and the zipper doesn't feel cheap like the new model. It's also easier to pick up my child without the new designs awkward sewn-together sleeves).    I would buy more of these in a heartbeat if I could find them in a large. My baby is now 6.5 months, 26 inches and 19.5 lbs and the medium is nearing the end of its life for us. We should be able to get at least another month or two out of it, depending on growth spurts. My baby already can also comfortably fit into the newer model of the ComfortMe (which I dislike). We have had 2 of these in medium and the monkey barrels in small (we outgrew small several months ago). They have all held up great in the wash and received daily nap and nighttime use for months.    Bottom line: buy these for your lightweight cotton sleep sacks instead of the newer ComfortMe model or another brand. The price is great and the quality is there.

review_body:

product_title: Pumpin' Pal Breast Pump Flanges
review_headline: I thought they would be great as a spare set with my Medela personal fit ...
review_body:
I thought they would be great as a spare set with my Medela personal fit connectors. I use a Simple Wishes hands-free bra for pumping and can easily walk across the room with it on with my normal Medela shields attached. But with these, I cannot move or else the flange comes loose from the connectors and the connector falls right off along with the bottle! I was just SITTING in a chair trying to pump (second time using them. Decided to wait til I was seated before attaching them after the time I was standing and saw one fall) and somehow the connectors fell off, landing in my lap and dripping some milk on me. I am trying to build supply, not waste milk. They just don't fit securely like the Medela ones. What a disappointment. Also, the smallest size available gives you a shorter length piece to attach to the connector than the larger sets. I didn't really see a significant benefit in the angled design, either. I still didn't feel like I could lean back to pump.

I have a terrible Evenflo electic pump as well so I tried the flanges on the Evenflo horn (horn is not removable) in an attempt to make the Evenflo a better fit for me. I felt NO vibration/suction at all. I think this is more an issue with the Evenflo product than the Pumpin Pals product but it made me wonder how well it works with other one-piece flange sets. Also, I imagine it would easily fall out just like it did with my connector piece, but I don't know. Maybe the horn is a safer way to keep it secure than the personal fit connectors.

To sum it up... I know the Pumpin Pals website says they were designed to go shield into shield but the site says they do work with removable shield sets as well. If they were a snug fit with my personal fit connectors I would be happy but they are not. I read a review that made me think they would fit well but maybe I just got a dud? I feel like I should have spent the money on a second Medela set of flanges instead of these...

review_headline: Beautiful diaper bag-purse hybrid that doubles as a camera bag
review_body:
I've been in the market for a diaper bag purse hybrid and this bag not only fits the bill but is beautiful. The leather is so soft that I will end up petting my purse just to feel the softness of the leather.

I have a 3 year old and newborn. I use a diaper wallet that I throw in the stroller and keep a tote in our car that functions as the "main" diaper bag. So I just wanted a purse that had lots of pockets to fit all those things you need to carry when you have kids. Snacks for the toddler, and toys to keep the newborn amused. The two smaller inside pockets are great for carrying the toddler's water bottle and I stuff her snacks in the other. The big side pocket is large enough to keep my wallet in, although right now I have a little makeup bag and a little case for teething items/pacifiers. The front pocket on the outside of the purse is very deep and large enough for any size phone, pens, etc. The inside zippered pocket is also deep. This bag does not scrimp on pockets!

I also usually carry a camera, which is the real reason I wanted such a large purse. I shoot with a Canon 7D + Sigma 18-35, which is a little hefty, not too massive. All the pockets in this are large enough to hold the kids' & my items and place the camera in the main body of the bag.

I love the two strap types which add versatility and style. The handle is big enough to wear over the shoulder if desired, or hung on your forearm/elbow as is the current trend. The crossbody strap is removable.

Inside the bag there is also a carabiner clip for keys, and on each side a stroller attachment strap/clip. I believe all OiOi bags have this and if you google it you will find images of them in use.

The purse also comes with a bottle warmer, a diaper changing mat, a plastic wipes case and a small plastic cosmetic type bag.

This is such a stylish diaper bag, I don't even consider it as such. I think of it as money invested in a purse which will be useful for years to come. product_title: Ergobaby Bundle of Joy Carrier and Infant Insert
review_headline: Comfortable, safe and easy on the back
review_body:
The ERGObaby is truly a pleasure to use. It is comfortable to wear, and my 4 month old is comfortable in it. We previously had the Bjorn baby carrier, and its poor design made our baby instantly uncomfortable and fussy since it only supports the crotch and the legs hang free. The ERGObaby supports our baby in a natural sitting position, and she was never uncomfortable and was so cozy she fell asleep. It also has a built in cover that can be snapped on over either shoulder or both that protects the baby from the rain, or the sun.

We were able to to outside in typical Seattle winter weather watching the Christmas boats on the lake and baby was quite comfortable.

Initially it may feel that the baby is squished, but if you put your hands inside and adjust your baby to make sure they're centered and snug, you will find that they'll be safe and quite warm. They'll also keep YOU quite warm.

Pros
Comfortable for baby
Padded, wide straps
Easy to put on
Infant liner (excellent addition to keep newborns safe)
Extra pocket for a diaper or two
Nice-looking
Easy on the back, very well balanced

Cons
If you're chubby, be aware that the strap may not fit. My son weighs 300lbs, and the strap just barely fits around his waist when he carried the baby.

product_title: 4Moms 2014 MamaRoo
review_headline: Gave it a total of 4 month trial but ended up returning - baby hated it. He didn't mind it quite so much ...
review_body:
This is a review for 4Moms Mamaroo, Multi Plush.
Gave it a total of 4 month trial but ended up returning - baby hated it. He didn't mind it quite so much as a newborn since he was mostly asleep ( most newborns are more asleep than awake), but once he passed 1 month that was the end of mamaroo for us.
Why we didn't like it:
1. Side to side motion did not sit well with the baby - he wants a back and forth kind of like Graco glider offers (http://www.amazon.com/Graco-2-Glider-Elite-Swing/dp/B00CXVOOZG). Graco glider saved us instead.
2. Toys are as boring as can get - don't move, can't touch
3. Position not comfortable for the baby

Positives:
1. Easy to assemble - video available (also useful video on how to unassemble and put back in the box so you can return it)
2. Fabric is soft to touch and feels nice ( most baby swings/gliders are like that though)
3. Has an audio plug in so you can play your own music (do people really use that?!)

Overall I would say skip this one. Buy Graco 2-in-1 Glider Elite Swing - Brompton instead - provides amazing gliding function that rocks baby right to sleep and also can be picked up ( just the seat portion) and carried to another room without disturbing the baby.
Also, great for the baby was http://www.amazon.com/Fisher-Price-Cradle-Swing-Adapter-Little/dp/B0092YYGMS/ref=sr_1_1?s=baby-products&ie=UTF8&qid=1421782713&sr=1-1&keywords=lamb+swing. Great rocking - either side to side or back and forth. 2 seating positions. Very soft and baby will love to be in it.

Thank you Mamaroo you are just not for us.

product_title: Zenoff Products Nursing Pillow Slipcover
review_body: Hands down the best breastfeeding pillow!  I bought mine at the recommendation of a friend, after doing a ton of research. The market is saturated by Boppy, whose ubiquity was reinforced by recommendations by the majority of my family and friends. Well, I think they all recommend Boppy because they've never tried another pillow!  I bought a Boppy at a discount store, and tried it as well. The Boppy is thicker (higher lift presumptively) and softer than this, also curved top...but I needed support for my baby, not softness. My baby sunk into and rolled off of the Boppy, usually toward me, and into the space between the pillow and me, pushing the pillow away from my body, so I struggled to keep it on, constantly holding it in my arms in a pseudo-hug.    I at first thought the idea of a wrap-around flat pillow with a belt and \\"bumps\\" was strange...but after my Boppy failures I understood these features were the solutions to my problems!  My baby doesn't roll off the flat surface, and the belt keeps the pillow up against by body, so my hands are free to hold and touch my baby during feedings. Even better - if I am reclining in my glider, the belt angles the pillow up, letting gravity keep my baby close to my body. Boppy is great for lounging baby and tummy time (which this pillow should not be used for). But if you are looking for a serious pillow for breastfeeding (which you spend a lot more time doing), save yourself some frustration and buy this!!  I've bought one for our second home, one to keep at my parents' house and a travel one too. So worth the money. Don't hesitate to buy it - you'll love it!

product_title: Ergobaby 360 All Carry Positions Award-Winning Cool Mesh Ergonomic Baby Carrier, Carbon Grey
review_headline: Ergobaby 360 vs Organic vs Beco Baby Gemini
review_body:
I researched and tried all 3; here are the pros and cons of each, and ultimately which one I decided on.

Beco Baby Gemini
Pros: cheapest option of the 3. You can have baby face in, face out, hip, and back carry. Slim profile, which some smaller people might like. This can be used for newborns without the cost of an extra insert. You can wear the back straps backpack style, or crossed for more support. Can flip the front up for privacy and more support for younger babies.
Cons: it felt stiff to me and not as comfortable as Ergobaby. My husband has back issues, and it didn't seem like it would work as well for him. Weight limit is less than the Ergobaby organic; I don't see myself carrying my boy to 45 lbs but with how tall he's planning on being it's nice to have the extra support. 2 part safety buckle on the hip belt is ridiculously hard to operate, and someone with bigger hands may seriously consider cutting the darn thing off. I also didn't like adjusting the different crotch positions with snaps; felt like over time the fabric might rip.

Ergobaby 360
Pros: Same 4 carry positions as Beco. No adjustments necessary at the crotch area to switch between front in and front out. Wide, comfortable hip belt. Has a sleep hood, which tucks away in a zippered pocket.
Cons: most expensive of the 3. Front facing out position is only good for 22 lbs, and then it's a regular 3 position carrier again. Material is a rough twill, and the current color options aren't the most attractive. Lastly, the hip belt is velcro, which I hate. Wrecks clothes, and could wake a sleeping baby if you take it off in the same room.

Ergobaby Organic
Pros: Oeko-Tex certified organic fabric, and it is soft! Like a brushed twill. Plus, healthier for baby. Weight limit is higher, so hopefully we'll get full use out of it. Has a pocket in front, large enough for phone, lip balm, cash and a few cards. Easy to get on and off with baby, I've only tried front position so far since he's still little. Hip belt dips down a little in front, preventing any unsightly bulge squeezing out.
Cons: only 3 positions,with no face out option.

Ultimately which one is right for you depends on your preferences.
It's recommended that baby not face out for more than 20 minutes at a time, and the weight limit for this position is low. A hip position can potentially give babies most of the visibility from this vantage point. This is why I didn't really care about losing the face out position.
I hate velcro, and didn't dig the 360's fabric. The 2 part buckle on the Beco Gemini was just too frustrating to deal with every time.
I'm 5'7 and my husband is 6'4,and the Ergobaby Organic was comfortable for both of us! Baby loves it so far, he's just tall enough (24 inches) to peek out at the world, and has fallen asleep comfortably a few times for quick naps.

review_body: I am not a fan of potty training. Perhaps it has to do with my husband teaching my son to pee standing up. Predictably, he does not have great aim. You just have to be the adult around the house and make sure that thing gets dumped and rinsed a few times a day. I don't think I have to tell adults that pee stinks if you leave it sitting around. And it scales if you don't rinse often enough. Thats why real toilets flush. But this costs 15 bucks. Don't expect perfection. Grown men can't make it happen most of the time. Things drip.
