review_headline: This monitor is great for the price
review_body:
This monitor is great for the price. I had another brand before this one for my first child and it almost immediately had static interference all the time. So far, this one has none. It has everything that I was looking for, which was really just video and sound capability. I gave it 4 stars because of a couple of things that are starting to occur, I've been using it for about 4 months now. It takes a while to start up when you turn it on versus my other one which just turned on immediately with a dial. Once in awhile, the monitor will beep loudly out of nowhere and signal that there is no signal, even though nothing has moved or changed. This is very startling when it happens in the middle of the night. I am assuming that this is just some sort of interference, but I can't be sure. You then have to turn it off and on again and it is fine. My only other complaint is when it is in the VOX ON setting, where it will hibernate when there is no sound, if I turn it off when it's in this setting and then turn it on again later, it doesn't always register when the baby wakes up, so I've had times where I haven't heard him crying until I am near his room.
They do have great customer service, which is something that can be very hard to come by. Our first monitor fell over on the nightstand and the antenna cover broke off. I contacted customer service and they emailed me back within an hour, I believe. They also sent a replacement monitor right away once I sent mine back, before it even was received by them. The video and sound are good for what I was looking for. I did lots of research before purchasing since this was my second monitor. This one is great for the price.

The only two features I like about it are the soothing buttons- well sort of. The vibrator helped but we never left it on for more than a few minutes because it felt too strong. Too many adjustments.  -Waist strap is too low and doesn't provide any weight support. My lats were sore.  -It's enormous on and off in the bag.  -Not easy to switch from front to back. product_title: Fisher-Price First Steps Count 'n Teethe Soft Book
review_headline: More Fun Than Our Other Soft Books
review_body:
Baby soft books are pretty simplistic without a lot going on so there is very little for a parent to consider when buying one. That said, compared to other soft books I have, this one seems to provides for more visual, tactile, and audio stimulation than others.

There are 3 cloth pages, which is equivalent to 6 readable pages (if you count the covers) and they contain colorful/adorable images. The mirror on one of the pages, attached toy and link, ribbons, and peek-a-boo flap (think cloth version of a flap book) adds to the visual appeal. For tactile stimulation, there are plenty of textures for baby to explore. The attached toy and link are plastic and make great teethers. The ribbon is different than fabric of the book and offers some contrast. The velcro closure also is a lot of fun for my little one. The book also makes more noises than just the sound of the crinkly pages. Baby can bang the two plastic pieces together and play with the velcro closure which makes a velcro sound. There is also a squeaker. And this book is bigger than my others which were around the same price.

These probably seem very minor to an adult, but that what made this soft book stand out from the others we own. Also, my girl loves cats so we were very happy to add this book to our collection.

I do wish there was at least one or two more pages even though 3 or 4 pages/flaps seem to be the standard amount for soft books. I would like to give this book 4.5 Stars...but since that's not an option, I bumped it up to 5 Stars.

NOTE: I just throw it into the washing machine with the rest of the laundry. I do put it in a laundry mesh bag to keep it from snagging my other clothes. Then air dry.

product_title: Chicco NextFit Convertible Car Seat, Mystique
review_headline: Tightening straps when rear-facing is too challenging
review_body:
I really want to love this seat. It fits well in our car (mid-size sedan), is easy to install, and seems to have more cushioning than a lot of the other seats out there. Given that we drive long distances to/from grandparents houses almost every weekend, making sure that our kiddo is comfortable is key.

We have an infant seat in one car (the KeyFit) and this seat in our other car. My in-laws have a KeyFit base and use that seat when they drive him around. Our kiddo is getting big enough that I'm starting to research purchasing 2 more seats- one to replace the KeyFit in our car and one for my in-laws. This seat was one of my top contenders. However, tightening the harness in our current car with the seat rear-facing is SO HARD that I'm investigating other options. Seriously, tightening the harness goes something like this: strap kid in, pull as hard as possible to tighten, check harness which is still way too loose, take a deep breath, tighten harder, check straps which are still too loose, take another breath and pull as hard as possible to get another 1/2 inch out of the straps. My husband's routine to get this seat tightened isn't any different. I also saw similar comments from other reviewers. Tightening the straps on our KeyFit is a breeze. I just don't know what makes it so hard on this seat.

Because of this issue and the fact that our child will be rear-facing for at least another 12 months after we install our new seats, I am considering other seats so I don't have to deal with this. I'm doubtful that my mother-in-law has enough strength in her arms/wrists to get the harness tight enough so our son is sufficiently secure. Since safety has to be the #1 priority with car seats, I'm looking elsewhere for something that will work better for all of us. I'm disappointed. Like I said above, I wanted to love this seat, but buying a seat where we can't properly secure our son isn't the right answer.

product_title: Motorola Remote Wireless Video Baby Monitor withColor LCD Screen
review_body:
We were given this monitor as a gift (from our registry) back in April 2013. Our child is now 18 months old and we still use this monitor nightly. Every function of the monitor still works except for the one that didn't really work to begin with: temperature reading. I saw another user post that it is roughly 5 degrees off and I'd completely agree. This morning the monitor showed that it was 72 degrees in my son's room but the fan we had running read 66. It was 48 degrees outside and this was a fan running, no hearer on in the house. It was very unlikely it was 72. Right now it reads 78 and after just being in there I'd say low 70's, no fan running. Best I can figure is it picks up body temperature heavily and not ambient room temperature.
Otherwise most amazing monitor I've ever seen and I love that we've had no returns and no problems with it at all whatsoever. Super clear picture in both day and night modes and the sound is sensitive, which is a must-have for first-time parents.

product_title: Sony 900 MHz BabyCall Nursery Monitor with Receivers (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Lasted over 2 years and still going strong!
review_body:
We got this as a baby shower present over two years ago for our son. Happy to say that it still works perfectly. Some minor issues when the receiver syncs to the mic, but these are few and far apart.

The feature that I enjoy most is the fact that the receivers are rechargeable. And the receivers have a handy clip that allows you to clip it on your belt, especially handy when you take out the garbage or run to a different section of the house. I have even left the charges receiver on for over 16 hours and was still functioning without it being plugged in.

The receivers also have a feature that only switches on when there is a significant sound made. Handy when you have a white noise generator playing next to the baby. The receiver won't sound the white noise but will activate with the sound of a rustle or cry or whimper from the baby.

All in all super happy with this monitor. Happy that it's lasted over 2 years and still going strong. Only minus is the sync issue which happens on occasion.

review_headline: Handsome furniture and excellent for the price
review_body:
This is a nice looking piece of furniture, once all is said and done. It is not actually nice furniture, and it was a bit annoying to assemble, but I'm giving it five stars because for the price point, it's really something.

As perhaps you realize, there is nothing that makes this \\"baby furniture\\". It's a chest of drawers.

I have assembled a variety of furniture over the past couple of years in my new home. A media center, bookcases, a CD cabinet, a pair of beds with underbed drawers. Some of this is \\"high end\\", as assemble-yourself furniture goes, and some is pressboard crap. A range, is my point, and several different pieces. This was not as well engineered as some, meaning that it could be easier to put together and be more foolproof, but it does look handsome in the end.

Pros:
1. Looks nice
2. Relatively low price
3. As well packed as the stuff I got from higher-end places
4. Larger than I was expecting
5. The instructions are reasonable

Cons:
1. The finish seems to get dinged pretty easily, like the veneer is not very sturdy. (This is in comparison to other veneered self-assemble furniture.)
2. Annoying allen-wrench screws for the first set of screws. All the other furniture I've assembled recently has philips head screws, and I use a screwdriver bit on my drill. Some of these had an awkward reach, but I found the allen wrench hard to set into the screw head. I wish at least the heads would have allowed a socket wrench or something. Those eight screws were really really annoying to get in and get tightened.
3. Not entirely foolproof assembly -- just ask this fool! There are dowels that help you make sure you've got parts in the right place before screwing them together, but it's possible to put things 180 degrees off at times. So you have to pay more attention than I was doing.
4. The top is attached with plastic pins. I don't like that idea at all; lots of people move chests of drawers by holding onto the edge of the top. There are eight pins holding that top on, and it'll probably be strong enough for moving this way, but meh.
5. There was a surprising amount of off-gassing when I opened everything up (and it still smells).

Indifferents:
1. Make sure you know that this is heavy. it comes in a flat-pack box that's hard to lift (99lbs), and instructs the shipping folks that it's a two-person carry.
2. There is lots and lots of packing material. A box within a box, styrofoam, and protective layers. It's a bit of a challenge to get everything out of the box, especially when the box is so heavy, and then you have the big pile of trash to get rid of.
3. I assembled this by myself, but the first part (putting together the outside cabinetry) would be a little easier with another set of hands.
4. The drawers are chipboard on the bottom, but have a support across the middle underneath to help support weight.
5. FYI that there are small furniture glides on the bottom (one for each leg)

review_headline: Very Comfortable and Secure (but a lot of fabric to fiddle with)
review_body:
The Moby is great for wearing my daughter around securely but it sure is a lot of fabric to fiddle with. The length of fabric does make it very easy to size and feel safe with though. I'm a 6'3" dad and my daughter was born weighing about 6.5lbs so there is a big disparity in size but she is comfortable and the variety of available positions makes it easy to shift her around if she is being fussy. Not to mention my wife is much smaller than I am and the one-size-fits-all design means we don't have to buy two of these!

It took a few weeks before I was comfortable wearing her but the Moby was the first wearing device I felt comfortable with her in. She still sometimes gets lost in some of the folds, and the design (one long cut of fabric) makes it more difficult to put on quickly than some other wraps out there, but overall it allows for a number of different hold positions and will work to grow with her.

On the plus side the biggest drawback (a ton of fabric) also happens to be a nice feature in that there are no hard edges, snaps, or clips to get caught in or bumped up against. This means I am free to move around without worrying about pinching her adorable legs or hands in something.

product_title: Diono Radian RXT All-In-One Convertible Car Seat, Shadow
review_body:
We've had this seat for a couple months now and here's the scoop now that it's broken us in...
We really like it.
It's narrow, it comes with a cup holder (and has 4 positions to choose from) and could fit up to 4 if we wanted that many. He has yet to be able to get the cup holder off and throw it. Double plus in my book. It's easy to put in the car, and you can also carry it with the backpack straps.
It's easy to pull the cover off to wash in case of accidents. Like the stomach virus that just went around.
Toddler thinks it comfy. We only got it recently and have only used it forward facing. I wish I had known about this seat before, I could have saved money on the 4 I bought before this.
My jeep is ancient and doesn't have LATCH, but this easily threads a shoulder belt and secures snuggly. (Which was the deciding factor in choosing between this and the recaro ).
The cons. Well really there's only one. The breast clip is easy to unclip.
Which would be fine of we didn't have a super mechanically inclined, creative toddler. Pretty much everyday he unclips the chest clip and takes his arms out. When I called customer service they said they don't offer another chest clip. However they offered to send me a replacement clip to give the toddler to play with. SMH. So I docked it one star for the clip.
I'll just replace the chest clip with a clip from one of the other car seats I have sitting in storage, then it'll be the perfect seat!
If you're struggling to decide on a car seat get this one.

product_title: Motorola Remote Wireless Video Baby Monitor withColor LCD Screen
review_headline: Iffy model, IMPROVED customer service! (plus MBP36s review!)
review_body: UPDATE 1/22/15    So, the day after my scathing review (see below) a wonderful rep from Motorola contacted me and offered to make the situation right. I couldn't be more grateful! Turns out, like the original unhelpful rep stated, they know of the issues with the MBP36 (notice it is now discontinued) so the new rep sent me a newer model (MBP36s). Surprise, surprise, its power cord connection point in the monitor is completely different! Much sturdier and I have had no issues as of yet (have had this for about a month I think now).     The MBP36s is essentially the same monitor with a few changes that I've noticed thus far:    1) Power connection point into the monitor resembles more of a firewire/phone cord connection.    2) Power cord end that plugs into the wall is more compact and square, taking up less space than the old cord when plugged in.    3) This monitor has a feature that allows you to set how long you want your monitor display to be on, showing your slumbering little one. This is set within the monitor screen and is next to the volume, contrast, temp, music, and zoom options. You can choose from 5, 30, or 60 min. My only complaint is when the monitor power is on but the screen is in power save mode (black screen) and you turn on the feed by pushing the video button, you get an irritating red icon on the screen accompanied by how long the monitor screen will stay on, e.g. \\"5 MINS <video feed icon>\\". This information is large enough that it essentially covers your sleeping little one until it goes away, a full 30 seconds later. Not a huge deal, but an irritant when all you want to do is take a quick peak and turn the feed back off to save power (which any closely monitoring parent is apt to do!). To quickly get the time alert to disappear you have to push any other button. Strangely, the \\"OK\\" button does not make this disappear and that's the button you'd think would have that effect. Again, not a big deal but Motorola could certainly keep it up for 3 seconds and that would be sufficient. Or better, just remove that completely. If one needs to be reminded of how long the timer is programmed for, one would just click over to it. It's basically unnecessary.    One option that isn't different is the minimum volume setting. It's still pretty loud for the minimum, especially when you have 8 noise levels from which to choose. Sometimes it's just quiet (we are trying to get them to sleep, after all!) and you want to hear if they fuss. But even on the lowest volume setting it's pretty loud and that means loud white noise you're listening to unless you mute it altogether. Many parents use white noise for the little ones to sleep to and if you are hoping to have a low volume option here, you won't get it. In a quiet room with the monitor next to me it's too loud to turn on and keep on unless I, too, want to be lulled (or driven crazy) by the white noise in his room.    All that being said, I will say I am quite impressed with Motorola's support (or at least the folks checking up on their product reviews, as opposed to those answering the phones!). I really appreciate them reaching out and saying \\"Hey, we stand behind our product, how can we make this right?\\" and actually DOING IT!    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~    I purchased this monitor in July 2013 and had very high hopes for it. Unfortunately, after several months the connection point within the monitor for the power adapter became loose. In order to charge my monitor I had to try all sorts of MacGyver tricks to keep just the right amount of pressure and angle on the connection point when the cord was plugged into it. Tiring of this pretty quickly, I called up Motorola and received a replacement as mine was still under the 1 yr warranty.    Life continued and wouldn't you know it, several months later it started again! Same issue, and same phone call to Motorola for a replacement.    It's now December 2014 and my third monitor is having the exact same issue. REALLY MOTOROLA?! What total crap construction on these things. The irritating beep that occurs every 20 seconds on this thing due to a low battery is now a noise that will forever haunt me and I'm seconds away from gouging my ears with a sharp object.    SOOOO...what do I do? I call Motorola again. But now, they say they can't help me as my original purchase was over a year ago and the warranty on my last replacement with them was over 90 days ago. Yes, that's right -- a ONE year warranty on what you purchase but only 90 days on the \\"new\\" replacement they send -- shady?! So now my only option is to find a monitor on eBay (the rep tells me) as they don't just sell the monitor separately. I tell her this is outrageous, that this is clearly a defective product and she tells me \\"Sorry\\" and they know about the issue and they have tried to improve it for the monitors they are making now. You can imagine how much this helps me.    LAME Motorola for not standing behind a product that KEEPS BREAKING. If it was reliable this product would be great. Even if the night picture is a tad grainy and the thermometer always registers 3 degrees higher than it really is.    Look elsewhere!

review_headline: I love this swaddle and so does my son
review_body: I love this swaddle and so does my son. He's been busting out of swaddles from the word go. In the hospital he got out of the blanket swaddles, so we bought velcro swaddles from Halo and Summer Infant, which were both good, but he would sneak out of them relatively quickly. They also had a tendency to end up covering his mouth because he would wrestle inside them so much. That scared the crap out of me. I loved the idea of a zip up swaddle like the pods, but I didn't like the fact that he'd literally have no way to mobilize his arms should he need to (like rolling over), so when I found this swaddle, I thought, perfect! He loves to self-soothe by putting his hands in his mouth so this allows him to do that and also feel secure. It's also really easy to change diapers in the middle of the night with the bottom zipper. The material is super soft and comfy with no velcro to rub against him like the other swaddles. I can pick him up comfortably under his arms to nurse during the night, which was always kind of awkward when he was in a regular swaddle. He also looks crazy cute in it, like a little snow angel! Highly recommended if your little one is a Houdini and a hand soother.

product_title: VitalTemp Non-Contact Thermometer Temperature Range from 89.0 to 107F Surface Temperature Sensor -58 to 500F
review_headline: A Lesson in Precision vs. Accuracy
review_body:
Both my wife and I got a reading somewhat below accepted body temp. Neither of us was ill or did we take anything that would lower our core temp. My real life job involves research and statistics, I thought this would be a great way to demonstrate precision vs. accuracy. Fortunately we had some family and friends over later that day, so there was enough of a sample to conduct a proper study. Before the football game (Fly, Eagles Fly!) and the subsequent cold beers and hot pizza, we took the temps of five adults three times each. We used a glass oral thermometer and the Instaread, that's 15 readings for each instrument. We followed the directions on the Instaread to ensure consistent usage. The glass thermometer was cleaned, allowed to cool, and 'shook down' between readings. I plugged the numbers into Graph Pad Quick Calc (http://www.graphpad.com/quickcalcs/ttest1.cfm). Here's the results:
Oral Thermometer; Mean-=98.14; SD=0.35. Insta Read; Mean=95.59, SD=0.75. The P value was less than 0.0001. This is a statistically significant difference.
The results from both measures were precise, meaning each device, looked at by itself, repeated consistently over the sample. But if the oral thermometer (and accepted human body temp) is the reference standard, the Insta Read is not accurate. I guess if you add a 'fudge factor' of about +2.5 you can tell if somebody has a fever. If you rely on the readings of the device to determine fever, you should confirm by another method such as, my wife putting her hand on our kids forehead and announcing \\"You have no fever, get to school\\"!
EDIT 12/1: While thinking about this, I realized that two stars is a bit harsh. Added a star for two reasons. (1). The device was not defective or poorly produced. The construction is quality. (2). We did another test with another brand. The findings were consistent with this one. I guess the only way you can have precesion and accuracy is to use either a regular oral thermometer or pay a few hundred bucks for a hospital grade non-contact thermometer. There is no free lunch.l thermometer or pay a few hundred bucks for a hospital grade non-contact thermometer. There is no free lunch.

product_title: Britax Pinnacle 90 Booster Car Seat, Manhattan (Older Version)
review_headline: A bit disappointed with Britax. There are other Britax that are better, not to mention the Recaro.
review_body:
I bought this Britax Pinnacle 90 Booster Car Seat, Manhattan and a Recaro and I have to say the Recaro is a much nicer seat. First is the construction. The Recaro is just more robust. The sides really feel like they could take an impact. The Britax? Not really. it looks awesome in the picture till you find out that black side impact is a hollow plastic chamber. You can easily punch thru it with your fist. And what looks like really thick padding is more like a pillow with a stiff member inside.The Recaro's is a very tough feeling plastic. I slammed on it, the Recaro, (open palm) many times and it feels like it can take a pretty good hit. But if I did that to this Britax Pinnacle 90 it would collapse and permanently deform.

Also my child really struggles trying to fall asleep in the Pinnacle 90. He can never really get comfortable. So we are keeping the Recaro and sending the Pinnacle 90 back. (and keeping the Britax Pavilion 70.)

Lastly, I do not know why everyone complains about the latch system of installing any car seat let alone this one. It's by far the best way to secure the seat. I have never had any problem using the latch system on this Recaro, or the Britax Pinnacle 90, or the Britax Pavilion 70 that we still use and love. It does take a bit of effort, but your kid is worth it. :-) The latch system with the click on this Pinnacle 90 is excellent. Clearly the easiest latch system to use. And it looks great, it has cup holders, and arm rests, etc... But for the comfort and safety of my child.... there are other car seats I feel are better.

review_headline: Built like a Tank - probably the best out there (but heavy)
review_body:
UPDATE: I recently received the opportunity to review the [[ASIN:B009S1DWP2 Diono Radian R120 Convertible Car Seat Plus Booster, Storm]] and I have that review there if you want to read it. Basically, fairly similar seats but this one I think offers better side impact protection (and a nice headrest for your child to sleep -- similar to the Radian RXT) at the expense of it maybe not being as comfortable when your kid gets to be taller. Overall, tremendous seats, you can't go wrong with any of the Diono line but you do have choices to make.

As a father of two adorable girls, I've agonized over car seat decisions for a long time. Let me share what I have found about this car seat and in general but this review is no substitute for a lot of research:

STEEL CONSTRUCTION
- This car seat features a steel framework making it very strong. All the important components and side impact are constructed of steel. Your child will be as protected as possible in this thing. I'm not entirely against plastic in car seats, a lot of synthetic materials perform very well but there's a satisfaction to modern metals that is comforting.

- The metal does add weight so consider this carefully. I'm of the mind that this product is intended to be a permanent car seat in the primary vehicle vs a carseat that you take out and exchange between cars or a carseat that you plan to take on plane rides.

LATCH
- The latch system has been a joy for me to use in this car seat and in others. For smaller children, latch provides a convenient and quick mechanism to attach your car seat to your car. Instead of going through the motions of having put the seatbelt through various rabbit holes and then wondering if you did it right, latch provides a great and simpler and foolproof way to attach the car seat

- Latch. The problem that latch has always had is that in most cars up to 2013, it was only rated to 40lbs. This was the combined weight of baby + car seat, so very quickly you wound up having to go to the seatbelt once your kid got over 25lbs.

- Superlatch - This car seat has superlatch which means that it can hold kids up to 65lbs (combined weight of car seat and toddler) which is an improvement but there are a few caveats. If you want to use superlatch, both your car and the carseat have to be superlatch compatible.....if you have a 2006 car and a childseat equipped with superlatch, you really should hold to the lowest denominator which for most cars is 40lbs. I also noticed that this car seat has metal in it so it is heavier than average so you might not be getting much from superlatch in the sense that your kid might outgrow it pretty fast.

FIVE POINT HARNESS
- I recently had the terrible experience of driving by a highway accident where a child had been ejected from the vehicle. By the time my vehicle had gotten to the accident site, the child had been removed but a plain old bottoms only booster seat rested in the middle of the highway and it broke my heart ---- I'll keep my kids in five point harnesses as long as I possibly can.

- Five point harnesses are the safest and I will keep my kid in one forever.

- Know the weights of your child plus the babyseat and make sure you're attaching it correctly to your car.

REAR FACING
- Rear facing car seats save kids lives as well. This car seat can be set up to be rearfacing for infants. There are laws in every state for how long your child should be rear facing so please make sure you know your law and keep your kid rear facing as long as possible. I kept my children's seat in the rear facing position until I absolutely had to change.

- Bear in mind that this is a big car seat so in a rear facing position, it needs a lot of room so if you have a small car, look at your measurements carefully to make sure its going to fit, it might be a tight fir or you might lose oneof your front seats if you have a compact car.

- Consider a mirror or a baby presence alarm if you have your child in the rearfacing position. Every year, busy parents leave a child in a hot car and the majority of the ones I have heard about have involved a rear facing big seat where the parent just didn't see the baby. Do whatever you can to avoid these kinds of tragedies. Until my children could self rescue, this was one of the concerns that was always on my mind. I'm so glad we're past that phase.

COST & CHILDWEIGHT
- This car seat is intended to be the single car seat that you'll ever need from 5 to 120lbs. Very few carseats could make this claim when my children were first born so yes it is expensive up front but consider that you won't have to buy an infant car seat and you could be looking at a very cost effective solution here.

- The tradeoff is that you wind up with a big car seat up front and it can be very big in the rear facing position.

- The other tradeoff here is weight -- it's not a light car seat but it's constructed like a tank.

WEIGHT OF PRODUCT
- If you've ever lugged a car seat through the airport you know that it can be a royal pain. This car seat is too heavy to be lugging around through the airport in my honest opinion. This is the car seat that you put in your minivan and attach securely and know that your child has the highest level of protection. If you're going to be moving this car seat from car to car on a regular basis or taking it through an airport and you're a more petite lady, you're likely going to be unhappy. It's a set it and forget it thing.

- It does come with a strap for carrying and the seat folds flat against the back-rest making it easier to carry. Still, not the lightest thing out there.

- Consider carefully the measurements and take a tape measure to your car if you have a really small compact vehicle and you plan to use this in the rear-facing position.

ACCIDENTS
- Never buy a car seat used. There is a rule out there that if your car has been in an accident then the carseats that were in the vehicle should be discarded and not used because the forces in accidents are extreme and latches and buckles bend or get close to breaking points. If you buy a used carseat you don't know if it's been in an accident. Know the law and what the manufacturers recommend.
- I would never buy a used carseat for my most precious.

review_headline: Fantasy animal sounds are not helpful
review_body:
No, no, and noooo. Such a good idea and so disappointing.

I decided I could live with the sproing sound of the starfish, or three would have been gone.

product_title: Maymom Breast Pump Accessories for Medela Pump In Style Pumps, mm Large Breastshields
review_body:
I am primarily pumping because my little one was having difficultly latching on the breast. I was using a larger breast shield (27 and 30mm) and my breasts were getting really raw and painful. After reading other posts, I realized that I should try a smaller size. I tried both 19 and 21 mm. They were comparable. As with the experience of others, it was much more comfortable and I did get more milk (probably an ounce more each breast...each drop helps!). My mistake before was I thought it would be better if the whole areola was sucked in the tubing (that is why I was going with the larger size and that is why it was hurting. It is more efficient and less painful if it is only the nipple that is sucked in the tubing and that is why the smaller size works much better.

The price is also unbeatable! I pump every 2-4 hours so I bought enough sets so I don't need to wash after each pump. I just put them in the dishwasher at the end of the day.

product_title: Safety 1st Top-of-mattress Bed Rail, Cream
review_headline: Three minutes from box to bed... if you know what you're doing.
review_body:
Installing this was a bit of a pain in the backside, mostly because the instructions don't make it clear in Step 4 that the little lock symbols are _supposed_ to be showing red still. The instructions make it sound like 'click into place' is the kind of thing that should result in the green showing. But no, the colors are actually to show you've got the right tension against the mattress. So if you're stuck on step four, take a deep breath. If the mesh rail doesn't fall off the supports, you're doing it right.

Once in place, it is fairly sturdy. The tensioners press it into the mattress a few inches away from the edge, so there's no gap between the rail and the mattress. This means, of course, that you will have to take it off the bed every time you change the sheets. It also means your child is less likely to get stuck.

As the parent of a relatively young toddler who insists on sleeping on a big kid bed, this will save us a lot of future late-night loud thumps and sobbing child sessions.

I was so disappointed by this since my daughters room was just remodeled.  I'll just keep this up for a few years until regular repainting is in order - fortunately she is very young, and I put this in her reading nook, so it should be appropriate for a few years.  I've ordered other decals before, and they have always been easily removable....hence, why I like them - cute decoration with no wall repair to move things around.  Such a bummer that these did not serve me the same.

review_body: I’m a newbie in terms of cloth diapering, not having researched it during pregnancy like I should have. My baby is 3 months old and generally wakes up every 1.5 hours, I assumed to nurse, but I was curious as to whether he would go longer in between feedings (assuming he’s not in a growth spurt) if he stayed drier at night. Well … HE DID! The first night we tried the overnight diaper, I was thrilled when he slept for 3 straight hours, ate, then after I determined he still felt dry, he slept for another 3 straight! A few nights later, same thing! (Now I just have to learn to sleep that long, since I constantly wake up to check on him :)). I went to the actual website (http://happyendingsecodiapers.com) and found even more prints and deals, and I’m following on Facebook to take advantage of discounts and sales to further increase our stash. The affordability of these makes me much less anxious about weeding out ’sposies because of the cost!

product_title: Buttons Flannel Baby Wipes - 15 Pack
review_body: Note that I did not buy these for their intended use.  I had purchased handkerchiefs to break from the ecologically unsound habit of using disposable tissue (which clogs landfills and contains dioxin) because they can be washed and re-used (with a bit of bleach for those who need to sanitise them thanks to cold or flu germs).  Handkerchiefs, though, proved too large and bulky for the pocket and began to fall apart fairly quickly.  Then I read about reusable wipes and kept reviewing until I found these where various people have stated they are too thin.  They are - for baby wipes, but they were the perfect size for a hankie. I can tuck four or five in a pocket (I carry a sandwich baggie to tuck the used ones in for later laundering).  They are very strong and have held up to more than a few washes already. In a pinch or for travel, I take a bar of tea tree soap (natural, non-toxic germ-killer) and scrub them out by hand and hang them on a hanger. They dry within a few hours and are perfectly sanitary, and more important - keeps germy paper from the landfill and saves a few trees.  So I give them full stars and will definitely be purchasing more as these eventually wear down.  Not anytime soon, though, I'm thinking as they are very nicely constructed.

review_headline: This is an upgrade from a Graco IMO.
review_body:
Overall, this is a pretty great seat. I believe the pros out-weigh the cons when compared to a graco. You're going to have to be careful with the seat cover though. It's not really all that durable. Hand wash if possible. if you MUST put it through the washer do a thorough hand clean-up first and stuff it into a pillow case first so it gets handled more gently.

Also, note that several other reviewers seem to have dinged them for the sunshade. I looked at this pretty closely. I honestly don't see an issue with it. It doesn't have a window, but i'd prefer it not. They mentioned it's flimsy... mine seems stiff if anything. Perhaps they changed the design?

One of the other reviewers also mentioned that this doesn't sit well in a standard grocery shopping cart. that's not good, though I haven't tried that myself so I'm not listing it as a Con that I've seen.

Pros:
- Very well made / sturdy
- Includes awesome indicator built right in showing you if you have the seat at the right angle or not
- Detaches from base
- Easy to install
- AMPLE room for kid.
- Love the side impact cushions. this is a major safety bonus IMO.

Cons:
- Straps are a bit short compared to other seats (not good if you have a big kid)
- Seat cover/Liner isn't really made all that well. Looks like it's not intended to be washed.

product_title: 4moms, Baby Bath Tub, White
review_body:
While 4Moms as a company carries a great reputation, this bath tub is not one of the better products.

The tub was gifted to us, so I have given it a chance a few times.

I am a second time mom and have a lot of infant experience prior to my own babies. This tub is overkill, in my opinion -- however, it appears many other parents and caretakers like it. So, just do your research.

This tub is not a necessity. It's bulky. Finding storage for it without creating an eye sore in your bathroom or home is difficult. However, since it's made for infants, it really shouldn't be around past five months or so (depending on your baby's size and ability to sit up a bit).

I find a bath sling way easier to store, set up, clean and wash an infant. I'm going back to it because, unfortunately, my 11lb infant at two months old really seems awkward and uncomfortable in the 4Moms bath tub. He slips around a lot.

Apparently some parents find the thermostat a helpful feature. I am comfortable with my instinct and awareness to gauge water temp and my infants temp, as well, so I don't find that feature necessary. If my husband was any good at washing a newborn, he would probably rely on the thermostat for peace of mind.

product_title: BOB Sport Utility Duallie Stroller, Orange
review_body: I have had the BOB Sport Utility Duallie Stroller for over a year now. I wanted to wait and post a review after I had used it extensively. The only reason I bought this stroller was to run. I run at least 4 times a week and am currently training for a marathon. I bought this to push my 4 year old and 1 year old during my runs. Both kids fit perfectly and there was room to grow for  both of them. I really do not like that the negative reviews on this stroller have to do with the fixed front wheel. This is an amazing jogging stroller, meant for running. The fixed wheel is necessary when running! It is very dangerous to run with a swivel wheel in that it may swivel just as you hit a bump and could cause the whole stroller to flip. This stroller takes some getting used to as it isn't easy to push two kids around while running no matter what. Once you get it down and get comfortable with how it moves, I feel it is a great stroller for a runner. The only con I found with it, was that it was hard to get it to track straight. Mine always ran to the left. This was easily fixed as I took it to a local bike shop and they did it for me for less than $10. It now runs perfect! A great investment if you are planning on using it as a jogging stroller. If you are planning to walk, then I definitely recommend the Revolution.

product_title: Reusable Food Pouch Uniquely Transparent for Easy Cleaning
review_body:
So, we've all heard of Go-Go Squeeze, it's a mass producer of fruit sauce pouches, that were meant to have the convenience of Go-Gurt and be long lasting like canned goods or dried foods. But they can be quite expensive, have additional ingredients, and also are not reusable. It is much cheaper, in the long run to buy apples, pears, other fruits or veggies, and yogurt and make smoothies, fruit sauces, or healthy juices right at home. While I wish these pouches came with an e-book of recipes and ideas and also instructions for beginners, these pouches are super easy to use and also easy to clean.

My kids love these pouches. I make home made apple sauce, berry apple sauce, and pear sauces and they love that they are like the Go-Go Squeeze they so love, and I love that I know what goes in them and saved a bunch of money by using them. The see through front is super convenient as my kids and hubby can see what is in them and grab whatever variety of whatever I've made and drink it on the go. I like the convenience of being able to grab a pouch and go do what I need to do but still get either a healthy snack or meal substitute (smoothies etc) that leave me feeling refreshed and re-energized.

These pouches are easy for me to open from the bottom and fill, yet stay closed tight even when my kids squeeze them stongly. the easy open pouch and see through feature also make them extremely easy to clean and tell if a spot has been missed or if there is still soap in the pouch after rinsing. I really love the screw tops because then my youngest can not just grab a pouch and open it up without help or make a mess as he's prone to doing and yet I can open it up and he can easily drink whatever is in the pouch, whether it be apple sauce or yogurt. These pouches are thick and durable, easy to use and clean, and a great way to save money and know exactly what my children (and my husband and I) are putting in their bellies. Overall a great product and I plan to buy more so I can stock up on home made snacks and freeze some as well for future use.uy more so I can stock up on home made snacks and freeze some as well for future use.

product_title: Ubbi Diaper Pail
review_body:
I'm giving this a generous one star rating, one star instead of none because it did work well the first 3 months and it is nice that it doesn't require special bags. Yes, its much more attractive than the average diaper pail but does it live up to its advertised description regarding the non-absorption of odor due to its powdered coated steel interior? Absolutely not. It did for a few months but it was short lived. I'm beyond compulsive about regular bag changes, I close the door to the pail as quickly as humanly possible, I've tried various scented bags, I've even begun to put the soiled diapers in individual grocery bags, tied shut, before they go into the ubbi...all to no positive end. My daughter's room stinks. Im realistic and I certainly never expected this can to not smell at all when opened, but this darn thing reeks even when its empty and airing out outside! My husband and I have been fanatical from the beginning of our sweet baby's arrival about cleanliness, and especially about odors. I'm unsure of what else we can do to make this diaper pail effective. The odor it has even when the door is closed is absolutely foul, and its beginning to make the entire house reek. I am a sensible, clean loving mom, without abnormal product expectations. Ive used as instructed. It's a major disappointment.
Sorry, Ubbi. I wanted to love you, I really did, but alas, I do not. Not one bit.

product_title: SnotSuk TM Nasal Aspirator for Infants
review_body:
My Thoughts

I'm just going to be really honest and get this out of the way up front. Yes, this is kind of gross! When Ir dad that Snot Suk is done by literally, sucking the snot out of your baby's nose with your mount, I was a little bit disgusted. I thought, there is no way I'm doing that! And yet, I did!

How Does it Work?

Well, you literally do suck it out of your baby's nose but it's a little bit more hygienic than that! If you look at the image, there is a mouthpiece that you suck on, connected to a tube, connected to the piece that goes in the baby's nose. In that piece, before it hits the tube, is a filter that gathers everything so it does NOT pass though the tube into your mouth.

51u4141iD2L._SL1500_

Does it Work?

Yes, it actually works! To me it was easier than a bulb syringe. I use them as infrequently as possible and I just never got the hang of it. It seemed like you almost had to shove it in hard to plug the air to suction the snot. This gets it out even if you don't have a good seal in the nostril. I actually like that you control the power of the suction with your mouth.

Using It

I found this to be much less traumatic to use! It's easier to get in the nostril and doesn't have to be as precise and it doesn't have that same startling effect that the bulb syringe seems to always have.

Is it Hygienic?

I know it's hard to get past the psychology of sucking the snot out. I'm still not completely over it. But have you heard reports of what's in those bulb syringes? I mean you can never really get them completely clean and I've read about the disgusting things they've found when cutting off the end to investigate. This has a filter and everything comes completely apart to be cleaned so it's actually much cleaner.

The Cost

This is $14.95 on Amazon so more expensive than your average bulb syringe BUT much more effective! I spent more then that on bulb syringe's that DIDN'T work.

My Conclusion

I still cringe just a little bit at the thought of sucking my baby's snot out his nose. But when I used SnotSuk and saw how effective it was and much less traumatic for Jax, I'm a believer!re then that on bulb syringe's that DIDN'T work.

product_title: Motorola Baby Monitor LCD Screen
review_body:
My first experience with a video baby monitor was at a friend's house. They had received a free monitor when buying a car seat - and I thought "hey, how cool!" Except when I actually looked at the picture on their screen it looked like an ultrasound and I wondered how they were using that to see their baby it all. It looked like a gray screen to me.

Insert the MBP33S. Out of the box I could already tell it was much more sleek than my friend's unit, and installing it was a breeze. The hardest part was getting the battery installed (and there isn't anything tricky there unless you're not good with a screwdriver).

Buttons on the side of the monitor allow you to increase or decrease both the volume and brightness, which are by far the most used features on a monitor anyway. This monitor can also play music and has the ability for a two way radio (though if you have a baby that will calm down after hearing your voice through a speaker I applaud you). You could use this if someone is in the room with the baby, though - perhaps this is what the manufacturer intended this for.

The temperature gauge seems very accurate, and the camera can be mounted. You can't control the camera via the monitor, but this shouldn't really be an issue anyway if you spend a minute getting a good angle on the crib.

Once your children have grown, you could use this monitor in lots of other creative ways. An ill person or animal could be monitored (and the two way radio for an ill person could be quite useful).

Overall this a great quality camera for both picture and sound, especially if you've seen and used some of the low grade video monitors that exist now.

product_title: Graco ComfortSport Convertible Car Seat
review_headline: Fine as an affordable, 2nd car seat
review_body: We bought this as a 2nd car seat for our son, who was 18 months old at the time of purchase.  Our primary car seat is a Chicco Nextfit Convertable car seat which cost arount $279.99 when we bought it.  This seat was much less expensive, and after receiving it/using it, it is apparent why that is.  This seat was much harder to attach and change from rear to forward facing than our other car seat.  This seat is not adjustable (inclide, height) the way our Chicco seat is.  Also the padding and quality of materials that make up this Graco Seat are not of the same caliber as the Chicco Nextfit seat that we own.  The Graco seat also lacks any shoulder pads, and we found that on longer trips the shoulder harness belts seemed to leave red marks on our son's neck.  We ended up purchasing separate harness pads to remedy that. To be fair, all car seats have to meat the same testing requirements, and this seat does that at a very affordable price.  One positive note, is we found that since this seat is not as bulky as our other seat from Chicco, it is easier to take our son in and out of the car.  I would recommend this to someone who needs a 2nd, economical car seat for short errands around town.  For longer drives/trips, I would invest in something a little more comfortable.

product_title: Skip Hop Pronto Changing Station, Metro Stripe (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Excellent design, easy to use, skip the red wipes case.
review_body: My daughter is 22 months old and we have been using this since the day we came home from the hospital.  I have the metro stripe version.  I love the bold bright colors since it hides any dirt.  We used it in the beginning for all those diaper changes at home instead of buying a changing table that we did not have room for.  I have used it in the dirtiest bathrooms, and I am glad that it wipes down easily.  I have not had any issues with the quality.  Mine is extremely well made, and with high quality materials.  The exterior is a sturdy nylon waterproof fabric, and the interior is lined with a clear plastic that is easy to clean.  The design is excellent.  There is a wrist strap that is adjustable and also has a plastic buckle for easy hanging on the stroller handle. There is also numerous zipper pockets for extra storage of small items.    The one negative is the red wipes case that it comes with.  The case is extremely difficult to snap closed and does not have a tight seal, so the wet wipes can dry over a period of time if the wipes are not used frequently.  It does not hold many wipes, and the red color from the case stains the wipes pink.  As other reviewers mentioned, the wipes case is pretty useless and takes up valuable space.  The case however, is not bad enough for me to lower the rating for the entire changing station.    The most important thing about this changing station is that it can be easily opened and closed with one hand.  I have used it in the strangest locations, where you need to hold the baby in one hand, and get the changing station set up with the other hand.  Everything unravels with just a click of the buckle, and you can fold everything up easily with one hand after you are done.    I also love the fact that you can just take this for short trips without lugging the large diaper bag around.  I have this stocked up with a few diapers for those quick errands or a going to the neighborhood playground.  Its a must have for all parents with babies.

product_title: Spectra Baby USA S2 Double/Single Breast Pump, 3.3 Pound
review_headline: Perfect investment for any breastfeeding mom!
review_body:
Don't think too long, just get this pump. It has been amazing! I went through 4 different pumps, including renting a hospital grade Medela Symphony, this pump definitely stands out of all of them.
Pros:
- Very light, compact, and easy to carry around.
- Unlike every single pump I have tried, does NOT lose sucktion after awhile.
- It has a timer! So handy to keep track of how long you have been on.
- Customizable in every way from strength to frequency of pumps, which is just amazing when you are just starting out.
- Fashionable, has a light for night pumping. Trust me, looking at some of those ugly pumps gets frustrating after awhile, this one is actually pleasant to the eye, so you don't feel like you have some scary machine attached to you.
- Easy to wash! The parts are quite large and easy to get to with just your fingers so you don't have to get some oddly shaped special brushes to wash it!
- No moisture in tubes!!! Ah, tubes are so hard to wash, but thanks to the closed sucktion system Spectra has, you will rarely if ever need to wash the tubes!
- Yes! It helped increase my supply! I have yet to get disappointed by how much milk I get out with this. However it could also be that I have more of an established supply now, but don't remeber having this much lasting success with any other of the 4 pumps I have tried.

Cons:
(I'm just nitpicking here, because there aren't any big cons)
- The tubes are made of this odd rubber that gets a lot of dirt and fuz stuck to it
- The power cord gets wrinkled quickly
- Parts with bottle are a bit bulky, but then again, this is what makes it easier to wash it, because they are not tiny like the other ones where you have to pick at with special brushes to get clean.

Bottom line. My favorite pump and hands down the best I have used or seen!

review_body:
This thermometer does not measure temperature accurately. I ultimately returned this item.

I tried it on myself and it showed me having a fever in both ears, but at different temperatures. A regular oral thermometer confirmed I did not have a fever. Similar results in my child, a low temperature in one ear, standard temperature in the other. It was consistent at a standard temperature in my husband, perhaps you need to have huge ear canals to get accurate results. I do not trust this to give me an accurate reading for my child (at just over 7 months, it fit fine in her ear).

Pros:
Gives quick readings
Compact and fits nicely in the carrying case and in diaper bag

Cons:
You have to switch it to Fahrenheit readings every time you use it.
You have to wait quite a bit to take another reading.
Most importantly, the readings are simply not even close to accurate.

product_title: Snoozebaby Sweet Dreaming Comfort Blanket
review_body:
Really just a soft wash cloth, it is made of soft velour and cotton jersey. There are twelve little tags and one white string with a piece of cardboard attached. I assume you are to remove the cardboard and replace with a pacifier. It is most definitely not a blanket. Designed by a parent of a child suffering from KISS Syndrome (Kinematic imbalances due to sub-occipital strain) essentially a subluxation of the cervical vertebrae which cause the brain to misinterpret information. Symptoms include noticeable tilt of the head to one side, scoliosis and poor muscle development. The little tags are supposed to stimulate a child's fine muscle skills.

More of a toy than a blanket, it does machine wash. Be sure to check the tags as they do curl up and some loosen after washing. Although I liked the softness, washability and the fabric, the small size, string loop and flimsy tags give me pause. A larger size would make an ideal blanket but this size is just silly.

review_body:
I have tried the Bugaboo Bee, Jeep All-Terrain, Baby Jogger City Mini, and some other Graco models and this has to be one of my favorite strollers.

This stroller is super sturdy, smooth and easy to steer and push, has a huge canopy, and a decent size basket. I love that there's a small bag for storage that hangs in the back (you can roll it up if not in use) and that the canopy has a nice window to peek in on my baby (something the Bugaboo Bee doesn't have). The straps are sooo easy to use and fit my son very comfortably (which isn't the case with the City Mini). I love the location of the break pedal, it's easy to get to and doesn't take a lot of force to engage. The adjustable handlebar works very well and is convenient for couples who range in size like my husband and I. The snack tray can swing to the side without having to be completely removed if the child wants to enter or exit the stroller (City Mini, Bugaboo Bee all require the full tray to be removed for the child to exit/enter the stroller). Folding and unfolding is quick and easy. Because this stroller has four wheels, it easily folds flat (with strollers like the City Mini with one single front wheel, if the wheel is turned outward, it prevents the stroller from folding completely flat). Overall, I just really like the look and feel of this stroller. It feels solid and looks great. I have this stroller in the orange color and it is easy to spot in a crowd. The material holds up well and wipes down easily for keeping clean.

The only thing I do not like about this stroller is that you have to separately purchase the parent cup holder/console and the baby snack tray/cup holder, but both are made extremely well and are worth the additional cost in my opinion.

product_title: Graco Affix Backless Youth Booster Seat with Latch System
review_headline: Fantastic booster seat at a good price!
review_body:
Our five year old daughter just moved from car seats to a booster seat. I wanted a booster seat that uses the Latch system, as it helps keep the seat from moving around and, well, it just feels safer (even if it isn't). I liked this booster seat so much I bought a second one for my wife's car.

Installation was easy. There are two straps on the left front corner - attach the Latch clips, put a knee in the seat and pull the straps, and you're done. Unlatching is just as easy - lift up on the two release buttons, pull the booster seat away from the car seat and unhook the Latch clips. It's certainly more complicated than just picking up a booster seat when it's just sitting there on the car seat, but it still takes less than a minute to latch and unlatch. To me, it's worth the added complexity.

It also comes with a clip that slides onto the shoulder strap and pulls the strap down, bringing it away from our daughter's neck and more toward her shoulder. We used this for a week or two, then ended up taking it off - she didn't seem to mind one way or the other.

The cup holder is convenient, and our daughter loves using the drawer (although it is kind of hard to open and close). The arm rests are a good height, and she has no complaints with the hardness of the seat.

Great booster seat, especially for the price.

It's a decent purchase.

review_headline: We LOVE this product!!!  Super portable, light weight, and keeps food from falling on the floor.
review_body: This product is really fantastic! This particular seat can be attached to any chair with a back, and adjusts very easily for whatever size the chair is.  The tray is also adjustable, so it can move and grow outward as your baby or toddler gets bigger.  It is super easy to bring along to restaurants or wherever you are going, folding up very nicely, and it is very light weight.  There is a top part which keeps the tray clean before use, and then covers the messy tray until you get to a sink or dishwasher and wash it off (yes, the tray can go in the dishwasher!).  What we especially love is that since the tray can be adjusted to be very close to our daughter's stomach, less food drops outside of the tray - normally in restaurants we would use a high chair that the restaurant provides, and the gap between her belly/the high chair and the table causes lots of food to fall to the floor when she's feeding herself.  Also, since you have your own tray, you know it's clean - unlike a restaurant table surface, should you not have a child who can yet handle a plate, or you don't have a place mat with you.  All in all we think this product is so great, that we plan to buy one for ourselves back home to take with us whenever we go out locally!  You could even just get one of these and have it for everything, not having a separate high chair, and taking it for restaurants and travel.

product_title: Diono Radian R100 Convertible Car Seat Booster, Shadow
review_headline: From a recent purchaser: Positives & Negatives
review_body:
We've only had the carseat about a month, now, so it's likely there'll be more thoughts to come. OK, here are my thoughts:

I bought this model because it's the more affordable Diono model, and I didn't think we needed a carseat that would fit my kid to 120 pounds; local Moms have touted Dionos over all other models for their ease of use; our car is a compact one, and I've read reviews indicating that Dionos are great for compact cars - especially if used in combination with an "angle adjuster" (separate purchase).

We're using the carseat rear-facing at the moment, as I've heard that's the safest position until the child is at least 2 years old, if not 4 years old. We're using the seat in combination with the foam angle adjuster because our car is compact.

It's a good-looking seat.

From reading one particular review, I'd feared that the upholstery material would be not-plushy-enough, and that my child would feel the straps through it, but it's appeared to be sufficiently comfortable.

Although the chest buckle is easier to operate than the Graco chest buckles, it's a little more challenging than I'd figured it would be, having tested it at a local store. That's a little disappointing. I'm hoping it gets easier to buckle as my child gets bigger, giving my hands more room in which to work.

The shoulder harness pads (although gorgeously soft / velveteen-y) make buckling the groin buckle more challenging than I'd like. I'm hoping this issue will clear up as my little one grows taller, providing more spatial separation between the pads and the buckle.

My biggest issue with this carseat is: I'm disappointed that when my child falls asleep, his head hangs to the side at what would appear to be an uncomfortable angle. I'm considering rigging some kind of additional pillows for head support. When I see his head hanging to the side, I wished I'd spent more money and bought the model with the head-rest-pillows.

My child likes to hang a leg over the side of the seat, since the armrests are so low. I wonder if this is OK, safetywise?

All in all, I'm feeling more positive about my son being in this carseat than in his infant carseat, which he just outgrew. (He seems far more comfortable and better-humored, now.)

I feel good that I bought a highly safety-rated seat.ad-rest-pillows.

product_title: Keekaroo Height Right High Chair with Tray
review_body:
I love the idea of a "grow with me" chair but I couldn't bring myself to spend the big bucks for the stokke. this chair is pretty and seems sturdy. They must have updated design because a plastic tray topper now comes to fit over top of the wood so you can choose to use wood or plastic tray.

Every time I undo it I feel like I'm going to break it.Also the seat height is a little weird. The tray is right on top of baby's legs whereas I feel it would be more comfortable if it were at her belly button or mid chest height. While putting this together, I noticed the allen wrench doesn't quite fit the screws. It took me almost an hour to put this together because I had to fight with the wrench. in my situation, we have a table that has a ledge on the side. This chair has a plastic crotch piece that you "must use" when using the tray. Unfortunately, the crotch piece does not let me scoot the chair all the way under the table. My baby ends up with her knees about 1 inch from the table edge thus making her lean over to reach the table top. (theoretically I could lower the seat to scoot her closer but then she would be too low and her chin would be at the table top).

my little is six month old and sitting on her own. No need for the infant insert. I'm not even sure there would be room for it even if you wanted it.

after some trial and error, I'm using this with the seat in the lowest position, without the crotch piece but still using the tray. There needs to be a third seat position between the two that exist now.

for almost $200, I'm disappointed in this purchase.

product_title: Pack N Play - Playpen Netting
review_headline: Decent net but had to cut opening to get on Pack n Play
review_body:
The net does what it is supposed to do. It is being used on a Gracco Travel Pack n Play. I live in a malaria/ dengue fever zone so having the mosquito net is an absolute requirement.

The good: it covers the entire Pack n Play down the sides, which is a necessity if the net is going to be functional.

The bad: I had to make a couple cuts in the stretchy opening in order to actually get it around the Pack n Play. It still works just fine, but I find it annoying to have to purposely damage things like this. This is a basic design flaw as it would not have been difficult to make the stretchy part big enough to properly fit over the top of the Pack n Play.

That said, this one is significantly better than the net we were given at first which only covered the top of the Pack n Play, as mosquitos could just enter the sides through the mesh.

Overall, this is an ok net and I am still using it, though it could be made significantly better with a minor change in design.

Better side impact protection
Easy installation
Sturdy design
Reclines
Latches and tether strap
Goes from harness to Booster
No re-threading straps
More padding so the seat seems more comfortable
Child can sleep in it more comfortably

Forward facing only

product_title: FridaBaby NoseFrida The SnotSucker Nasal Aspirator
review_headline: Best invention ever- use with saline when you can!
review_body:
Purchase 2 or 3! As other reviews have stated, this is simply the best product ever for a stuffy baby. It's good to have a spare, because we are always losing one part or another, and then scrambling when baby gets a cold!

I find it's best to use Little Remedies saline drops first. I put the bottle in lukewarm water for a few seconds so it doesn't shock the baby. I use the Snotsucker in a circular motion and it's fabulous.

It really isn't gross at all. In a pinch I've used it without the filters, and it hasn't come close to getting near the danger zone!

Needless to say, this is far more effective than traditional nasal aspirators. It's also safer because there is no chance of jamming baby in the nostril. The tube can only go so far, and the wide opening means you can get more out in one shot.

Baby hates it, but it's over in about 10 seconds, versus much longer torture with the pointy blue bulb.

I also like that you can actually see what's coming out, and know if you're being effective.

If you have the time, use it in a steamy bathroom. On bad nights, I would run the shower hot as can be, and add a drop or two of eucalyptus to a bowl. We would just sit for a few minutes, put in a few drops of warm saline, and use the Snotsucker. Presto!!!!

product_title: Seven Slings Baby Infant Carrier Sling Size 4
review_headline: Love these slings, especially compared to Baby Bjorne
review_body:
I'm always surprised by all the awful reviews on forums for this sling. It is what it is, a very inexpensive, yet attractive way to carry your baby. I have three kids and over the years 3 of these slings in size 2, 3, and 5 and always use the free coupon codes, pay $11 in shipping and UNCHECK the box for insurance to change sizes. I hated my Baby Bjorne when compared to the seven Sling. I use all three different sizes, I keep the bigger two in the car.

The smallest (I measured when I was just 3 months pregnant) I use to front carry my newborn around the house, I use one hand to hold the head, but it takes the weight off my hands and wrists and gives me a free hand. My larger two she sits in the pouch, lays in it or sits on my hip with my assist. I used for my toddler till he always wanted to walk.

I have used these daily, no tears, breakage or issues with three kids.

Pros: Easy, fast, light weight in hot Texas weather, great patterns, Takes up hardly any room in a bag, no sagging after years of use, infants to toddlers

Cons:
Tricky sizing, Not resizable, no back carry, weight is only on one shoulder

Key: Got to get the size right. Remember you will not be as thin right after the baby is born and you will probably be rocking some killer boobs far larger than you are used to. At 3-6 months, measure minimum size and order two sizes higher.

product_title: The Bugaboo Cameleon3 Stroller in Aluminum
review_body:
I love this stroller. I previously had the original cameleon and got the cameleon3 for my new baby. The improvements are great. First of all, it is the most stylish and sleek looking stroller out there. The bassinet is very big, much bigger than other strollers bassinet options. You can easily fit a baby in there thru 6 months old. It is so comfy that my baby sleeps better in the bugaboo bassinet than anywhere else. The basket is a nice size, but it is difficult to get to it when using the bassinet option. It is much easier to use when you are using the seat. The seat reverses as does the handlebar, so you can always choose to have your baby facing you or the world. If you reverse the handlebar note that the big non swivel wheels will be in the front, making it slightly harder to push. I have done this on occasion when the baby was getting fussy while we were already out and about. The best improvement is the belly bar. On the original stroller you had to take the whole bar on and off and it was pretty difficult to do. On the new stroller you can easily take off one side and swivel it to get the baby on and off. The extended sun canopy was also a big improvement, although I did not buy the tailored fabric set at all, I bought the fully extendable breezy sun canopy and borrowed a bassinet apron from a friend (since you only use the bassinet for about 6 months and her child is older already). Also, bugaboo strollers have fantastic resale value so when you are done with yours you can usually sell it on craigslist or eBay for a good price.
I checked out the uppababy vista, and while it seemed to have many of the same features as the bugaboo, it just felt like such a knockoff. It is more affordable and also a good stroller, but the bugaboo is the original and the best!
I don't take mine in the car much, but my neighbor takes hers all the time and has no problem folding and unfolding it. It folds pretty compactly because it is in two separate pieces. On the rare occasions that I do take the stroller in my car it fits into the trunk of my minivan without folding!

review_headline: Best portable light travel crib available
review_body:
Light and easy to transport and setup. A comfortable but sturdy hypoallergenic foam mattress ships with the crib and it being on the floor you know your child is safe. This has traveled with us easily and brought to grandma's and to the beach.

I did a lot of research and looked at all the pros and cons of portable cribs like the 4MOMs (not portable...too heavy). The closest competitor being Lotus Travel Crib.

In the end this beat out the Lotus for me because though the side zip entrance is nice......as a crib having see through mesh from the top to the bottom does not work for my child. My son has bumpers along his crib sides which prevent him from seeing us and enables him to goto sleep with less distraction. The Baby Bjorn Travel crib has a solid non-see-through material through the bottom half of the crib allowing for this privacy. Also, The Baby Bjorn's mattress is also thicker and more comfy than the Lotus.

For the price, this is the best portable Travel Crib available. There are sheets available for sale to fit the mattress exactly if needed.

If you have a bad back and don't want to lean in to put your baby down or want to use it as more than just a crib or as a playpen, or don't mind a harder mattress like the 4Moms (which is similar) the Lotus may be the better option.

product_title: Yummi Pouch Reusable Food Pouches (Set of 6)
review_headline: Great reusable pouch for on-the-go feedings
review_body: These pouches work pretty great. I've used them a few times and so far they're holding up very nicely. We store pureed veggies and fruits in the freezer as a quick/convenient on-the-go food option. They thaw easily by just moving them to the refrigerator overnight or submerging in warm water if needed for more immediate consumption. I chose these because they have the seal across the top and are able to stand on their own. I did see others that had the seal on the bottom and couldn't stand alone. Having the spout on the side hasn't really been a big issue, although my 9 month old doesn't quite know how to squeeze the last little bit of food out. I'm not sure he'd be able to do that if the spout was on top though. A note of caution (as I saw in another review) the caps do come completely off and can get lost. I mostly use the caps for long term storage and opted to purchase the[[ASIN:B00ERZ4AUA ChooMee Sip'n Soft Top - Orange and Aqua - One Size]] which can attach to the pouch and provides a softer mouthpiece for my baby. If you baby doesn't quite know how to use get the food out from the spout you can always use a feeding spoon which has worked out well for us as well.    Filling the pouches is pretty easy with the wide opening on top, just make sure the spout is covered so nothing comes pouring out. There is a fill line indicator that you want to make sure to stay under to avoid spills. Be careful if you have very watery/runny food in the pouch as it can come gushing out especially if baby isn't quite used to holding the pouches. The only thing I've noticed when filling them is some food gets stuck in the seams of the zipper seal which is a little annoying, but I recently purchased the [[ASIN:B00AYWXKZ6 Baby Food Pouch Fill Station - Fill and Squeeze Starter Pack with 5 Pouches - Reuse or Make Your Own Pouches]] to see if I can fill these from the spout itself. I'll update my review after I use that station with these pouches. Also, I did notice that the carrots Istored left an orange stain that I cannot remove even after multiple cleanings, but I think this would have been the case with any plastic pouch.    Cleaning is a breeze again due to the wide opening. I tend to wash these by hand with a bottle brush to get all the gunk out. So far I haven't had any problems getting the food cleaned out from the zipper seam, though I haven't been using them for more than a few weeks. I did see another reviewer posted a picture of mold in the zipper, so if this becomes a problem I will need to update my review. So far so good though.    All in all, I'm very happy with these pouches and would recommend them.

product_title: Vera Bradley Womens Make a Change Baby Bag
review_headline: Only a couple of things I would change about the bag
review_body:
I received this diaper bag as a baby shower gift and loved it! After using it for a little over a month here's what I think about the bag so far:

Pros:
-I loved being able to have a diaper bag with such a cute design! I don't have the "Priscilla Pink" (mine is in "Heather"), but love having a diaper bag that everyone else had.
-The changing pad that comes with the bag is the perfect size and helps in situations when there's no liners to lay down or no changing table at all!

Cons:
-Compared to another diaper bag I have, it doesn't have as much room. I can comfortably fit about 4 outfits, 2 bibs, 2 burp clothes, socks, wipes, 4-6 diapers, 2 bottles, a formula container, gas drops, and some random things that I may need on a certain day (like saline spray, a nose bulb, etc.). Don't get me wrong, it by no means is "tiny", but if your looking to pack for a day rather than a couple of hours, I'd consider using a larger bag.
-The magnetic tab that holds the changing pad compartment together comes off-centered. I'm not sure if that's just from using the bag over time or if it came like that and I just didn't notice at first. It doesn't get in the way of anything but looks weird, so it may bother you if you're a picky person.

Overall I love the bag, there's just a few things I didn't like about the bag and I would definitely recommend it to someone else!

product_title: Medela Harmony Manual Breast Pump
review_headline: Not efficent and can't be cleaned properly
review_body:
I got this pump for my first child. I was going to be a stay-at-home mom, so I figured I would only need something simple for pumping the occasional bottle. However, I had a really hard time actually expressing any milk. Even with the "expression" feature, it would still take several minutes to actually achieve let-down. I could only get an ounce or two from each side at a time, so it would take at least 3 pumping sessions to gain enough milk for one feeding. Hardly efficient.
I also had a lot of trouble actually cleaning out the pump. I always hand-washed it, since we don't have a dishwasher. However, what you can't tell in the picture is that there is this tiny little tube that runs from the flange down towards the bottle. It is impossible to get this clean, since there is no way to get at it. Even with the pump all the way taken apart, you just can't get to it. I would try running lots of hot water through the pump, but it still developed a white build-up despite my best efforts.

product_title: Charlie Banana 2-in-1 6-Piece Reusable Diapers
review_body:
I bought these diapers from Target (on sale, cheaper than Amazon) about a month ago. Overall, I like them.

The inserts are microfiber which I don't care for. They are bulky, hard to get clean in my HE front loader, and worst of all is the compression leaking! Even if the diaper isn't that wet, it'll still wet my kid's bottom when he sits and give him a rash. One insert seam started coming unraveled after just a few washings, but no biggie as I don't use them much. I mostly stuff the diapers with natural fiber inserts (the hemp inserts that come with Thirsties pocket diapers are a good fit).

What I like about the diapers: the rise more adjustable than with snap rise adjustments, creating a nice snug fit that doesn't leave red marks on my toddler. The interior of the shells is super soft. I like that the pocket opening is in the front, even though it can be harder to stuff that way, as it keeps my hands farther away from the poop when removing the inserts (and my kid is a frequent pooper). The snaps are fine - should last a long time, although of course harder to snap onto an uncooperative toddler than aplix would be.

I read the reviews that warned of the elastic slipping and resizing the diapers during wear, but mine have the triple bar buckle which seems to fix the problem. I also read the reviews that warned of said brastrap buckle rusting and breaking the leg elastic, that is tricky to deal with since diapers spend so much time with wetness. I use a dry pail system, and plan to wash and dry the diapers promptly. I hope that will do the trick.
