product_title: Snuza Hero Baby Movement Monitor
review_body:
We bought the Hero before our daughter was born and have used it every night (she is now five months old). This is one of our favorite baby items. It is reliable, easy to use, portable, works very well, and we haven't had any trouble with false alarms (2 in 5 months, only because she was wiggling a LOT and it slipped off). We clip it on both disposable and cloth diapers and it works easily on both. It is still running on its original battery. The sensitivity is very well calibrated: we tested it by setting it on our bed while we moved around, to make sure it wasn't picking up our movements when she was in bed with us, and the alarm went off as it should.

Bottom line: SIDS is very rare, so hopefully this alarm wont ever be necessary. But the urge to keep your newborn alive is so instinctual, most parents still worry about it and find themselves checking frequently to make sure their baby is still breathing, especially at first. If your baby does stop breathing and the Hero alerts you, it is worth every penny, of course. But much more likely, it will just give you the peace of mind to sleep soundly at night, which is also worth every penny. Highly recommended.

It has a stretchable quality to it - so it does allow some room for arms/legs movements after swaddling, but that also makes it easy for the little ones to break free from the swaddle.  I generally use it as sheet for my son to sleep on and I swear he sleeps better on them (guess he likes it's soft feel).

product_title: Nursery Fresh Refill for Diaper Genie
review_body:
I've bought several dozen items off of Amazon and hardly ever write reviews. I'd been using the Playtex real brand for months and saw that these generic bags were SLIGHTLY cheaper and gave me a few more bags. The reviews were good enough so I figured, sure, why not. Why not is because these bags are HORRIBLE. Instead of writing the little annoying thing about them (like there's no indicator to let you know it's running out, but again, that's a small issue not a deal breaker) I'll just say my one major gripe that will ensure I will never buy these bags again:

They are wasteful. What I mean is that everytime you put a diaper in the genie these bags will pull several inches extra for no reason. You won't know this till the genie is full and have to go dump it. At that point you will open the genie, attempt to trim the bag like you always have and then realize you now have about an entire new lengths worth of wasted bag. You can't stick it back inside the casing so it's forever wasted. I thought maybe only my first canister was doing this so I waited til it ran out (which wasn't long at all) and continued using regularly with the second canister and sure enough, same deal.

I wish I would have read a review like this about this product and I sure wouldn't have bought it.

product_title: Baby Pocket Cloth Diapers Reusable with Adjustable Snaps, 6 pcs + 6 Inserts combined
review_body:
The prints on this product are very cute, and the laminate on the inside is very sturdy which is good for holding up overtime. However the elastic for the legs and the fabric around it don't sit right on baby's skin, leaving irritated redness. The elastic in the waistband seems cheap and dosnt give much. The inserts where beyond cheap and I tossed them out (I have far better ones in my stash). Using the better inserts they hold the mess in nicely and can be worn for 2 hours easy. I just cant use them one after the next, I have to rotate using Alva diapers with Charlie Bananas because if I use 2 Alva diapers in a row my baby's skin gets terribly red where the elastic on the legs sits. She's two so she can tell me, it's uncomfortable for her.

These are nice if your in need of a few extra diapers to round out your stash, but I would not recommend building your stash out of these diapers. There are far higher quality cloth diapers available. Do your research, try different brands out, buy a stash once you pick your favorite.

review_body: Let me just say that we love these cups, BUT we are a family of boys! We don't need or want the pink cups! There should be an option to pick boy colors or girl colors. If we could have just picked all boy colors, I would have given them 5 stars...

product_title: Infantino Sash Mei Tai Carrier, Black/Gray
review_body:
I have 3 kids and have used other carriers in the past and I have to say that I prefer this one by far!!!
For starters, I love the design. I think its very chic looking and a different look from your usual carriers that are the generic black on black with no design element to them at all. When I first looked into this type of carrier I was a little worried about how safe my baby would be in it as there are no belts or buckles to it all. Let me tell you I have had no problems with that at all. If you follow the insructions, which are very simple and straightforward you'll love this carrier as well. Comparing this product with other carriers I do think that it takes off pressure from my lower back that I would feel with others. The reason that I gave four stars instead of 5 is because The sashes themselves are very long. I'm a pretty short petite woman 5'2 and for me as I'm bundling up my little one the sashes touch the floor and can get dirty. But its a breeze to just wipe it down with a wipey or something of the sort. By the way the part that touches the floor never touches the baby, its what ties behind the baby's back. I just dont like to see it touching the floor thats just me... lol All in all I would def by this again!

product_title: OXO Tot Sprout Chair Replacement Cushion Set
review_headline: Nice cushy material with lots of potential applications.
review_body: Fairly cushy material. Easy to cut to size so that it fits ANY high chair. Comes with adhesive backed Velcro like strips so it's a relatively seamless application. Just plan your cuts appropriately. The high chair we got from our registry had very little actual padding. This stuff fixed that issue pretty nicely.

product_title: FridaBaby NoseFrida The SnotSucker Nasal Aspirator
review_body:
I, like many, was very squeamish at the thought of this when I first heard about it. But it was so strongly recommended to me that I had to try it. I bought it before I even had my baby so that it was on hand when he got his first cold...and I was SO glad! I was too scared to use it at first and tried the old blue syringe that most people have, but it did such a horrible job I resorted to the Nosefrida within minutes.

Now I use this on my baby at least once a week, as he seems to be congested on a fairly regular basis. He doesn't like it, but it goes quickly and he is so much happier once I've finished that it's worth it to me.

Save yourself a lot of misery and invest in one of these BEFORE your baby gets a cold. You'll thank me at 2 a.m., I'm sure of it.

product_title: Blackburn Model A Trailer
review_body:
Product was here in less than estimated by the website, installation was very easy and the attachment to the bicycle works with all bicycles because it doesn't attach to the frame. My daughter loves it and wants me to take her to school in it all the time. Here in Houston it starts to be a bit too hot for it though but come fall we will definitely use it more. When pulling I need to remind myself that I have a trailer behind so easy it is on the rider with the large wheels with air tires.

Love it and suggest anybody to buy this product who is looking to buy one.

product_title: Gummi Crib Rail
review_body: My toddlers were able to peel this right off their crib. I liked to soft texture but it was too easy to peel off the crib's rail.

product_title: Safety 1st Heavenly Dreams Stars a Plenty Baby Mattress
review_headline: Not as firm as I'd like
review_body:
This is a nice quality low end mattress. We bought our crib used and it came with a super firm expensive mattress, but after reading the risks of using a used crib mattress I got the fever to buy a new one. I didn't have much money to spend, so I was glad when I found this one.

Comparing it with my old one it is much less firm than the one we threw away. But I do feel better about it being new (as the child who used the old one was very sick for a time, which kept nagging at me.) We tested it with a 20lb cat and while it didn't sag much at all, it was less firm than the old one. To the touch (while pushing on it) it does give a little which worried me.

Overall I think it'll be fine for a newborn and I'm not as worried about smothering on it after using the "cat test." Perhaps it not being as firm will be more comfortable for the baby as well. I am a first time mom, so not sure what to expect. I think this was a good purchase overall and I enjoy that the mattress is super light so it makes changing the sheets quick and easy.

review_body: We bought two of these gates based on reviews.  We had them professionally installed.  After we spent $200 on the install (we have a brick wall...), we discovered that one of the gates latches improperly.  One gate is easily opened (for a parent) with one hand.  The other is a pain in the rear and I have to fight with it every single time.  The latch is two pieces that you push and then lift.  One of the latch pieces sticks and I have to get it just right to get the door to lift.

product_title: Trend Lab Cotton CribWrap Wide Rail Cover for Crib Front or Back
review_body: I really like this crib cover. It is so soft my daughter lays her head on it like a pillow. It never comes off and prevents her from chewing on the crib. We have a white crib and it is hardly noticeable on it.

review_body: I ordered a small pillow that I could throw into the wash machine - and of course needed a pillowcase for it.  This one fit the bill perfectly and we love to use it.

review_body: I bought this chair for my second child, before this one we had the huge plastic high chair! I hates that one, first it was huge, second it wasn't blending with the house, I was completely irritated because I was seeing white huge plastic thing with my beautiful furniture. I decided to get the wood one, I picked Abiie because it grows with your child. Assembly is super easy, removable tray makes cleaning easy! Also I do take off the tray part and push the chair closer to the table, she feels like she is sitting with us but has her own chair. product_title: Foscam FBM3501 Wireless Digital Video Baby Monitor
review_body:
I did quite a bit of research on video monitors and the most expensive ones had some very poor ratings. I wanted something that I can watch my son with, period. I also did not want to spend more than a $150.00 if at all possible. I found the Foscam on Amazon and the reviews were pretty good along with some cons.
Pros:
Clear day & night video
Easy to work
Love the temperature feature

Cons:
Battery charge does not last, but I just plug it in, not a big deal for me
I wish the volume was a bit higher

All in all, I have recommended this to several women who are looking for a monitor without the high price and all sorts of bells and whistles.

review_body: I bought this for my 6 month old. It's cute and good quality. Easy to care for. Glad I found it!

product_title: BOB Revolution SE Duallie Stroller
review_body:
So I have to admit that I had stroller envy before biting the bullet and buying this. I would stare longingly at other moms at the mall and zoo who had this beast of a stroller, usually wiping some drool off my chin. I finally talked my husband into buying this (sidenote: it cost more than his junker commuter car, so we joke about that) for mother's day/a birthday gift. Seriously I wish I could ride in it, but I don't think my 3.5 year old would do a great job steering.
When I received it, the foam padding on the bar under the brake was torn but I don't even care. It isn't a big tear, and I'm sure it would happen eventually anyway. The right back tire also always goes flat. I am bringing the tires into Les Schuab to have them filled with some sort of goo foam so they don't go flat....ever. Or at least that is the claim!
We have only used this for walks and and to the zoo, so I have no experience bringing it into close quarter spaces.
I do wish it came with the handlebar console, but whatevs, whats $20something more when you're already spending the money to buy this.

product_title: LorexBaby LBN511 Little Link HD WI-FI Video Baby Monitor (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Not perfect, but it works well for our purpose
review_body:
I like the idea of the wifi feature of this monitor, and I hope it's safe and secure. I didn't experience any problems installing this. My phone is new enough that it was compatible, but I would suggest that everyone check compatibility before investing in this monitor.

The images are fairly clear on SD mode. HD was too slow, but isn't really necessary for us. The color is decent as long as the room is well lit. The night vision works well, better than I expected. I was able to capture still images, which was nice. I haven't tried to record videos, probably because all I see are two little dogs sleeping all day. I do seem to lose contact every now and then, but it works well most of the time.

The unit is lightweight and small. The nightlight is a nice touch and puts out just the right amount of light. It's easy to use, and I like the way it looks. Overall, I think this is a good monitor with nice features.

product_title: Orbelle 3-6T Toddler Bed
review_body: Bed is exactly like shown in the picture.  Assembly was pretty straightforward. Instructions for the assembly were actually very good, considering sometimes products like this that are made over seas have instructions that are in Chinese-English, or whatever. These were understandable and with good illustrations.  Took me about 30 minutes to assemble after I inventoried all the parts.  Be sure to check the hardware against the parts list before you start. Some reviewers have complained because they did not have all the hardware. I would speculate that this is because they happened to get a kit that had been returned by someone else, and that person lost some of the hardware before returning it. If some hardware is missing, call the 800 number and they should send you a new bag of hardware. Picture shows a mattress, but it is not included in the kit.But any standard mattress will fit. Some reviewers have complained that it looks "cheap".  Well, yes, it is inexpensive, but if you want to pay more, go ahead and go to a furniture store and spend $300-$400.  It won't be much better.

product_title: Munchkin Twisty Figure 8 Teether
review_body:
This was a gift for my friend's teething baby and he loves it! He is a baby who loves bright colors and shies away from the dark "natural" and "organic" colors, so I knew that this would be the perfect teether for him. He loves twisting away at it and seems to use it more of just as a general toy instead of a teether, but there is still no denying that it finds its way into his mouth quite often.

This toy has definitely withstood the test of time and use now and I can attest to the fact that it is very sturdy! No worries at all about the toy breaking in a baby's mouth. Mom and baby are very happy with this little teether!

And I will add as a side note that this little toy can be quite fun for a sleep deprived adult as well! :P

product_title: My Brest Friend Inflatable Travel Nursing Pillow in Green Paisley
review_body: I was looking for some kind of pillow to use while out and about with my son. I really need something to hold my son when I am feeding him and this is perfect. Its an inflatable cushion and its quick and easy to inflate. The valve has a back flow stopper so you aren't constantly worried that the air will leak out while you are taking another breath. When its time to deflate you just pop the valve out and it deflates quickly. The cover is thin but it doesn't bother me since I only use it when I am out of the house. I read on one of the reviews to place the inflatable part into the cushion first and then blow it up to make it easier to get the cushion on and that really helps. I just leave it in the cover unless I am cleaning it.

product_title: Evenflo ExerSaucer Jump and Learn Jumper
review_body:
If your kid is walking, this is not the toy for you. However, if you want to give your kid some fun and exercise, I definitely recommend this guy. It's actually quite large and has a lot of different parts that your kid may find fun including the 3 rubbery figures that hang down as well as the electronic parts closer to their hands that make noise.

The real winning feature of this jumper is not the toys however, it is what the kids stand on. Instead of jumping on the ground as most cheap jumpers do, there is a great trampoline like rubber bouncer that really helps the kid to get more exercise and bounce higher. There's also something to be said for softer landing as well.

Even though was a little pricey and we only got about a year's use out of it, this is a very high-quality item and I would recommend to others even for a short time of use.

product_title: BABYBJORN Smart Potty
review_body: We bought this for our 9-month-old daughter to use and she's now 11 months old and has only had about one #2 in her diaper per month since we got it. She LOVES using this potty. I'm a SAHM who cloth-diapers and does EC and this potty is a fantastic tool that get used nearly daily. I predict she'll be fully potty-trained by 18 months, thanks largely to this cute little potty. She's about halfway potty trained now because of it - I'm such a proud mama!

product_title: Born Free Soft Clean Bibs, Medallion, 3-Pack
review_body: I love these, came from the aden and anis bibs to this because it was a better value with the extra microfiber layer, and it was proven a good buy.  I love how absorbant they are because my LO is teething and constantly drooling.  They dry quick, and stay soft.  So I can even rinse them out each use, hang to dry and its good to go again.

product_title: Ameda Flexshield Aereola Stimulator - 2 Pk
review_headline: Good way to reduce flange size
review_body:
I purchased these because I needed to reduce the flange size for my pump. I thought I would try these rather than the flange reducers thinking if it made pumping more efficient, then even better. I like these, they do the job well, and I certainly get more milk and get it quicker using these than I did using the bare flange, but I don't know if that should be attributed to the flexsheild itself or just the better fit. Either way I am happy! My only complaint is that the end of the part as it fits into the flange has 3 holes for the milk to drip out. I'm not sure why they needed to do that rather than leaving it completely open, but it does impede the milk dripping into the bottle a little bit. When I am finished pumping I have to pull these out and shake them off to get the last few drops of milk into the bottle.

I didn't ever have any issues with reduced suction or leaking with these, although some other people have complained about that. For me, they work great.

product_title: Sassy Rattlin Ring, Blue /Black
review_headline: I Like But Baby Less Than Thrilled
review_body:
I like this rattle. Makes sounds and is bright, textured, and has a fun shape. Wished my baby liked it too. She might just not like rattles. All babies are different. She will hold it and shake it for a couple of seconds but mainly she just throws it on the floor whenever I hand it to her. On that note, it is easy to wash.

Good thing it was not expensive!

product_title: Infant Optics DXR-5 Portable Video Baby Monitor
review_headline: Great product; even better customer service!
review_body:
The Baby Bargains book recommended this monitor, and sure enough it is the perfect combo of easy-to-use with the necessary bells and whistles. It's cute, lightweight, and and both the screen and audio are very clear.

After several months of use, my monitor screen began to fail, unfortunately. From the moment I contacted Infant Optics' customer service department (on a Sunday, no less), they were profusely apologetic and acted swiftly to provide a replacement unit. Through every step of the process, their team was attentive and helpful... I only wish they had more products for me to purchase!

product_title: OsoCozy Unbleached Prefold Cloth Diapers - 6 Pack
review_headline: Best Prefolds out there for the price
review_body:
I love these prefolds and they are definitely worth the price compared to other prefold brands out there. They are thick, very absorbent, and last! We're expecting baby number two and all of the OsoCozy size 1 diapers we bought for our first baby have lasted, and they look and feel nearly new (almost no stains, and no tearing or worn spots). All of the other brands we tried cycled to the rag pile very quickly - well before our daughter was out growing them. We had no hesitation about buying OsoCozy size 2 when she outgrew the size 1 and we'll be restocking for the coming baby with only OsoCozy.

(When washing I put them through a rinse cycle first and then use Country Save detergent in a heavy soil, or sanitizing cycle. Diapers get washed 2-3 times a week.)

product_title: Levana Jena Digital Baby Video Monitor with 8 Hour Rechargeable Battery and Talk to Baby Intercom
review_body: This monitor is awesome.  The picture is clear and the sound is great.  I love that I can see my baby while he's sleeping, without having to go in to check on him.  I would recommend this to other people.

product_title: Ingenuity Moonlight Rocking Sleeper
review_headline: Comfy but lacks a few things.
review_body: The rocker is easy to assemble but if you plan on taking it down you will have to push in the buttons and take it apart each time.  No easy fold which isn't to bad because sometimes the button folds seem a little dangerous and unsafe.  The little mobile with the two stuffed animals doesn't turn on its own, but rather plays a few soft tunes.  It comes equipped with soft music and two nature sounds to soothe the baby.  The inside of the rocker is soft and comfy and comes with some straps to strap the baby into the rocker.  Comes with a vibrator to gently vibrate the baby which will help sooth the little tike.  Definitely not for a child that can reach up and grab, because the mobile snaps onto the side. If it can reach the mobile it will most certainly pull it down.  This is certainly not a bad rocker, it has a gentle rock, not a fast or deep rock, just a gentle rock that you could lay a hand on and move it softly.  Four stars for the mobile and how it clips onto the side.  If I wasn't near the rocker I probably would leave the mobile off of it.  Box says infant till five months, but with the safety of  your child you should judge on how big it gets before you decide it has grown out of this rocker.

product_title: Dreambaby Clip On Sun Shade with UV Indicator
review_headline: Does it's job buuuuut only if there's no breeze
review_body: Saw a friend with one of these and ordered it for our infant daughter.  It worked fine IF the wind wasn't blowing.  We live near the coast where it tends to be breeze so either this was blowing up/to the side or completely off.  Good idea but it just didn't work for us.

product_title: KidCo Bath Safety Rail - White
review_body: I didn't work on our bathtub! I do have it secured on the inside but the auction keeps coming loose.

product_title: Britax EZ-Buckle Belly Pad
review_body: I was looking for some padding to add to the bottom strap of a non-Britax lightweight stroller. I was concerned about the pressure the narrow strap was putting on my child's bottom area and wanted some padding to distribute the pressure better. The strap slips through a wide loop on the pad and it works like I needed it to. Because it slides on so easily (but not loose), I will have to be careful it doesn't slide off when I am unaware.

Can barely fit enough diapers in it let alone a change of cloths and bottles that would be needed for an all day outing.

review_body:
Maybe it is the size or firmness, but I was not happy with this purchase. I am about 5'6" and this pillow does not fit comfortably in any position for me. I am a little over 7 months pregnant and the firmness of the pillow does not allow for my belly to rest comfortable on it or against it. I find myself rolling over a lot at night and this pillow does not allow for easy movement either.
I have gone back to using a head pillow between my legs and a wedge for my belly. So far this combination has been the move comfortabel and manageable.

review_body: They get the job done, but don't expect them to continue to look good after a wash (if that's something you care about).

review_body: Got this when my son was 6 weeks and he was able to hold on to it bc he likes to hold onto something while he sleeps. I was really getting aggravated when he would wake up wanting his paci and it would be dark so i couldn't find it and it was constantly falling out of his mouth. with this if i swaddle him he can't push it away from his mouth. and he was already sucking soothies so whoever came up with this idea is genius. product_title: Tiny Love Musical Nature Stroll Toy Bar
review_body: My little ones seem to despise the carseat ride in the car but this purchase is a lifesaver. Honestly, i was so close to turning my little one around once he hit 20lbs but not i can prolong it a bit after this purhase.

product_title: Bummis Reusable Fleece Liners
review_headline: you can just cut up some fleece yourself
review_body:
It's so easy. Just take some old fleece clothes, or a length of fleece from a fabric store, and cut it into the size that you want. You don't have to sew the edges because fleece doesn't fray. Pretty much any fleece will do, but I would try for polar fleece or microfleece. (Don't confuse microfleece with microfiber, which can't go against baby's skin.)

That being said, I did try these and they are great. If you have an aversion to even the most basic DIY project (no judgment, I am the same way!), they are a good size and a good price.

product_title: Clevamama Clevafoam Baby Pillow
review_body: My son loves loves loves this pillow!! I had to buy two more for back up. Its lightweight and comfortable.  Very soft! Great product!

product_title: Bamboobies Ultra Soft and Thin Washable Nursing Pads, Wrinkle Free, Reusable
review_body: I love Bamboobies! Wish I had them with my 1st son but I am glad I have been able to use them with my second then third son! These are so soft and comfortable. I haven't tried the other sizes, but I'm sure they are great as well :)

I am not sure what size a book has to be for you to actually squeeze in 85 books in this thing but if you have a normal collection of books where some are thin and some are a little thicker, you come nowhere near that number.  For me it was around 40 books.  I wanted something like this so it'd be easier for my kids to pick the book they wanted as the book covers are facing them as opposed to a regular bookshelf, but the lack of space has been quite disappointing.

product_title: Nuby 2-Pack Two-Handle No-Spill Super Spout Grip N' Sip Cup, 8 Ounce, Colors May Vary
review_body: These little cups don't leak as some of the other reviews have said. Maybe my little guy isn't as rough as some children with his sippy cups. I bought these because we were having latch problems when we nursed, and I had heard that sippies with straws might be the culprit. These spouts look more "natural" and I thought that it might help him latch better. I think it helped! We take both these sippies with us because he likes to have one in each hand. :)

review_body:

product_title: Clips N Grips Toddler Baby Kid Adjustable Elastic Suspenders
review_body: I was looking for something good for my 13 months daugther. This is what I wanted. It works beautiful but a little bit a big for 13 months baby.

product_title: Spasilk Washcloth, 10 Count
review_body: I have bought Spasilk products before and this are always soft. this was a wonderful value also when you get 10 super soft wash cloths for the price others charge for 5-6. You can't go wrong with this purchase. Extra wash cloths are great for little faces instead of paper towels or wipes that are not designed for the face.

product_title: Dr. Brown's 2 Pack Natural Flow Preemie Standard Nipple
review_headline: Slowest Flow - BEST one so far, buy it!
review_body:
Yep - this is the one for the slowest flow - thus far! We wanted a "flow" that would simulate the breast as close as possible. It takes about 15-20 minutes to drink down 2-4 ounces. The biggest issue with breast feeding is not shape or design - it's FLOW! So if you are really going breastfeed but need to use a bottle from time to time - this is the nipple to use!!! No confusion here!

OH - and don't listen to those DAM breastfeeding nazi's at the hospital, if you need to use a bottle and pump, then do it.

We did test several others - breastflow, tippytommy, etc

product_title: Kolcraft Pure Sleep Therapeutic 150 Infant/Toddler Crib Mattress -150 Extra Firm Coils, Hypoallergenic, Durable Waterproof Cover, Crib Fit Tested, 52"x28"
review_body: Well I do love that the outside is made of a waterproof material that is the only reason I gave it 3 stars. The mattress seems cheap and thin. Not impressed.

product_title: UppaBaby 2013 G-Luxe Stroller
review_body:
Ordered this stroller since we already own the VISTA UppaBaby and were very happy with it until we started travelling frequently and needed a lighter and easer stroller. We chose this one since we trusted the brand having had a good experience with the Vista. It's slightly more expensive as far as umbrella strollers go, however, it did come with positive reviews.

Pros:
- it's light
- it reclines
- the seat is softer than most strollers and adjusts to extend for under-calf
- the canopy extends quite far
- fairly easy to fold it
- the basket is large for an umbrella stroller
- it stands on its own (sounds like magic, huh?)
- it cleans the house for you (no, but wouldn't it be great?) ;-)

Cons:
- the canopy tends to pop off when folding and opening the stroller, which can be particularly frustrating while travelling. For that I'd recommend buying a "check at the gate" bag to prevent from losing the canopy and getting the stroller dirty

product_title: Safety 1st Oven Front Lock

product_title: Fuzzibunz Elite Cloth Diapers
review_body:
I am at a total loss that these diapers get favorable reviews on Amazon and many cloth diapering sites. I've been using cloth diapers on our daughter for about 4 months now and have tried several brands and styles including Kawaii, BG, RAR, prefolds with covers, Thirsties, Moraki, etc. I have never, ever had any moisture problems with any brand except FuzziBunz.

I'm a total stickler for my CD wash routine, so I'm positive the problem is not on my end. I would guess 3 out of 4 times these go on my baby, they wick moisture around the legs- enough that when I do a diaper change, the onesie must be changed too. At first, I thought I solved the problem by tucking in the elastic around the legs so no microfiber in showing. This wasn't a great solution, since it made serious red marks around baby's legs, it looked silly, and it didn't really solve the problem.

Then I figured out there was additional wicking happening through the stitching around the legs! Most CDs will use an acrylic type thread when sewing, so when you prep your diapers with one cycle in the dryer on hot, the thread and waterproof PUL material sort of "melt" together, creating a waterproof barrier. I guess FuzziBunz missed the memo about acrylic thread.

So, I used these as part of my rotation for two weeks and almost every time they made it on my girl's butt, it ended in a wet outfit for her and frustration for me. You couldn't pay me to use these diapers.

product_title: Graco SimpleSwitch Highchair and Booster
review_headline: Does the job, but could be better
review_body:
This high chair is just ok. I wish I had been more mindful when purchasing a high chair and spent a little bit more money for a more convenient chair. It was great when my baby was eating purees, but now that she's feeding herself and making a giant mess, I'm finding many more flaws in this chair.

The Pros:
It's very cute and sturdy.
The 5-point harness is great for wiggly babies
It seems to be comfortable for the baby
It's easy to move around on hardwood floors even without wheels
The fabric seat cover is very easy to clean (machine washable)
Easy to assemble/take apart for cleaning

The Cons:
The tray doesn't hook on anything, so you have to put it on the floor (or another large surface) to get the baby out.
The straps are very hard to clean (I wish I had gotten the high chair with the rubber straps that wouldn't get food imbedded in them)
The tray is one big piece of plastic (i.e. it doesn't have a removable top surface part like many others), so to wash the tray in the sink you have to put the whole thing in there, otherwise, drip a sponge or rag to the actual chair to clean
No cup holder or partition on the tray
No wheels for easier movement (though this isn't an issue on hardwood)

All in all, this high chair gets the job done and seems safe and sturdy, however it has no bells or whistles to make clean-up or self-feeding easier or less messy.

product_title: Claessens' Kids KWID Learning Watch
review_headline: Do not buy! Display is hard to see, buttons are confusing, bleh
review_body:
I got two of these, the pink and the blue for my son and daughter after they became enthralled with my Pebble smartwatch. They were a bit young for it, 2 and 3 but the problems aren't even related to that.

The display is strange/terrible b/c it has no back so you can see all the way through to the circuit board (which is not how it looks in the product pictures), which makes it really hard to see the display and almost impossible to see when the backlight LED is on b/c there is nothing to diffuse the light. The contrast of the LCD make things even worse b/c the black of the display isn't very dark.

The setup and use of the watch is very complicated, which I'm guessing is to help keep older kids from messing with the time. It's even more difficult to setup b/c the little instruction book that comes with it has the exceptionally small font that is only readable in very bright light. There are also a bunch of different cheesy animations that that don't make any sense to me, probably b/c I can barely see them.

Furthermore the battery's aren't replaceable. I have no idea how long they last b/c the kids only wore the watch a few times and I never could remember the complicated operating procedure on how to work them. The watches went into drawer a few months ago and I haven't taken them out since, I have no idea if the batteries are still working.

I have a Computer Science degree, I can setup servers, program VCR's, I'm very very good with technology and gadgets, but these stupid things frustrate me to no end. I bought two at full price so I wasted $60 on these overpriced disappointments.

product_title: Regalo Easy Step Extra Tall Walk Thru Gate, White
review_headline: Has some flaws but its cost plus its height outweigh the negatives. Our standard poodle can open it with enough force.
review_body:
First let me say that we use this gate to contain a dog to a certain part of the house. I cannot comment on how well that this would be for use with children. We have found:

1. It is a bit flimsy in terms of how it connects to the hallway but we do have a large hallway and have not yet bought the adapter that will eliminate some of the gap--this could improve function. Otherwise, you can screw brackets into the wall to help keep it in place and that is what we did.

2. The gate itself seems to be made of a sturdy enough metal but the locking mechanism of the gate can be open with the force of our standard poodle! Granted, she can jump up on the gate and its fine, but with a bit of a head start--she out! Of course, she's also smart about it--she never busts out while we are home yet we always seem to come home to her rooting around the house!! She's a wily one!

3. I could not find a gate at this heigh anywhere else--making it invaluable for large dog owners. Any other options which came close to this height, were $$$$

Bottom line for use with pets: Be prepared to have to screw into the moulding--if you don't want to do that this may not be a good option for big dog owners. Know that with enough brains and a little bit of a running start--your big dog could break out! You will also need a bit of rope to tie the gate door to the support when away from home. Although, I'm hoping this doesn't result in her ripping it from the wall....fingers crossed but so far so good! Despite what might seem like fatal flaws, I challenge you to find a gate at this height! If you have found one - please comment because I will definitely try it. Until then, it is the only show in town for us!

If you have a small dog --this would probably be a great option, but then, you might not need the height anyway!

review_body: This diaper bag is one of my FAVORITE purchases that we "splurged" on for my son's birth. product_title: Summer Infant Dual Coverage Digital Color Video Baby Monitor Set
review_body: We just had a second child and needed a second monitor.  Our 3 year old Summer Infant Slim & Secure is still going strong for the first child although the buttons are difficult to press.  So I was looking for something similar and discovered that there were a lot of changes in the baby monitor world over the past few years.  These new monitors have all these new features that look nice on paper but in reality you're paying for stuff you don't need.  Did you ever need to pan and scan the camera before?  Why do you need to know the temperature in the room remotely?  Do you really want to talk to your child two-way and freak them out for life?    This set seemed to be the best combination of value and features that we were looking for.  It's working great out of the box and I can offer the following points for you to consider:    - This model seems to be more \\"solid\\" than our last Summer Infant monitor in terms of build quality  - The camera cord is still a long 7.5V DC supply with the same connector so you can reuse an older cord of the same specs (our camera was permanently installed so this was a nice benefit)  - Having two units should increase the lifespan of the system.  The handheld unit will fail long before the camera but now you have two handheld units!  - This model is easier to use than our old Summer Infant Slim & Secure    Also, you can compare Summer Infant models and features here:  [...]

product_title: Compac QuikTop Can Cap, 3 Pack
review_body: Got these like 10+ years ago when this French company first landed in the US.  Helped them submit one to The-Gadgeteer for review too.  I think many miss the main purpose of the QuikTop.  If you even remotely think that this can lock in the carbonation for more than a few hours, I have a bridge to sell you.  Liquid will leak through its integrated gasket once CO2 builds-up inside the can.  You will end up having a circle on your table.  But use the QuikTop so that you don't have to aim for the opening to gulp down the drink, THAT'S the main selling point of using the QuikTop.  Another big one is that you can shield your drink from dust, powder, insect, etc., which is another big plus.  But maintaining fizz is and can never be one advantageous factor of the QuikTop cos' it just won't work. It doesn't lock in tight enough onto the can, nor do you want it to as it may pop any time.

product_title: Born Free Nighty Night Nursing Light
review_body:
I received a sample of this from the company for review, and would certainly purchase it myself!

This is a wonderful product, and incredibly useful. It's designed to provide just enough light for nighttime feedings without waking everyone up with a bright light. The product works as intended, and I found it much nicer than turning on a lamp or even a night light - it helped me and baby settle in more quickly after middle-of-the-night feedings. I also found it gave just enough light to re-swaddle the baby. It is made of hard plastic, and I accidentally knocked my baby's head into it a couple of times when burping her, but quickly learned to burp from the opposite side. I also found this incredibly useful for travel - we recently stayed in a hotel room, and if I did not have this small light with me, I would have needed to turn on a very bright light in the middle of the night for feeding and changing and wake up the whole family. My only wish is that it came in a gender neutral color so I could give it as a shower gift for those who do not know what they're having.

Pros: easy to use, good price, perfect for travel
Cons: Not currently available in a gender neutral color

review_body:
I took care of a LO prior to getting PG who had a swing just like this that swung side to side. He loved it and so did I, so I knew I had to get one as soon as my LO arrived.

A lot of people complain about the side to side motion that it doesn't work for their LO's but babies are in general particular about swings. I'm lucky that my LO isn't particular and enjoys both this and a traditional swing.

So far, we've only used it in full recline. She often takes naps in it and in her first month, would really only sleep in this overnight. She loves the ocean sound and now that she's 2 months, I'll sometimes put the seat all the way up (strap her in) and let her listen to the songs, look out, and look at the toys which she enjoys.

I've had to wash the cover and also travel with this (via car) and it's easy to clean and disassemble into a few main parts.

Some have commented about how deep the seat is. It's a little deep for a newborn and I have had to put blankets in the bottom to help cover the uncomfortable straps and raise her up when she was new.

Great swing.

***Update*** My daughter (5 months old now) doesn't love this swing as much as she did when she was a newborn but it still comes in handy every now and then. I will say, this is in the same room as her crib and I use it as a noise machine at night which is a major lifesaver. I have another noise machine in my room since we were bed sharing but now it's at my work, so being able to just turn on the noise machine is great. We've always used the white noise which is really great. So, this item really serves a double purpose!

product_title: The First Years Ignite Stroller (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Deep & wide seat, sturdy, tall handles, folds easily & compact.  Reclines as much as baby car seat (45 degrees).
review_body: I really struggled to decide between the First Years Ignite ($57 on amazon), the Summer 3D Lite Convenience Stroller ($79 on amazon), or the Chicco  Liteway Umbrella stroller ($179 on amazon).  I looked all over for stores who carried them to actually try them out, but no luck. So, I decided to go with the two lower priced ones.  I almost bought the 3D Lite for about $80, then read some of the reviews, which said it was flimsy and sometimes un-locked and started folding, so I decided to go with the Ignite for about $20 less.  Now, you have to know, I don't mind a $20 umbrella stroller, but when my children fall asleep in one, it's darn awkward. Do I let their head bob around, or stop and tilt the stroller back onto a chair at a restaurant or wherever we are?  It isn't ideal.  I wanted a simple umbrella stroller that reclined. My youngest is 18 months old.  It would be nice to have full recline (like 3D Lite), but honestly, my kids sleep fine in their slightly reclined car seats (45 degree recline is great, but they sleep with even less than that.  So, I opted for the lest costly stroller.  If I didn't like it, at least I had wasted less money.  I am very pleased. It arrived in 2 days (amazon prime free 2 day shipping), the fabric is nice and thick, the sun shade is wider than expected and has three toy hooks on the front of the visor that I could easily attach more fabric to, like a blankie, to create more shade if needed, for a sleeping child.  My 5 year olds like it too, and they are 43 and 47 pounds, so still are under the 50 pound weight limit.  The seat belt:  I wish we could easily opt not to use the shoulder straps, but they are permanently attached and you can't buckle the waist belt without the shoulder straps coming with it.  I might cut them off?  But the 18 month old didn't mind them on!  I really like the mommy pack that comes with it in the back up by the handles, it's really nice.  And the bottom basket is nice too!  I don't use a diaper bag, but it fits tons of extra clothes and snacks.  Another thing I noticed after watching youtube videos about each stroller, is that the 3D Lite one, when folded up, has two of its wheels sticking way out in a strange angle.  The First Years Ignite one folds up nice and straight and compact and all together.  If you wanted a shoulder strap for carrying it, like the 3D Lite one has, you could easily create one, like out of a dog leash, with a slip knot on one end and the buckle side on the other, made into a slip knot, or with Rock climbing or camping straps and a two plastic buckles that you can buy at an outdoors store.  They both weigh the same, so weight is not a deciding factor.  The two features I liked about the 3D lite better:  flat recline, carrying strap (plus a little extra sun shade, which people say doesn't make a big difference.  The features I liked about the Ignite better:  Mommy cup and cell phone/zippered pack near handles,  compact and straight lines in the folded up position, $20 less money, and sturdy (maybe sturdier?).  They both hold up to 50 pounds, so that too is not a deciding factor.  I'm very happy with the Ignite.  My 18 month old loves sitting in it at soccer games, watching the big kids play, and loves the smooth ride. review_body: My infant son loves to be carried. I started carrying my son in it at about 9 ish pounds; he still seemed a little small for it, but it did work.

product_title: Safe To Sleep Sleep and Breathing Baby Monitor (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
This was hands down the best purchase I made for peace of mind.

My son was born 8 weeks premature. While we spent the first 6 weeks in the NICU, I looked for a sleepmat. (Knowing the higher risk of SIDS in premies) While doing research, I started reading about strangulations due to wires on some sleep mats, so I kept researching! I found the sleep mat - no wires! I went ahead & purchased it. Best buy I made hands down & lets me get some rest.

If you use the app over the remote you can control some of the alarms better. We have it set not to beep if he's awake. Our sleep monitor is set to beep with slow breath, rapid breath & absence alert... It has gone off a total of 3 times in 4 months - none were false alarms! We had two slow breaths & 1 rapid breath. So thankful for this mat!

This mat also travels well as we have all ready been on our first vacation to visit family.

The only issue we had was easily fixed. We were having issues with the app not letting us change his name or birthdate. We deleted the app & then redown loaded it. Problem fixed.

I will use this mat with any future babies I have - premie or not!

product_title: Pop Pals Ice Pop Holders, 2 Pack, Blue/Green (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Perfect to keep little hands from touching the cold freeze pop.  These work well & can be washed easily.  Definitely recommend.

review_body: Works great for inverted nipples. Even the hospital lactation nurses thought it was great and were going to suggest having it at the hospital. Love it

review_body: We had foam tub letters and numbers, but I wanted something my toddler could better understand. I found these and was very happy! They are adorable! She enjoys sticking them to the tub and of course, chewing on them.

review_body: I bought this for my 18 month old, but I didn't review the height which was my fault.  This is a great stool, but too small right now for what I bought it for. product_title: Baby's My First Photo Album of Family & Friends
review_body:
This was a wonderful idea. I've got pictures of everyone (Me and his dad, grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, daycare providers) holding my son. He gets really excited every time we go through the album. There is a soft fun house mirror on the back page. It's a cute idea, but the reflection is more fun house like than a real mirror.
My only complaint is the fabric outer covering gets dirty from my son teething on it. Not sure how to "wash" it... spot clean I guess. I just wish the outer cover was laminated. Overall, I'm glad I got it.

product_title: Kalencom 2-in-1 Potette Plus
review_body:

I have bought the liners that this company makes to go along with this potty because I like the ease of knowing there won't be spills or leaks if I were to use my own. I also like the ease of not having to carry around both grocery bags and something to put in the bottom of them (although that's a great idea in case I ever find myself without one of Kalencom's liner bags!).
We are using this as an emergency potty for our kids ages 9, 6, and 2, although the 9 and 6 year old are able to hold it until we find an actual bathroom better than the 2 year old.

product_title: Trend Lab Dr. Seuss Changing Pad Cover
review_body: Very cute pattern, have matching sheet in my crib.  Just wish, considering that it's a change pad cover, that it was waterproof on one size, find I have to put a soaker pad overtop to avoid leaking while changing.

product_title: Pickles Pals 27"X54" Hooded Towel, White Cat (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I have had this a couple of months now and use it every other day. My son loves cats and I couldn't find any of these towels that were boyish and figured he is little enough he wouldn't notice the pink too much. I don't believe when I purchased this, there was a picture of the entire towel showing all the pink detail/tail/hands, just the face, so it has more pink than I expected.

Pros:
1. It is a nice large towel that covers my almost 2 year old who is a longer toddler. I can fully wrap him up, and the width of the towel is a lot so it could wrap him up a couple of times.

2. Thicker than most baby/toddler towels I have had. This is a heavier towel, like an adult's towel.

3. Quality - I have had no issues with stitching coming undone. The only issue I could see occurins is with the "paws" where the child could insert their hands; it is a pink towel piece and only has one layer of stiching to attach it to the main body of the towel. If I pulled or tugged hard enough, I could probably pull the paw piece off. The rest of the towel is more like embroidery, and to remove it, I think you would have to take one of those stitching hooks to cut through it, so I don't think anything will happen to the mouse, eyes, ears, nose or mouth.

4. Price - I think it is fair. Towels can get really expensive and this one has some extra cute details for kids.

My son says cat every time he sees it or any animal with 4 legs and gets a smile, so I think we will get our $30 of use out of it. I will probably buy another one more for boys as he gets older because they make bath-time (or being made to get out of the bath, which he loves) a bit more enjoyable.

review_headline: So Convenient for short errands with baby
review_body: This is such a convenient little alternative to carrying a diaper bag, for short errands with the baby. It holds just enough and is compact, not bulky.  Fits both strollers we have, Love this!

review_body: Great so far. No complaints. Better price than the retail store, in stock, and free shipping. Variable flow seems to work if you turn the opening on nipple base to the match the notch on the ring.

product_title: Frozen Elsa and Ann Gilr's Swimwear Monokinis One Piece Swimsuit (5-6 years)
review_body: Ny daughter loves it. The only thing I am unsure of it how the decal of Anna and Elsa will wear. After repeated exposure to chlorinated water and being washed it may crack peel and or fade. So far so good.

product_title: Bumkins Waterproof Sleeved Bib
review_body:
The outer layer of the bib is made of a satin-like material, so it rinses out really well. The stitching at the cuff is done with a satiny thread, so that rinses out well, too (although it does stain, but not a big deal). The lining is like the inside of a raincoat - kind of rubbery maybe? So it gives great waterproof protection. So far, I've had no issues. The bib has worked well and has done what it's supposed to do which is keep my kid's clothes clean and dry. I do use a Baby Bjorn bib at the same time since it does a much better job at catching dropped food.

Two improvements I would suggest: Maybe consider adjustable snap closures (the tie works pretty well - I just prefer snaps), and also it would be great if it were longer to cover the legs better and also if it wrapped around the sides of the child more. It fits my 25lb 14 month old really well, and overall it does a great job of protecting. But I would prefer more complete protection.

It's very gentle on toothless gums and I love to watch my son go to town chomping on it.  He also enjoys the occasional chew on the 'ears' that stick out.  They make a crinkly sound that makes them stimulating to both the teeth and ears. The only problem is that if he were to hold on to the teether and chew on the white part himself, he would have to grasp the red knobby part in his hand and bring the teether to his mouth.  He has small hands and coordination difficulties, so he has a hard time with that.  As a result, when he's chewing on the white part, I have to hold it in his mouth for him.

product_title: BOB Infant Car Seat Adapter For Single Strollers
review_headline: Not a "perfect" fit but does the job

FYI, With our first child, at around 4 months we had the baby in the jogger for short runs with a Snuzzler to provide extra support. http://www.amazon.com/Summer-Infant-77510-Snuzzler-Ivory/dp/B0045VA3SO

product_title: Baby Jogger 2013 Summit X3 Double Stroller, Green (Prior Model) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I have only had this stroller for about two weeks, but I love it! The color is a nice muted lime green. I am using this stroller with my 16 month old and newborn. Obviously I will not run with this until my little one is 6-8 months or so. I put a stroller insert in the stroller and laid the seat back all the way and he fits really well. THERE IS NO CARSEAT ADAPTOR FOR THIS SEAT! This isn't a problem for us, but it might be for others. So far we have only walked about a mile at a time in the stroller, but it is through thick gravel and grass. The stroller has a really smooth ride and I feel comfortable having my infant in the stroller even on the rough terrain. (I had a cheap jogger without shocks with my daughter and didn't feel comfortable with her in it even when she was 9 months!) The ride on this stroller is super smooth! There are only two things I would change on this strolle. 1. The handlebar height. I am 5' and the handlebar is slightly too high. It is ok when I am walking, but I think it will cause discomfort while running. 2. I wish they would have put an automatic larch to close the stroller. This just has a strap with velcro. My other BJ has the latch so I am not sure why they didn't put it on this stroller.

Also, there are not a lot of adapters for this stroller, i.e. no carseat, a more expensive belly bar. Only the compact pram which is pretty small. Not a deal breaker for us, but you should consider this.

We debated this stroller and the BOB. We decided on this stroller because my daughter screamed and screamed when we tried the BOB. I think there are a couple of reasons for this if you are considering the BOB. 1. The canopy. With the canopy folded it kept covering my tiny 15 months head. There are strings to help a little, but it wasn't enough to fix the problem and she doesn't want the canopy out unless it is raining or too sunny. 2. The Bob doesn't have as much back support and a little more recline. I like having that extrasupport for the kids. 3. The fabric on the Bob isn't smooth. It is supposed to have ergonomic support, but the fabric just seemed to annoy my daughter.
I prefer the smooth fabric and canopy that doesn't hit my daughter in the face. That said, my SIL had an older style BOB that was wonderful! If they had kept the BOB the the way it was I would have gotten the Bob. Especially since the BJ is $200 more!

I do LOVE this stroller and am glad I chose it over the BOB!

product_title: Fisher-Price Ocean Wonders Jumperoo (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: My baby girl does not want to give this thing up, even though she's growing out of it. She has beefy little legs from bouncing in here all the time. I bought it because of it's pretty ocean themed look, and she loves all the toys and sounds it makes. Sturdy and heavy.

review_body: I love these sleeping bags. This pattern is super cute, but unfortunately the stitching came loose at the neck after two washes. I'm hoping mine was just a lemon, because I've never had an issue with the Grobags before and I've used them for both of my kids.

product_title: Graco Sweet Slumber Sound Machine, White
review_body:
I rarely ever write reviews... in case this puts this review into perspective.

When my husband and I were still just expecting our first child, we were told to get the Sleep Sheep... which we did. After countless muttering, tears and exhausted nights of wondering why anyone would only want 44 minutes of white noise, we decided there must be a noise machine that would just stay on all night. We looked into a few and picked this on a whim (an exhausted, pained, panicked whim).

The first night we plugged this in we ALL slept through the night. It has pretty much been the same since. This machine lasts all night, has great volume control options and a wide variety of sounds (we like the ocean one) and serves as a great night light - soft lighting but strong enough to actually let you see when you sneak in to check on everything.

My son is a pretty good sleeper - we were dealing with random awakenings and cries for replacing a pacifier, not horrible all-nighters that could not be soothed... but I will give a lot of credit for 99.99% peaceful 11-12 hour nights sleep sessions from 4/5 months to now (8.5 months) to this machine. Plus, if you have the monitor on like we do, you actually get two for the price of one since we joke that we use his noise machine too! Honestly, this product is terrific and I would recommend it for anyone whose baby could use a little white noise to keep peaceful nights peaceful.

product_title: Maxi-Cosi  Pria 70 with Tiny Fit Convertible Car Seat, Total Black
review_body:
We love this car seat!! It grows with your child from 5lbs to 70lbs. Instead of buying an infant seat, a toddler seat and a booster seat over the next few years, why not get all that in one seat and save some money. This car seat does exactly that. Our car seat was purchased August of 2012 from Amazon for $259.

First of all, it took over a week of searching online and calling customer service to find out where the instruction manual was hiding- FYI, turn the car seat face down, on the left side towards the top under the black part of the seat cover you will find a velcro pocket where the manual and other seat belt pieces are hiding.

I found it confusing to install so I had a cop friend of mine who was a certified car seat installer install it for us and it took him less than 5 minutes. He made it look easy and we got the hang of it quickly. If you can’t figure out how to install it, Google certified car seats installers- Its free to get them to install it for you and they’ll do it right.

We have a large SUV (Toyota Sequoia) and this seat fits in the center seat of the second row with plenty of room on either side for others to sit. We started using this seat right away when we brought our 7 pound baby home from the hospital. With the extra padding and attachments for newborns, she fit very nicely. We bought a second one after bringing her home for our second car (Crew-Cab Tacoma) and it fits perfectly in middle back seat. Now that we are expecting again we bought 2 more for our two vehicles.

We have traveled with this car seat too, installing it in a Chevy Impala rental and on an airplane coach seat. It fit in the rental behind the passenger seat with plenty of room for two other people to sit in the back but the airplane was a pain. It fits in a coach seat, it was just a pain to put in the seat, take out of the seat, and lugging around the tight plane aisles and carrying around the airport. Going through security was no picnic either. Save yourself the stress and don’t take this seat with you on a plane.

After 15 months of daily use, there are no signs of wear or tear. It’s in practically new condition. The seat cushion is easy to remove and put back on if you need to wash but its water proof so we just wipe any spills up and only had the need to wash it once in the past 15 months. There is only one cup holder though. I wish it had two but that wasn’t a deal breaker for us.

Aside from being a 3 in 1 system, what sold us was the safety features. The air bags gave us the extra piece of mind knowing if we are ever in a wreck, our baby is well protected in this seat.no picnic either. Save yourself the stress and don’t take this seat with you on a plane.

product_title: Clek Foonf 2014 Convertible Car Seat, Green/White Dragonfly (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
The car seat is expensive but the safety features are worth it to us. We have last year's model (2013) in blue and we had some issues with the metal on the straps getting caught when tightening. This particular 2014 model does not have that problem. We are still rear facing, and while some reviewers think the seat sits up too high, I disagree as there is still quite a bit of room between the seat and the roof (in a trailblazer) and I'm glad my son can see out the back window - it keeps him occupied during our commute. He generally seems comfortable in the seat. I haven't had any spills yet so I don't have a review of the ease of cleaning. I do wish the straps release latch was a bit easier to reach, but that's a minimal issue. It is also very heavy - we probably will not use it for air travel. Overall, we are happy with this seat.

Update 3/14: I recently rented a Chevy Malibu and used the Foonf in the rear center seat. I was surprised at how much space there was above the seat given how high it sits.

Update 5/4: We took the Foonf on a plane trip and it actually went really well. It is really heavy and I could not have handled it alone with a toddler, but my husband was able to pre-board on most flights and get it set up while I stayed in the terminal and entertained our son. We used a $20 luggage cart to roll the Foonf and we were able to put another carry-on bag in the seat so we didn't have to carry it through the airport. It did not fit through the security x-ray machines so leave some extra time for manual screening. It was also too wide to fit through some plane aisles so we had to carry it above the seat (again, I could not have done this alone), but it fit well in the seat. We set it on recline position 2 in the seat, and although our son didn't sleep at all, he seemed quite comfortable. We also used it in the rear passenger-side seat of a Camry, and it was a bit tight getting him into the seat under the door frame.

product_title: Cloud B Twilight Ladybug - Pink
review_headline: Perfect "night light" with auto shutoff and great features!
review_body:
Cloud B has hit it out of the park with their Twilight animal line. We have the turtle for my 3 year old son and now the ladybug for my daughter. This ladybug is even cuter in person. The animal is very soft and plush but the shell is hard plastic so it probably can't be used very well for snuggling but is very durable and can be used for play. I love that the projected stars are actual constellations. We are just getting to the age with my 3 year old where we can point out the different constellations and compare them to the real thing on clear nights. One of my favorite things about the ladybug are the color options. You can choose red, blue, or green stars and you can push the ON button a second time to make it rotate between the three at a slow pace. My son was in love with this feature and kept saying "wow!" Red is definitely the most muted color choice and blue is the brightest. The stars project very well all over the room but are more defined and brighter the closer you put the ladybug to the ceiling. We leave ours on the dresser, turn it on for lights out, and the kiddos are in dreamland before the auto shutoff at 45 minutes (another great feature). I find traditional night lights too bright for leaving on all night so I love the ladybug's auto shutoff and easy to find buttons for turning on or off manually. With fresh batteries (3 AAA) the stars seem very bright and project the best. Over time (months of daily use) you will notice the stars getting more and more muted and softer. For some this is preferable but when they become too soft for your liking just replace the batteries and the stars will be very bright again. The Twilight Ladybug is a fabulous way to help your kiddos drift off to sleep with a gentle night light that is fun and educational.

The 45 minute shutoff has also come in handy recently with my 3 year old that is starting to refuse naps. Now we tell him he has to stay in his room and rest until the stars go off and if he's still awake he can get up. 95% of the time he falls asleep :)s still awake he can get up. 95% of the time he falls asleep :)

product_title: Boppy Noggin Nest Head Support, Brown Wheels
review_body: My son developed a flat head, like so many other babies with the promoting of back sleeping.  My husband and I did do the helmet for our son, which we were so happy about. review_body: I got a medium, large and XL because I wasn't sure about the sizing, and I have a 35lb slender son, a 25lb heftier daughter, and an 18 lb infant. product_title: RECARO Performance SPORT Combination Harness to Booster
review_headline: Great Seat But Doesn't Fit Everywhere

BUT the only reason I bought this seat was to put it in the back of a Porsche 911 (a 997.1 C4 specifically). It does NOT fit, even though apparently past (nearly similar) iterations did. I tried it cold with no mods, I tried it without the seat backs, I tried it with towels, all to no avail. It's just too big and bulky on the back. So all you PCar owners consider yourself warned. Back to Amazon it goes.

Really, really wish this would have worked out! For cars with more room, this seat would be a no-brainer.

product_title: Baby Jogger 2013 City Select Single Stroller, Onyx (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I abosolutley love this stroller, my little one is 7 months old 16lbs and about 27\\", my 4 year old weights about 36lbs, slim and tall for his age, (wears size 6 jeans) and this stroller is just perfect, I did a lot of research for several days in dferent strollers, the Britax I didn't like the fact that the older child has to ride pretty much in the basket underneath top child, it looks horrible it feels like if you just threw your child in the basket, I noticed that the  setting in most strollers is the same as Britax also I looked at one where the seat for the 2nd older child is attach to the front and looks like it hangs up high it's just awkward. After days of research i decided to go with this one, I love it, I tried every single set up at home once I took it out of the package and tried it with both kids in it and on diferent positions just to make sure that I would be satisfied with I was looking for, (in case I needed to return it  so it wouldn't get dirty by taking outside) it is pricey but, well worth the money, I wanted something that I could use as a double, but that I could turn into a compact single stroller as well when is just my youngest daughter ride In it. is so small and light, the first time i used it, was very cold out and I didn't want to stand out getting the infant in it, so I put the oldest in the stroller and held my infant till we got in the mall, I pushed the stroller with one hand and held her with the other. I had no problems, the way I have set up is I have my oldest sitting closer to me, facing the front and my infant facing me in lower seat, just because I like the fact that I can recline her seat all the way if need to,  the basket underneath its huge and easy to get too, I bought from BJ a handle attachment for my keys wallet and also has room for a bottle water/soda. Both seats have a spot to store small things like keys and wallets in the back of each seat, but I wanted something closer to me, there is some seating positions inwhich you can't recline the seats all the way, but there is some where you can recline both, I looked past that, first because my oldest is 4 and doesn't need his seat recline as much as my youngest, and second of all NO stroller is going to be PERFECT they all will have its flaws but this one is the one I think I could get past that. Just to mention seat material I think is a very decent quality, and I like removing both seats just because it saves half the room in my trunk by putting them on top of stroller I also take the big wheels off with a push of a button . and I put them to the side and it saves even more room in the trunk, I was able to fit the stroller frame in the passenger seat of my car by taking the big wheels off, which isn't hard at all, it sure sounds like a pain to take wheels off and seats off, but when you have a small car like I do (Pontiac G6 4 door) taking the time to do it it's well worth it,  it is annoying at times that the stroller won't stand on its own, but oh well I can get past that, I noticed the first day I  used it that one of the smaller wheels with the suspension squeaked really bad, I was worry at first about calling BJ customer service to have wheels replace since I read previous reviews saying that BJ customer service was horrible, I called this morning and phone call wasn't even 5 minutes long , I gave the Rep the serial number, manufactured date, my name, address and email  and now the wheel is on its way via FedEx, a few minutes later I had an email confirmation with an order #, the Representative was awesome very professional and polite, and I was not required to sent defective wheel back. Last thing I should say is if you like this stroller but are unsure, take a chance and buy it, once you get it , put it together all you have to do is to snap the wheels in place and seat , and test it in your house with your kids I it, if you like it awesome and if you don't put it back in the box and return it, amazon is very flexiblewith returns and sometimes will even pay for shopping back to them if you are not satisfied, so you have nothing to loose, give it try .

product_title: Evenflo Classic Johnny Jump Up, Frogs (Discontinued by Manufacturer) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
The idea is sound, but the design is poor.

An others have mentioned, the leg holes are too far apart. My 8 month is still too small for it. The leg holds are much too far apart for her body. She falls over to one side (leg hole) or the other, with the other leg then in the air.Maybe she can use it at 12 months.

Also, the spring design is terrible. It isn't adjustable. Frankly speaking, it's cheap and does not flex (spring) smoothly up and down (the desired effect). For proper function, the spring tension must be adjustable, to adapt to the varying weights of different size children.

This is rated up to 24 pounds. So for a girl (my case), I can only use this from 12 months to around 18-21 months. Not even one year. This doesn't make for an attractive purchase. If the leg holes were closer together so that a 6-8 month toddler could make use of it, I could at least get one year's use out of it.

Children get bored with this, hanging in one location. A walker is much more attractive to the child as they can move about and have lights and other functions to play with, and they're legs get as much if not more exercise.

product_title: Philips AVENT BPA Free Natural Drinking Cup, 9 Ounces
review_headline: Worth the learning curve. Excellent training cup, improves hydration, and better for their teeth!
review_body:
We love this cup. Our son uses them exclusively at 14 months, which makes his pediatrician happy since sippy cups and bottles cause dental issues due to liquid pooling by the teeth.

He is able to drink more liquid faster from this cup than he ever did from a sippy. However, there is a learning curve. At first, our son would tip the cup and depress the valve, but not drink the liquid fast enough, so it spilled down his front. After a few months adjusting to it with water, he now uses it for both water and milk without spilling. (He doesn't drink juice yet.) If you are patient enough to let your child learn how to use it, it really pays off. (Conversely, if you judge it on its first usage alone, though, you will be disappointed.) It teaches a child how to use a regular cup from the standpoint of how the lips and cup interact -- they'll have to learn about how far to tip an open cup later. Everything in stages!

We still have to be careful if he is carrying it around because while it doesn't spill, sometimes we get dribbles on the floor if he didn't drink all of the liquid he released with the valve.

product_title: Ameda Purely Yours Breast Pump (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I did not purchase my pump through Amazon. It was covered by insurance and purchased through a medical supplier; however, this thing is so bad I feel compelled to write a review. It is not an exaggeration when I say my hand pump works better. In fact, I have resorted to using my hand pump while I wait for a replacement from a different brand. I’ve been using my pump regularly for about 2 months and after ongoing issues it is no longer working. I have replaced all of the parts with the exception of the pump itself to no avail.

- One of the flanges cracked at the base within the first 2 weeks
- I’ve gone through about 4 sets of pump valves, two sets in the last two weeks. They are very delicate and get little micro-tears in the bottom, rendering suction useless.
- Sometimes milk does not flow through the valve into the bottle. For whatever reason, the milk pools in the valve and eventually gets sucked up into the tubing….yes, sucked into the tubing. The exact opposite of what Ameda advertises.
- The diaphragm sometimes gets sucked into air input/output hole and clogs it up
- The writing rubs off of the storage bottles with only hand washing
- The pump makes a horrible beeping noise with every suction. I could live with this if the pump actually worked.

Not cool Ameda…very poor quality.

product_title: Safety 1st Magnetic Locking System
review_headline: Had them for over a year and they're still awesome!
review_body:
I have no idea what the few people who have said these locks don't work are talking about! Seriously, they either must have had bad batches, installed them improperly or installed them on non-recommended cabinets or drawers. The way your cabinets are built is important, they need to be framed. If the door is flush mounted into the cabinet, there will be nowhere to put the latch piece (which isn't the lock's fault).

My husband installed these on all of our lower kitchen cabinets that were built in the 1950s - solid birch wood, all of our new pantry cupboards built in 2012 - also solid birch wood and thick, on our bathroom cabinets under the sink, built in the 90s, on our hallway built-in cupboards built in the 50s but differently styled than the kitchen, and after a full year of toddler abuse (my son's nickname at 1.5 years old is \\"The Bulldozer\\" ) the locks work perfectly as if we had installed them yesterday.

I can't give enough praise for these locks. Our cabinets look as they always did, you would never know they have locks. When installed correctly they don't open at ALL, no pinched fingers. They work so well that my son very rarely tugs on them anymore and if he does it's very half-hearted, he knows he cannot get past these locks.

These shouldn't take the place of parental supervision of course, nothing is perfect (and we don't keep rat poison under the sink or anything ridiculous like that) but I feel VERY secure and comfortable knowing these locks are in place.

The disable feature takes these to a new level of convenience. When cooking, or for grandparents who don't have the kids every day, the disable feature is a must have. Once you try these locks, you'll wish you'd had them all along. I will never use another kind unless they find some way to improve on these, though I can't imagine how.

Buy a few extra keys, you may lose one as I did: the magnetic key stuck to a rarely used pot that was then put away for a long time. I recently found it and laughed, oh THAT'S where that darn key went! I installed 3M hooks inconspicuously on the walls near the locked cabinets, looped a ribbon through they hole on the key and hung them up - now that it's habit to put them back we don't lose them. Just takes a bit to adjust to constantly locked cabinets. And with 2 toddlers and 1 on the way, these will be in use at our house for years to come. product_title: Evenflo Tribute 5 Convertible Car Seat
review_headline: Cost is in line with quality, works fine as an extra car seat.
review_body:
Thankfully, I only bought this to use as an extra car seat in my mom's car, so it rarely gets used. It's very small and lightweight, so if you will be moving the seat back and forth a lot or have a very small vehicle and only drive short distances, this seat will work out just fine for you. And I do really like the way it looks.

My issues with the seat are:

-When my 16-month-old falls asleep in it, his head slumps forward, which does not happen in his other car seats. It's a little too upright, or something. This is the #1 thing I don't like about it, and why I recommend not using it if you plan to take longer car trips where you want your child to sleep.

-It just doesn't feel "sturdy".

-The optional cupholder is completely useless. It is basically a thin plastic circle clip thingy. My mom said the book says only to use paper or styrofoam cups in it. I don't know about you, but I'm not really comfortable giving a toddler a styrofoam cup, especially in the back seat of a car. I like the built-in double cupholders on the car seat I use regularly because I can put toys, sippys, snacks, whatever in there, and it's super convenient. It would be hard for a younger child to even reach the clip-on cupholder for this seat, so I think it's pointless unless you have a coordinated and well-behaved 3 or 4 year old in the seat. There's just really no room for any extras in this seat.

It is VERY basic, but seems to be just fine as an "extra". I would NOT recommend using this as your main car seat.
