review_body: This teas didn't seem to help me much.  I am drinking it as directed and I've seen little increase in supply.  I prefer the Earth Momma Angel Baby Tea or the Yogi Tea.

product_title: Sassy Soft Cushion Play Space Interlocking Mats (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: different than the ones at target
review_body:
i recently bought a few sets of these at target and loved them. each pack had 6 different colored squares with contrasting center shapes. since we expanded the play area, we thought we would order a few packs to add on. however, these were not as good as the ones in the store: in every pack, there are only 5 colors, with one repeated color. i noticed this in all of the packs i ordered through amazon. second, the centerpieces were only two colors - either red or blue! i might be picky, but the area just looks unbalanced now with fewer colors and contrast.

in total, from target and amazon, we needed 5 packs to cover our play room area. had i known we would need so many, i would've skipped these and purchased a larger set from a different manufacturer for less cost.

product_title: EveryDay Willow Wool Dryer Balls Gift Set of 3, Natural
review_headline: Better than the rubber ones by far!
review_body: I've used the rubber ones - several brands and have had mixed results - the most recent (and most expensive rubbery ones) literally started falling to pieces within a month!  Alarming.  I got these and really love them - no sticky perfumes, no sheets to find - just performance and happiness.  Highly recommended.

product_title: SwaddleDesigns Stroller Blanket, Color Puff Circles
review_body:
I don't know why it's so hard to find blankets for children with binding on them. All kids love to brush soft satin up against their faces or hold it in their hands. My mom paid full price (with a heart attack) for the first one so my daughter could have a blanket with binding. She's had this one about 1 1/2 years and absolutely loves this. It's been through the wash so many times. Now she's gotten so attached I just ordered a second one so I can wash the first.

This has held up incredibly well considering all the hugging, tugging, catching under stroller wheels it's gotten. All the trips it's been on, all the visits to the play houses, playgrounds, pools! There are no stitches or thread missing. The white part is a little less \\"fluffy\\" but to be totally less expected. I don't think that either of us can begrudge the price--I seriously doubt a set of sheets I bought for the same price would hold up as well with this much use!

product_title: Graco Smart Seat All-in-One Convertible Car Seat - Rosen
review_headline: Rock solid car seat for all ages but...
review_body: Very sturdy, great materials and padding, price is too expensive but it could be the last car seat you'll ever buy. We bought a Graco Snug Ride and we wish we could have bought this one first so to save us some money. I wish the arm rest folds up to sit our baby easily.

product_title: Graco Nautilus 3-in-1 Car Seat
review_body: This is a very nice, highly-rated car seat for a reasonable price.  I love that I can keep my son in the harness for a long time (much safer).  The two cup-holders are great and the little storage cubbies are favorite features of my son.  Raising and lowering the harness height is easy, as was installation.  We have a Britax Frontier in our main car, which we love, but have purchased two of these for our second car and grandma's car.

product_title: Diono Mighty Tite Car Seat Tightner, Grey (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: We bought one similar to this almost 10 years ago and absolutely loved it. We lost it over the years, and looked for another one. We just got two of these, one for each car. We have older cars without safely latches, and the car seats were still too loose and would wiggle around even when the seat belt was as tight as it could get. These worked perfect!

product_title: JJ Cole Hamper
review_headline: Not bad, keep a sharp eye out for sloppy workmanship.
review_body: Showed up very wrinkled fabric on something that's supposed to look tight. It's a nice alternative design style to typical baby stuff but I found problems with a few pieces from JJ Cole through Amazon. I'm not sure if someone bought some factory B grades from JJ cole and sold them as A grades, but I had a few returns on JJ Cole stuff until I found one that was perfect. Keep a close eye on this stuff if you order it. I found glue on a different piece of JJ Cole, and red ink on another.

product_title: Sesame 2 Count  Sheet Set
review_body: I got this set for my grandson and he LOVES it!!! He is 1 1/2 yrs. old and recognizes the characters and what they are doing. He gets so excited when he sees his favorite characters on his "big boy bed," and can't wait to hop right in.  The fitted and flat sheets are roomy and fit well.  The comforter is soft, colorful, more than large enough for bed or cuddling, and has just the right amount of filling so it doesn't make him hot and sweaty.

product_title: Reusable Food Pouch (Set of 8)
review_body:
Glad I finally found these. The 2 sizes are handy as some foods my kids can't eat a large pouch, but easily gobble down a small one. I was worried about keeping them clean, but after a few months of usage there are no spaces where food gets stuck. I've frozen them fine. I learned to double check the bottom ziplock as my baby squeezed hard and had a lap of yogurt! I've found that the lids from other pre packaged pouches fit, so I kept those for extras as no extra lids are provided.

The designs are cute, but would like to see some simple geometric shapes/ designs for school aged kids. I suspect my kindergartner will soon be calling the designs babyish and refuse to publicly eat out of one (unless its something really yummy).

My second time buying these, this time I also bought some as a birthday gift.

product_title: The First Years Toy Story Insulated Straw Cup (Colors may vary) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

review_body: These cups don't leak rather they just hold liquid in the straw that wasn't swallowed. While this doesn't bother me, that is because we only use them for water which is why I am giving them a 4 star rather than 5. They are durable very easy to clean and take apart and put back unlike other straw sippy cups!

product_title: Mommy's Helper Bath Mat Froggie Collection, Green, 6-48 Months (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: We have a very very slightly textured tub.  The suction cups wouldn't stick at all.  Return was easy.  They were very cute, but really have to have a completely smooth surface.

product_title: Pink Rosary in a Porcelain Keepsake Box Christening Baptism Gift
review_body: The rosary is delicate and adorable. The box would be lovely, but the lid simply doesn't fit.  I couldn't take the time to return because it was a gift that was leaving the country.  I spared the rosary and opted for a different box.

product_title: Evenflo SureRide 65 DLX Convertible Car Seat - Nicole
review_body: Package arrived on time & in great condition. Car seat is not too big, not too small... just the right size! Fits perfect in my Nissan Maxima! Very easy to keep clean & is very roomy. I see it as a long-term car seat for my daughter for sure! \\")

product_title: Doidy Cup - Red color
review_headline: Interesting idea but not really useful
review_body: My breastfed daughter hated anything other than the breast. I didn't mind but it was very hard to go out with my husband once a month or have any time to myself being that she refused bottles. So we thought maybe we should just skip bottles altogether and bought this along with some sippy cups. My daughter chewed on this but the claim that babies use it seems absurd, my kids have both been ahead developmentally but this cup was not what it claimed to be for my baby. Just get a sippy or use a regular cup.

product_title: Dandelion Organic Toy Crinkle Book (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I was very underwhelmed when we received this because I thought it was going to be more... Substantial? However, I was wrong to be disappointed with it because our son LOVES this! He loves to chew on the knots, shake it,flip the \\"pages\\", crinkle it in his hands and rub it on his cheeks. I wouldn't really describe it as a \\"book\\" though. Just a crinkle toy. It's super soft and the crinkle is great. It seems to be really well made and we will definitely be purchasing more dandelion products.

product_title: Graco Nautilus 3-in-1 Car Seat
review_headline: Good looking, well constructed but TERRIBLE BUCKLE
review_body:
I would absolutely rank this seat higher than I did, except for one big problem: the buckle.

The set itself is well constructed, it's a good looking seat (as far as car seats go) it's not too big to leave room for other kids in the back seat, but it has one glaring flaw: the BUCKLE.

The buckle is really difficult to unsnap, some might say impossible. Neither of the kids' grandmothers can depress the button well enough to unsnap the straps. If you have caregivers who will be using this seat with arthritis, forget it, get a different seat. I can barely get the buckle to work it's so tough. If you're putting your kid in and out of this seat many times a day, having to deal with that buckle is a dealbreaker. I wish I'd know that this was a problem so I could weigh the pros with that huge functional con. You can read other reviews that state the same thing: Some kids are getting stuck in their seats because the buckle will not budge, and this appears to be a problem the company is AWARE of, but is not fixing.

Also, the straps that go around the child's legs leave very little room once buckled in the seat. The buckle is way too far back on the seat, meaning it digs into your kid's crotch. I have a skinny kid, but if your little one has juicy thighs, the straps might be way too tight to be comfortable.

product_title: Lollaland Lollacup - Infant/Toddler Sippy Cup with Straw
review_body:
I bought this cup and a Zoli Bot 6oz cup because I liked the idea of the weighted straw following the drink around. My son has a tendency to tip his cup when he drinks and with other straw cups it meant as soon as it was half empty the straw wasn't in the liquid anymore.

The cup works fine, and it's cute, but overall I like the Zoli much better. In the Zoli, the straw itself is silicone so you can literally hold the cup in any direction, even upside down, and still drink from it. In this cup, the straw is weighted at the bottom but still pretty stiff, so it just moves from side to side at the bottom of the cup.

The Zoli cup does not leak. If you look at the Zoli straw, it has little prongs over the top to prevent spillage (sort of like a Camelbak water bottle, but the baby doesn't have to bite down for them to separate.) The Lollacup is just an open straw, so it spills quite easily.

The Zoli handles are attached to the lid and do not come off. The Lollacup handles are like a base the cup screws into, except I find it pops out really easily. The cup is wide enough around that it's not really comfortable for my 1 year old to hold with just his hands, so when I use it I'm always screwing it back onto the handles.

If all my other cups are dirty I'll use the Lollacup and it's fine, but I certainly don't think it's worth the price tag.

But I find that when I unzip the bra at all,I lose the much-needed support and the pump flanges start to move around, which can cause loss of suction, or pinching, or other undesirable effects. So, I find that I use ths bra a lot less than I had hoped.  I wanted to love this bra, but I find it just okay.

product_title: Diono Radian RXT Convertible Car Seat, Storm
review_headline: This is the carseat you want
review_body:
I have two Radian RXTs. The first I bought when my then not-yet-two-year-old was outgrowing the height limit on her Britax while rear facing. When we made the switch she was in toddler heaven. So much more room to still be rear facing. She could get comfortable and change leg positions - it was great. It was in the middle seat position before the baby came along so she had a very comfortable recline position. After the baby moved to the middle position when she outgrew her infant seat, the oldest was still comfortable enough to stay rear facing (now 2y8mos) for a while longer. The body is very roomy and she can still move her long legs around to get comfortable on long trips. We have to use the angle adjuster to get her seatback upright enough to make the front passenger seat able to move a safe distance away from the dashboard.

The baby has been in her Radian for 2 months and still does not like it. She did not like the infant seat either so I think she is just one of those that will not like any of them. At least she's safe!!

I like that these car seats will be used for many years and they are slim enough to ride side by side in my SUV - which allows an adult to ride beside the kids when warranted.

product_title: Best Bottom Inserts - Stay Dry Insert - Large
review_body:
I bought these NIP from Once Upon A Child about a week ago (a 3 pack). I'm writing the review because I always rely on amazon consumers reviews before I make most of my purchases and I like to return the favor. At first I was SO excited about these! They snap into the diaper (front and back) so they don't slip out of place! I love that unlike a pocket diaper it stays in place (especially when you have a boy it's an important feature!) and won't slide back after a few minutes of bottom-scooting. Unfortunately, I have two very big issues with these. The first problem I noticed right away, EBF baby poo isn't absorbed quickly, and (I left a review on the owl diaper about this) ends up sliding out of the top back side of the diaper and getting poo EVERYWHERE (yuck!) my second problem is after only about a week- week 1/2 (once a day washing and hang drying) the blue surging is fraying and looks like, in a short amount of time, it will come undone and fall apart altogether. If this was a $5 diaper I wouldn't be disappointed but for 1 diaper and 3 inserts I paid nearly $30! Definitely NOT worth the money for a diaper that's only going to last a month, even if its well taken care of, its just going to fall apart unless you have a giant rotation. Buyer be warned!
~UPDATE~
It's been 8 months of using these in my diaper rotation daily so I thought I would add to this review. The fraying stopped after the first couple weeks and has not seemed to be an issue, just cosmetic. It is a pretty absorbent insert but the downside is it's extremely bulky and due to size restrictions won't last all of your diapering days. It can be used as an inner for pockets such as an alvababy BUT you'll probably get the plumber crack effect due to it taking up so much space as the baby gets older and fills out a OS diaper. The nice thing about this is it really does keep the urine off baby if used as intended. I stand by my original review on the EBF poo; it simply did not work for us in thatway and the cover was sold off because it too was a large factor. The insert doesn't absorb EBF poo the way it does urine and I would caution buyers that have a baby who often times create \\"blowout\\" type of bowel movements. I still stand by my price review as well. I do not believe the set was worth what I paid for it. After all is said and done I wouldn't buy this again. For the pice I paid for an \\"okay\\" diaper set (3) that last less than a year I would have purchased 5 OS china cheapies with some flour sack towels for extra absorbency. I did bump up my review from a one star to two because the inserts didn't fall apart as expected. ***disclaimer*** every baby is different and everyone has their own preferences.

product_title: Infant Optics DXR-5 Portable Video Baby Monitor
review_headline: Low budget but worth a look
review_body:
I purchased this for our newborn daughter's room. The price is one of the lowest I've seen for such a capable product and while there are some shortcomings -- it performs well within acceptable ranges.

A few things I wish the monitor had:

1) A talk button
2) A sturdier kickstand mechanic
3) The ability to recover from a power outage without manually turning it on
4) A video feed that didn't appear always washed out no matter the lightning conditions

Despite the above features I'd like, the monitor was significantly cheaper than most video monitoring systems, worked within the range we required in our home and has thus far been reliable.

product_title: Britax Advocate 70-G3 Convertible Car Seat Seat, Opus Gray (Prior Model)
review_headline: Great Seat - No Issues Except it is Large
review_body:

We do a lot of traveling and he seems very comfortable and happy in this seat compared to the old baby seat. Maybe it is the soft, fluffy material?

It was fairly easy to install. When the seat was not yet installed, I thought the adjustment handles were going to be difficult to use, but once installed I never noticed any issues (and forgot about it completely).

My only slightly negative comment (I can't even say that it is a complaint) is that the seat is quite large for my vehicle. I have an older Toyota Highland. There aren't any clips in the middle seat, and the middle seat is slightly curved, so car seats have to be installed in one of the outside seats. In our Highlander, the seat folds down to make a larger trunk, with a 2/3 and 1/3 fold. We installed this seat in the outside seat that would allow the 2/3 seat to still fold down so that we can still access the third row seating. However, we can't fold down the 2/3 seat-back because of the giant "wings" on this car seat - without quite a bit of effort. We don't use the third row that much, and often it is just for kids who are happier to climb over the seat anyway, so it hasn't been too much of a problem.

product_title: Maxi-Cosi Prezi Infant Car Seat, Delightfully Natural
review_headline: Too deep and/or snug-fitting - we hate this seat.
review_body:
I did a lot of research to find what I thought would be the best infant car seat for our baby girl. We have had a lot of comments on how nice this one looks, but being a first-time mom, I had never really paid attention to what car seats look like. I chose this one for the safety features and the fact that it's one of the least toxic in terms of materials. I read good reviews of it, but there was not a ton of info available - I think this car seat just came out at the end of 2012. We are now on the hunt for a better car seat, but I thought I would share our experience with this one in case it's helpful to others.

The issues we have with this seat:

1. Too deep and snug fitting - The main issue we have with this car seat is that it is extremely difficult to put the baby into it - right away, even bringing her home from the hospital in it was torture. She was 7 pounds then, so not a huge baby. She's now 12 pounds and the seat is even worse (it is supposed to last till 30 pounds). The seat seems really deep and I thought that's just the way car seats are - it's supposed to be snug fitting for safety, right? Then I started talking to other friends with kids and realized ours is exceptionally difficult. I feel like I have to bend my baby in half to get her into the seat, and then she is sitting so deep into it that it's a nightmare to get her out again - I basically have to work my hands around behind her to push her body forward enough to get her little shoulders in front of the shoulder straps. The shoulder straps are in a fixed position which makes this more difficult.

2. Shoulder straps are fixed and difficult to maneuver - also the padding over the straps is only on the part that sits behind her - the straps still dig into the side of her neck and face if I don't put a cloth there. I finally bought some strap covers to remedy this but kind of felt annoyed at having to do that since we did pay $300 for this car seat. ***Added: Oh yeah, and it's really irritating that when you go to put the baby in the seat, the straps fall down into the seat. I try to pull them to side and sort of hang them over the edge but they usually fall back in, and then I have to put the baby in on top of the straps, and work my hands down around and behind the baby to dig out the straps. I don't know if all car seats are like this or not, but seriously - there has got to be a way to keep those straps out of the way while positioning the baby in the seat! I would gladly pay an extra $100 for a seat that offers this feature because I'm so irritated every single time we put her in the seat.

3. The 5 point harness is really tight - it's extremely difficult to loosen it, and so far I've really only been able to do that when the baby is not sitting in the seat. I like that it's safe, but right now we seem to have it on the very largest setting and it's extremely tight on our 12 pound baby. There is no way this will last to 30 pounds.

4. The angle of the seat is too upright - when my baby falls asleep, her head drops forward. This was even worse when we took the seat in a friend's car where the back seats are more of bucket style - then her head was falling forward while she was awake.

5. The fabric is already pilling at the bottom where her feet go. This doesn't bother me much, but for $300 this shouldn't be happening.

6. The sunshade doesn't provide much coverage. We live in a sunny place, and I'm constantly pulling out a muslin blanket or something to put over the car seat. It would be better if there was an option for the sunshade to pull all the way over. I looked online to see if Maxi Cosi makes an accessory for this purpose but I was unable to find anything. Again, not a huge issue but I thought I was buying a premium car seat for $300 and there are all these little things in addition to the big issue of size/depth.

6. I guess I should have avoided thecompany when I could not get them to respond to my questions about compatibility with stroller systems. I wanted to know in advance whether the car seat was compatible with the new Bugaboo Cameleon 3 and I couldn't get them to respond (contacted them through their Facebook page and also their website). Finally I contacted Bugaboo and they assured me that it was. We bought the adapters from Bugaboo and we are able to use the car seat with the stroller system, but the stroller will not fold if the adapters are on it. So that's another thing to take off and put on again if we have to fold it up to put it in the car. Again, it's not a huge issue but I thought I'd mention it in case you are interested in this car seat to use with a Bugaboo.

So for all of those reasons, I basically avoid taking my baby anywhere in the car because we hate the car seat so much. The bottom line is that this car seat does not work for us and we are in the market for a new one, after nearly 4 months of torture using this one. Several friends have recommended the Britax or the Orbit system, so we are going to look at those. I will be bringing my baby to try out the seat before we buy it.

***Update*** We managed to adjust the whole harness section of the car seat by moving some parts on the back. I did feel a bit silly at not having noticed this before, but in my defense, the car seat was the domain of Papa Bear and he didn't figure it out either. It was not straightforward and I could not find any instructional video on the Maxi Cosi website (seriously, how hard would it be to include?) and their user manual might as well have been written in Martian. But since we adjusted it, the car seat is MUCH better. I've therefore changed my review from one star to two stars. I still don't think it will last to 30 pounds, and it's still a pain to get her into the car seat, and I dread having to put her in it - once she's in it and we go somewhere, I dread taking her out of it because I know it will be such a hassle to put her back into it. THIS WORKS GREAT. It takes up the whole length of the tub, and almost the entire width, it sticks like crazy (we'll see if it'll ever come off when we're ready to move). The baby is comfy on it, and she doesn't slip around AT ALL. You can wash it with any cleaning products you use, and it won't come up. Now if only it came with seatbelts so she wouldn't try to stand :)

This is one of the best purchases I've made in baby products.

product_title: TY Beanie Boos 7 inch Sting Plush
review_body:
Our toddler loves bees, and she's been carrying around this little guy all day since she got him. She even takes him to bed- NO ONE goes to bed with her but her dolly. She's been sleeping with her dolly and the bee every night!

Just one thing- he didn't come with wings. I cut out some plain white fabric wings and sowed them on before giving her the bee.

He is also very machine washable and dryable- the fur doesn't even get matted. Put him in a pillowcase or a lingerie bag to keep the eyes from getting scratched.

product_title: Carters Easy Fit Jersey Cradle Fitted Sheet, Ecru (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I returned another product because it wasn't snug around the cradle pad. This one is snug and won't come loose. Much better! Also made of high quality fabric and is nicely constructed.

product_title: Pacimals: The Huggable Plush Pacifier , Janet the Giraffe
review_headline: Just got 4th one so we can keep a steady supply - she absolutely loves it!
review_body: Her favorite toy! She doesn't even use the pacifier part anymore now that she's a year old, but it has become her treasured security item.

product_title: Diono Radian RXT All-In-One Convertible Car Seat, Shadow
review_headline: I've tried them all!! THIS ONE IS THE BEST!!!!
review_body:
I never write reviews, but I'm taking the time to do this one b/c I've tried every car seat out there! I live in a small town and we are limited to Graco, Safety first and Britex car seats at the local Babies R Us. I didn't like any of those. I've order from Amazon the Clek Foonf, Recaro Proride, Cicco convertable, and the Combi convertable. The Diono Radian RXT is by far the best! Here's why...

-It reclines far enough back that my baby's head doesn't droop down when she falls asleep in the car.
-We have an SUV so it's hard to put the baby in with the car seats that have the bulky side. This one doesn't have the big bulky sides, so it's easier to slide her in and she doesn't hit her head on the top of the door as we put her in.
-It's compact and easy to take out for travel since it folds up.
-It will be the only car seat I will need to purchase b/c it will grow with the child.

Info on the other car seats we tried:

My next choice after this one is the Foonf, but it's super heavy and assembly was a big hassle. It too me forever to figure it out.

The Chicco convertible is great b/c you can vary the recline, but again, it had the big bulky sides which makes it hard to put her into the SUV. However, if you need something more compact, I highly recommend that one.

product_title: Munchkin Twisty Figure 8 Teether
review_body: Bought for my daughter when she was about 6 months old, and she still loves to play with this at almost 8 months. It holds her attention because you can bend and twist it to change the orientation. It does rattle a little, but it is VERY quiet, I wouldn't buy this if you are looking for a noisy toy. Would definitely buy again!

product_title: Bob Pre-2016 Single Infant Car Seat Adapter For Chicco
review_headline: My little one loves walks in his BOB
review_body: The attachment is easy to attach and remove while also adhering to the easy use of the car seat for my son. He absolutely loves going for walks in his BOB stroller at the park and around the neighborhood.

product_title: Recaro ProSPORT High Back Booster Car Seat - Hanna
review_headline: no complaints, dtr loves this carseat.
review_body:
First off, i did not buy this on amazon.I bought it from a store and got the Hanna style of this carseat.

It is easy to install and my 3.5 year old 40 inch tall dtr loves this carseat. She can climb into it very easily, she can actually clip herself into the 5 pt harness and all I need to do is tighten it. The straps do not get tangled.

It is easy to install, easy to change the height of the straps, and the handle on the top is wonderful.

Its not light, but that doesn't change anything for my review.

I have an 06 honda accord and it fits great in there.

My dtr is tall and she fits in this great, I would recommend this car seat to anyone.

product_title: Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim Baseball Infant Baby Hooded Bath Towel
review_body: I love hoodie towels and to have one with my favorite team oh yeah! Love using this at bath time!

It was only 12 bucks!

product_title: SwaddleDesigns SwaddleDuo Stripes and Little Chickies Duo

product_title: Safety 1st Heavenly Dreams Stars a Plenty Baby Mattress
review_body: Fits my Delta crib/changer combo exactly.  I also like that it is made with a stain resistant material, but doesn't feel too stiff.

product_title: Baby Einstein

review_body: i received my tray and it fits perfectly its really comfortable and it was what i expected its very usefull

product_title: NUK Orthodontic Bottle, 10 Ounce, 3 Count
review_headline: Great quality at a good price
review_body: My daughter rejected nine brands of bottles before accepting Nuks.  Thankfully, she didn't like the really expensive ones; stocking up on a bunch of these Nuk ones didn't break the bank.  The description isn't clear on this: the nipples that come with these bottles are the medium-flow ones.  Also, in terms of color, I got the "Boy" variety.  They're totally gender neutral. Well im not one to return items that i get over the internet so i fixed it myself ( safety pin did the trick)

review_body:
We like this mat because of the size. Our tub is large and although the mat seems as narrow as many, the length is longer than others. The only reason I gave this a 4 star is because it takes a few times to push the mat down to stay down.

I do like the knee pad, however at first I thought to myself "technically I could just roll up a towel," so at times our son will use it as a play toy in the tub. He likes to sit his rubber ducks on it. I have used it for it's real purpose and it's nice.

When we are all done with bath time, we stick the mat to the inside wall of our tub so it can dry off. Our tub is tall enough so the side does not sit on the bottom of the tub.

product_title: Baby Bottle Holder (Magenta)
review_body: for those times you can't hold both babies at once, this is a real lifesaver!  Highly recommend for parents with twins!

product_title: Angel Dear Blankie
review_body: My baby loves the fabric of this item.  Even I could see myself sleeping with it since it is so soft.

product_title: Wubbanub Infant Pacifier - Lion with satin mane

product_title: Graco FastAction Fold Click Connect LX Stroller

A few of my favorite features include dual cupholders for Mom and baby, the multi-position recline, large storage basket and smartphone caddy! Although I am not a runner by nature I do love to jog as well as talk long walks/hikes both on and off the trails in our neighborhood and I've never encountered any issues transition from dirt path to asphalt with this jogger! My old jogger was difficult to fold and cumbersome to pack into and take out of the car. I can easily fold this jogger with just one hand and lifting it into and out of my car is MUCH easier! Fantastic stroller, Graco!

product_title: Samsung Wireless Video Security Monitoring System (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
This is our second system, but not for the reasons you think! The first one didn't survive the mighty power of our little one's left arm. product_title: Vital Baby Toddler Straw Cup, 10 Ounce
review_body: We bought it because of the great reviews I read on amazon. Decided to ignore those who said it is hard to drink from thinking they just got the "lemon". Well... So you decide, do you really need this cup or not.

product_title: Munchkin 4 Pack Fresh Food Feeder
review_body: I fill them with some homemade fruit yogurt or mashed fruits and he loves that he can hold the grip and eat it himself.  Plus when they are frozen or cold he really enjoys the releif on his poor swollen gums during those painful teething times.

product_title: NUK Disney Winnie the Pooh 5 Ounces Learner Cup Silicone Spout, 6+ Months
review_body: Since the handles attach at the bottom of the cup it's so easy to line them up with the spout!!

product_title: Baby Deedee Sleep Nest Lite Baby Sleeping Bag

product_title: Alva Baby Double Rows of Snaps Cloth Diaper with Two Inserts
review_body:
I have been cloth diapering my infant for six months. I am an educated professional and invested hours into researching cloth diapering options and cloth diaper brands. I own several types of diapers, representing many brands. I purchased these because the price is much lower than rival brands. I compared the Alva diapers to my BumGenius pockets and Happy Heineys pockets, which are more expensive.

Cons:
1. They leak. Period. They outer material is does not contain moisture 100%. I never have leaks with my BGs and HHs, but consistently have leaks with these. Leaks occured even after I adjusted the snaps and triple checked the fit on my son.

2. The snaps are awkward. My son is in the 50 percentile for weight, so he's not an overly large or extremely scrawny kiddo. The snaps around the waist do not allow for a snug fit. The company needs to add a few more snaps to ensure a better fit.

Pros:
1. The diaper comes with two inserts.
2. The pocket fits 2-3 inserts for heavy wetters (my son isn't a heavy wetter, but I stuffed the diaper to see how many I could fit)
3. Lower price

Conclusion: Spend the extra $8-$10 diapers and purchase BumGenius or Happy Heineys. You won't encounter leaks and will have a much easier time fitting the diaper on your baby's bum. I always tell new moms to prioritize baby spending; splurge in 2-3 areas and cut back somewhere else. I bought more expensive diapers (BG All in Ones & Swaddlebees etc. ) and saved money by NOT purchasing fleece wipes. Instead, I collected old cotton t-shirts, cut them into large squares, and made my own wipes. If you identify 2-3 areas where you can DIY or simply do without (bottle warmers etc), you can free up extra funds to purchase better diapers.

review_headline: Would LOVE this stroller if I could change a few things.

For a slightly shorter couple, this is likely a 5-star stroller, however, my husband simply can’t stretch out as much. Perhaps if he were able to adjust the handle bar this wouldn’t be such a problem. We have a friend who is his exact height (6’5) and he hasn’t had any problems but his legs are much shorter proportionately. For me, the weight of the stroller has been something I’ve had to get used to. It’s a double workout to run with the stroller and I would suggest not going out for your first, post-baby run with the Bob.

On the upside, the stroller is incredibly sturdy and may be a smoother ride than our car (!). After struggling to get up on sidewalks with our great travel system and lightweight stroller, the Bob feels like an off road vehicle. Although we have only used this stroller on a track and on sidewalks, I have high hopes for an upcoming beach trip.

review_body:

We tried this cup and the very similar Zoli straw cup. I prefer this one for its larger size at a lower price, easier to clean (the Zoli left water cloudy after the cup was rinsed), and ease in putting the top on. The Zoli top screws on, but misthreads very easily which leaves you open to spills.

product_title: Summer Infant By Your Side Sleeper Portable Bedding (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Sturdy design but not without it's flaws
review_body:
I bought this for my newborn. My wife and I looked around on Amazon for a good co-sleeper, and came to the conclusion that this one was the best fit for our son.

Sadly, he doesn't like sleeping in it, because he needs lots of space, and he fusses if his arms or legs feel constrained. But I can speak for the construction of this product.

The quality of its production is fairly good. It is very sturdy, and pretty easy to assemble. The co-sleeper is big enough to handle a fairly large baby comfortably, and the mattress seems compliant to standard pack n play and crib mattresses (i.e. hard as hell!). And we didn't really notice a lingering smell on the product, which was nice.

However, there are a couple of problems I encountered with this product. First, The braces to prevent it from flipping over need to be screwed into the metal frame, and it was hell trying to get two of the four braces in! The screw threads in the bars themselves were very poorly drilled, and it took a huge amount of effort overcoming this (not least because the screws themselves had various bits of metal stuck between the threads - it was like they had been poorly machined). As a result I am not able to get two of the braces off, which is annoying. Second, the braces really should be a bit broader. When our son (who is an average-sized baby) rolled from his back onto his side the whole co-sleeper heaved and shifted on the bed.

Additionally, we haven't run into it ourselves, but I can see how the concern about how difficult it would be to pull an infant out of this co-sleeper for breast feeding.

I'm giving this product the benefit of the doubt and giving it 4 out of 5 stars. For less active and/or smaller infants I think it would work out alright. But beware of those screw threads and screws! Make sure they are clean and the screw threads are sharp before you start screwing in!

product_title: The First Years Ignite Stroller (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
My daughter has been very ill and unable to walk as far as she is normally able. We decided it was time to order a stroller to assitst with appointments, ect. I researched online and found several parents commented that this stroller fit their older child well. When it arrived we had her sit in it and discovered the seat is slightly tipped forward compelling her to use her feet on the foot rest to stay well seated in the stroller. Because we will be using this when she is tired, relying on her legs to hold her in was not a reasonable option. I thought we would be ok with the five-point harness holding her in, but it was too low for her shoulders by and inch and wouldn't buckle across her belly. She is 46" tall and weighs 43lbs.

We returned this stroller (great customer service through Amazon) and purchased a used Peg Perego at a local consignment store. Even used the Peg was $125, so if you are looking for something for a child this large who is truely tired you will have to accept spending a little more. The Peg was actually lighter than the ignite despite being larger.

I would strongly recommend going to a brick and mortar store to try a variety of strollers before committing to a purchase.

product_title: Kolcraft Pediatric 2000 Mattress
review_headline: Soon enough tore on both sides.
review_body:
Within a few months of use the plastic coating on this mattress began to tear. My son obviously always slept with a sheet, never had toys or even bottles in his crib, and I always wiped clean after accidents.

I turned the mattress over once the tear got long. Then in a few months...tear on that side. I bought a mattress protector but the tears keep on getting bigger. I've used duct tape.

This morning I noticed there is a supposed ten year warranty; as, even though my son is about to switch to a bed, I am afraid of health issues because of the tears and thought of buying a new crib mattress for the several moths he'll still be in his crib.. But when I go on the company's website to learn how to go about it, none of the links work...I can't even get a phone number.
My guess is that the warranty won't wind up being anything useful anyway.

In conclusion, I would look elsewhere for a crib mattress...and unfortunately perhaps buy a protector, even though mattresses like this one are supposedly watrproof.

review_headline: Kicking myself for not buying it sooner
review_body:
My only regret about buying this bag is that I didn't get it for my first kid. I needed something to use as a travel bassinet while we were moving coast-to-coast. Since we were flying, a regular travel crib was less useful. It's a little bulky and heavy, but the outside pockets are brilliant - no pawing through an oversized diaper bag. The pockets remain completely usable even as the bassinet is in use. The changing pad is huge, taking up an entire large pocket, so in the interest of space I just took disposable changing pads with me. The magnetic wipes holder is a neat idea, but didn't fit the opening on my pack of wipes. It may work fine with other brands. The bassinet portion will work for a baby up to 29\\" and 20 lbs. It doesn't seem amazingly comfortable, but it's for short term use.

For the record, I can fit 6 of each size 2 and 5 diapers, travel pack of wipes, 4 disposable changing pads, roll of diaper disposal bags, 2 complete changes of clothes for a 2 year old, 4 complete changes for a 4 month old, 4 burp cloths, small blanket, rattle, breast pads, and sanitizing wipes, with a little room left.

review_body: This pillow was purchased with high hopes of living up to its reviews, however, it only lived up to the bad ones. I have used it three times and each time, have had the worst sleep and woke up covered in sweat, with the worst tension headache. At first, pillow has too much padding for head support but after 20 minutes, the padding goes flat and your left without proper neck support. I'm short, 5'3" and the pillow is too short to provide ankle support which alters the placement of my hips and I wake up cracking and popping in all my lower joints and I'm only 26! review_body:
This system was not what I expected it to be. First, when we got it home and opened the box, it's in pieces and needs assembling. Second, once it's assembled, it's HUGE! The stroller is way to big when it folds down. I had to watch a video on youtube to figure out how to fold it down. It was very frustrating. The front wheel is a headache and our wheel detached while baby was in it! The speakers are really no big deal. I don't even see myself using them if I'm out for a walk because it would bother others around me. (Something I didn't think of when I saw them at first.)

Now the car seat: it's big and heavy. The handle is a pain to lower because the buttons are so difficult to push in. Once again, I had to watch to a video on youtube on how to adjust the straps!

This is my 5th child and I know very well how strollers and carseats work. This one is a total pain. I wish I had done more research on it but I didn't and now I regret my purchase.

It does have some nice features once you get it all figured out but getting there is frustrating and just not worth the time. Spend a little more and get something better.

product_title: Fisher-Price Luv U Zoo Jumperoo
review_body:
Pros:
Safety - Baby can jump all over the place and doesn't hit the side bars holding it up; no fear that baby will fall out. Safer than door jumpers which I've heard can cause hip dysplasia and other hip problems in babies.
Adjustable Height - This is a great feature and it's easy to use
Set Up - Setting it up only took 5 or 6 minutes - Very simple- didn't need the instructions
Baby Appeal- Baby LOVES this jumper, particularly trying to grab the hanging monkey and spinning the plastic alligator toy. The music/sound effects aren't terribly interesting to the baby, but perhaps yours will like them. In either case, it's definitely gotten plenty of use.

Cons
Durability - Although the jumper itself will probably last indefinitely, the little hanging toys are drooping significantly after a few months of on and off use. The plastic leaf has a plastic joint that pops into the frame of the bouncer, and that joint wears out rather quickly, particularly if your baby can reach the hippo and monkey and likes to grab them.

Other:
The jumper takes up more space than a lot of activity centers I've seen for baby's. That didn't really matter in this case, but if you have very limited space, consider a stationary activity center that baby sits in.

review_body:
My 7 month old son loves this cup. We started him on it when he started eating solid foods at 6 months. He has never taken a bottle, but he does really well with this cup. It has arrows on the side that you are supposed to line up with an arrow on the lid for it to be 100% leak proof and it is practically impossible. If you do get it in those arrows, good luck getting the lid back off!! However, even when I can't get it screwed all the way on to that point, I haven't had any issues with it leaking even though my son slams it on his high chair repeatedly and throws it on the ground. The handles are very easy for him to hold and he likes to chew on the spout (even though the directions say not to let them chew on it). Overall, great cup!

product_title: Lansinoh mOmma Feeding Bottle, 5 Oz, 1 Count (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: If your EBF baby refuses a bottle, try this one first!
review_body:
This is my first Amazon product review--the Lansinoh mOmma worked so well under desperate circumstances that I felt compelled to let other parents know.

Our exclusively breastfed 11-week-old daughter took to the Lansinoh mOmma with two weeks to spare before I had to go back to work. We had tried several different standard, wide-neck \\"breastfeeding\\", and orthodontic silicone nipples (Tommee Tippee, Comotomo, Avent Natural, Breastflow, Nuk, and Dr. Brown's). She latched on the mOmma right away--she took 2 oz. with her first feeding (some fussing), 3 oz. with her second feeding (minimal fussing), and 4 oz with her third feeding (no fussing, and even fell asleep as she would at my breast!).

We first introduced a bottle at 5 weeks, but the most she would take from the first two bottles we tried (Tommee Tippee and Avent) was 1 oz. We wish we had tried the mOmma first, as it would have saved us both the cost of assembling a bottle 'collection' and the worry that feeding would be difficult for her caregivers.

We observed two problems that the above mentioned silicone nipples posed for our baby: 1) The nipple would slide around in her mouth; or 2) The nipple was so long that she would gag on it. Both prevented her from latching properly. I should mention that we did not try latex nipples--some parents on the Nuk bottle reviews cited success with this as softer and grippier, and it would have been our next try had the mOmma not worked.

The three features that distinguishes the mOmma from other bottles is 1) the shorter and smaller nipple which gently slopes to a wide base; 2) the matte area around the base of the nipple which encourages proper latching; and 3) the short, round bottle shape. We observed that our baby did not gag on this nipple like other longer and wider ones, and that the matte part of the silicone allowed her lips to grip on to the base and prevent the nipple from sliding around. The bulbous bottle shape allows myhusband to get a good angle and close hold for feeding.

We also found mOmma's air vent system to work well and prevent excess gas, unlike the Nuk orthodontic nipple bottle (the second best bottle she took to). The silicone nipple is soft (unlike the Tommee Tippee, Avent Natural, and Comotomo) and so far seems durable. It truly has a slow-flow nipple (unlike the Avent Natural which caused our daughter to cough and gag)--when you hold it upside down, it either doesn't drip or drips sparingly. The wide-mouth bottle shape is easy to clean--you don't need a bottle brush, just a sponge cut into 1/4 and dishwashing soap of your choice.

Some critics here have complained about the lip near the bottle thread preventing all the milk from entering the tip, leading to waste. While we agree that the lip is annoying and could be redesigned a la Comotomo's seamless shape, my husband found that it was not difficult to unlatch and then relatch her to get all the milk into the nipple reservoir. Other critics have cited that it is difficult to measure ounces on the bottle. While it is true that the ounce marks are clear and could be more visible, I use my Ameda pump storage bottles to measure ounces--it has never been a problem. A third criticism I've read is that the bottle shape does not fit some bottle warmers--we use the Kiinde Kozii and it fits the mOmma with no problem. If the mOmma doesn't fit one's existing bottle warmer, one could use either pump bottles or breastmilk storage bags and transfer it into the mOmma.

These minor drawbacks aside, given that we were starting to make plans to have a caregiver spoon or dropper-feed her when I returned to work and see a Lactation Consultant for help, we are THRILLED overall with the mOmma and would highly recommend it to other 'panicked' parents. Give this innovative bottle a try early on!

product_title: NUK Advanced Dry Disposable Nursing Pads, 36-Count (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: So far the best I've found
review_body: I have an oversupply, so absorbent pads are a must, and washable ones leak through my clothing.  The pads I liked with my first child were discontinued, so I've been through pretty much every brand out there looking for a replacement, and these are the best I've found.  They slip in easily and keep their structure better than the other kinds (which fold up on you, especially if they get shoved out of the way during a feeding), they're absorbent without getting stinky, they wick moisture pretty well, and best of all, they don't crinkle.  The other brands are all backed by a very loud, crinkly material that sounds like you've got a diaper in your bra if you move around a lot, and more importantly, sounds exactly like the crinkly part of baby toys, so my infant goes for the pads like a magnet and tries to play with them, eat them, etc.  These are silent.  My only negatives with these are that they are a little on the scratchy side (not awful, just not super comfortable), and they don't come individually wrapped - if I remember to put them in before I leave the house, that's fine, but I like to keep an extra pair in my purse or car in case I forget, and I can't do that with these easily.  It's a minor quibble, though, and better in terms of waste, so it's not a big deal.  Other brands I've tried: Medela, Lansinoh, Nuk/Gerber thin pads and multiple other varieties, Tommee Tippee, and a generic (maybe Target brand?).  None of them are as good as these for night wearing or, if you leak a lot like I do, for daily use.

product_title: Leachco Podster Sling-Style Infant Seat Lounger
review_body:
My husband bought two of these shortly after the birth of our twins. I admit, I scoffed ... we had the pack n play, why would we need these?

That lasted all of a month, when the twins started (inadvertently) rolling into each other in the pack n play and waking each other up. The solution? Two podsters fit side by side in the pack n play (and a standard size co-sleeper). The design cradles the baby, while also elevating them a little, a position that helped reduce spit up after feedings. It also raised them up high enough that I could see them in the pack n play without having to go over and peek in. Granted, once they really started wiggling and moving about, that wasn't safe, but I still use them almost daily (the twins are now eight months old) as cushions behind them while they learn to sit up. One of them loves to get up on his knees, put his arms in the seat pocket, and scoot all over the floors. I foresee these being used until the twins simply get too big to fit.

They've gotten spit up on and drooled all over, and I admit, I haven't wanted the challenge of taking the cover off (well, really the challenge of getting it back on). But a damp cloth or sponge is generally sufficient for most of the messes.

All in all, I can't recommend the podster enough!

You could always let the baby rest in the bassinet prior to changing, but I didn't like the idea of pulling the changing table down on top of where my baby was lying so I always held her pror to changing. And, the middle compartment is roomy enough to tuck away all your diaper changing essentials. My favorite features is the stroller straps. It makes it so easy to get at your stuff!

product_title: JJ Cole Caprice Diaper Bag, Shadow, Black and Grey
review_body:
For about 2 years I was using a diaper bag I pretty much hated. It was the deep, narrow kind of messenger bag that things always got lost in and there was never enough room. What I wanted: a more purse-like bag with a wide body to easily locate things, insulated pockets for sippy cups, a somewhat neutral design (so my husband wouldn't totally refuse to carry it to the bathroom when he changes our daughter), and the option of a messenger strap. The JJ Cole Black & Grey Caprice Diaper Bag fits the bill. I almost went with the Skip Hop Black Dot Studio Diaper Bag, in fact was all set to purchase when I realized it didn't have the extra messenger/shoulder strap. I was pretty bummed bc (at the time) I didn't think the Caprice was as nice looking as the Studio, but I'm so glad I took that leap of faith! I'll also post some pictures so it's easier for others to see how it really looks.

Some things to note:
1. an insulated pocket is a huge deal for us. My daughter loves milk and I feel milk MUST be cooled if we're out and about all day. I really wanted a zippered insulated pocket, but no one seems to have that. I thought I would have to buy a separate cooler, but have been pleasantly surprised with the functionality of these. Each insulated pocket fits 2 of her sippy cups (First Years/Playtex/etc) AND a small gel freeze pack! So this could easily hold 2-3 regular size bottles or 2 wide bottles in each pocket.

2. The purse-like shoulder straps are a little short, so it can be a little tight to just throw over your shoulder. Also, one strap will sometimes slip off especially if the main bag is not zippered bc they're rounded and not really grippy. This happens more if I'm in a rush, but the whole bag doesn't fall, just one strap. Neither of these issues is something that would cause me to look for something else though.

3. The bottom front 2 pockets do not offer a lot of space. The big zippered bottom pocket on the front isdesigned to be like Mom's wallet with slots for credit cards and a cell phone. It doesn't really allow for anything bulky. I just use it for coupons and keep my wallet in another pocket. The small zippered pocket on top of that is TINY! I can put a couple pens, a very small comb and a few clips for my daughter there. It's functional, but not big.

4. The main zippered portion is HUGE! (for what I'm used to anyway) There are 4 stretchy pockets. I do: 1. diapers, 2. wipes and bags, 3. snacks, and 4. toys. The rest of the bag I'm able to stuff several changes of clothes, etc if needed.

5. the back pocket has no zipper or Velcro. We use it for the companion changing pad and some magazines.

Hope some of these facts answer some questions! I'll try to upload some pictures too.

***UPDATE March 1, 2014:
I still love this bag! My daughter is now fully potty trained and has been for some time, but I continue to use this bag for every outing with or without her. There are no signs of staining, fading, or wear. I'm impressed and still satisfied!

It is very lightweight and comfortable. Baby can be worn facing you or facing outward, and there aren't any adjustments that need to happen to the carrier once it is sized to you and baby. My husband is much larger than I am, and I was afraid it would be difficult to adjust from one to the other, but it is really easy to adjust if you need to.

I live in a warm climate, so I'm glad we got the mesh. It is very breathable and doesn't make my son sweat like his carseat does. It is also very easy to clean (machine washable and air dry).

review_headline: Awesome High Chair!!!- SimpleSwitch vs. Contempo
review_body:

Not only am I saving money with this model (I am like to get the best deal possible still good quality), but it does a great job being a high chair ;).

I read reviews for the Contempo that some people had complaints about the Contempo's seat sides pinching their kids' legs and also the removable tray pinching arms when leaning on it for feeding. I never heard any of that with the SimpleSwitch, so decided to go for it. There is no way that your kids or you could ever get pinched in the SSwitch's chair/booster seat.

I realize that the Switch can't be collapsed in 2 seconds like the Contempo video showed, but seriously who has the time to continuously put the high chair away between feedings...? Does not take up much room.

I love that I am able to put the tray table on and off with only one hand. Super easy.

Loving the pattern on the Pasadena because it's gender neutral and has a gray tray. No swatch of green as showed in the pattern swatch photo- Just gray all over and patterned seat cover. Everything is super easy to wash. I'm all about it.

Assembly took 3 minutes- no problems.

product_title: Sassy Disposable Scented Diaper Sacks
review_headline: Best diaper disposal bag - 200ct box lasted me 6 months!
review_body: I tried about 6 different diaper disposal bags on the market with my surprise baby who is now 18 months old.  13 years ago, I got sucked into the Diaper Genie system for her older brother - what a pain to empty and replace the roll, and so expensive.  Went to a simpler diaper disposal pail system with her older sister 11 years ago that used standard tall kitchen bags, much easier and cheaper but still a big smelly plastic bin in the baby room.  So this time around, much older and maybe a bit wiser, I just walk all her diapers out to the kitchen trash which, in a family of 5, goes out at least every other day.  Wet diapers just get wrapped on themselves and tossed.  #2s, of which this baby girl is a champ, get bagged, and I have tried a number of brands because she has been the smelliest and most prolific #2 producer of my 3 babies.  The best and thickest diaper disposal bags that I've tried are the Munchkin bags that come on a roll.  The roll fits in Munchkin's small plastic dispenser that hangs on your diaper bag handle.  I still use the Munchkin bags in my diaper bag because the dispenser is great, and so are the bags.  Even if I get stuck having to carry a smelly diaper in one of the Munchkin bags for a bit before I find a trash can, it doesn't smell up the other items in my diaper bag.  Same with a smelly outfit from a blow-out that needs to go home to be washed.  But the Munchkins bags are way more expensive than these Sassy bags which are almost as thick and have a similar baby powder scent.  The 200-ct box is awesome.  If your baby has outgrown the newborn stage, and is averaging one dirty diaper a day, you will easily get 6 months from a box of these.  I have on occasion double-bagged a really smelly diaper or had to take out our kitchen trash right away because of a really nasty diaper, but both situations have been really rare.  These bags contain the odor very well.  Another hint... I put one of the large 6\\" diameter Arm & Hammer deodorizing air fresheners with baking soda at the bottom of my kitchen trash can under the trash bag - works great!  Do yourself and your baby a favor - keep those diaper smells from accumulating in a nursery diaper pail and save yourself the hassle of the diaper systems, and just keep these disposal bags near your diaper wipes for the 1 or 2 dirty diapers a day.  You'll be amazed how much simpler life is!  :-)

product_title: Pura Kiki 11 Oz / 325 Ml Stainless Steel Sippy Cup With Silicone Xl Sipper Spout & Sleeve, (plastic Free, Nontoxic Certified, Bpa Free)
review_body:
I have tried several other brands of stainless steel sippy cups for my children and this one is my favorite so far. My favorite feature of this Pura bottle is probably that it is 100% plastic free (I have yet to find another sippy that is). The entire bottle and cap are stainless steel and the nipple and bottle cover are composed of pure silicone.

The silicone spout is well designed and does not leak when held upside down but liquid still comes out fairly easily when sucked on so your little one won't have to work too hard to stay hydrated. I found with other brands that I tried that their no leak feature made it very difficult to get any liquid out, and although they usually break in with a bit with use, they still give me a headache to try and drink out of. With one brand, Thermos Foogo, I have resorted to removing the no leak valve altogether (and I am very glad that they designed it to be removable because otherwise my kids wouldn't use them at all).

Some people reported that the metal caps on their Pura bottles have sharp edges but I haven't found that to be the case with the two that I have.

Overall I am happy with these bottles and I highly recommend them.

---- UPDATE 2/23/14 ----

After having had these cups for over a year we still love them and they are still the favorite of my two kids (2.5 years and 11 months). They have held up well to abuse, and multiple drops on tile floors, and only have a few dents to show for it (do keep in mind that we do not use the protective silicone sleeves). One thing that I have noticed however is that over time the bottle nipples do begin to leak (but it is still fairly minimal compared to \\"free-flowing\\" sippy cups). If the leaking becomes a problem for you replacing the nipple on a regular basis (probably once every 6-8 months I'd guess) would keep the leaking at bay.

I still highly recommend this product and I hope my review is helpful to you.

product_title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump [Model - 67060]
review_headline: Okay but not worth the extra cost
review_body:
I used a pump in style for over a year with my first child and was given this pump as a loaner in order to give feedback for my hospital lactation consultant to provide a review for her pumping class. I would not have spent the extra money on this pump myself and I'm glad I didn't. I have been using this pump for almost a year now. I use this one when at home and use a hospital grade Symphony while at work. I have also recently tried the new Lansinoh Affinity Pro.

Pros:
Small/compact/lightweight
Portable - the rechargeable battery feature is actually pretty nice and I didn't notice a difference in suction compared to the power when plugged in. I didn't use the big carry bag that came with it, but instead used a smaller medela bag designed for transporting/storing your pumped milk.
Timer - I actually liked this feature a lot. I liked being able to look at the pump and know exactly how long I had been pumping.
Battery - great for portability and actually lasts quite a while between charges.

Cons:
Parts - too many pieces to take apart and clean. the design of the freestyle compared to the PIS makes it impossible for milk to get backed up into the tubing. this was achieved by adding the membrane and cap on the back of the connector instead of the valve and membrane inside the bottle under the connector as in the PIS. Great in theory, but I never had a problem with milk backing up into the tubing in the PIS and I find the new membrane and cap annoying to take apart and clean and find that I was constantly re-snapping the cap while pumping in order to maintain suction.
Tubing - this pump has a split design as compared to the PIS having separate tubes for each side. so when using as a single pump, you simply plug one end into the holding hole to maintain suction. However, when using as a double pump, the suction is then split between the 2 sides and there is a loss of suction power noticed.
Flanges - thesoft sided flanges that came with the pump will tear you up! Again, good in theory, soft should be more comfortable, but they actually end up causing too much friction on the skin and end up hurting. I used the standard hard side medela flanges and had no issues. They are readily available at most stores to buy individually.
Suction - Very Finicky! Everything has to be placed exactly right to get the suction right. As I mentioned before, I found the cap and membrane to be a nuisance and was constantly snapping and re-snapping the cap during a pumping session to get the suction. You have the ability to change suction levels from 1-9.
Noise - louder than the PIS. more of a mechanical sound than a soft \\"swooshing\\" sound. but not too loud. Worse than the PIS & Symphony but bettet than the Affinity Pro.

Other features:
Hands free accessories - ridiculously cumbersome! A snap on strap attachment that clips to the top and bottom of your nursing bra....difficult to get adjusted just right and adds a lot of prep time to setting up to pump. Better off getting a nice hands free bra like the Simple Wishes or cutting a couple holes in the front of your own bra!
Memory/Programming feature - designed to remember your preferences for letdown phase and expression phase. Simply adjust the timing of going into expression phase and how you like to adjust the suction level and hit the programming button and next time all you have to do is hit the one button and it will repeat that program automatically. Once again, great in theory, but not very useful. Pumping day to day and hour to hour changes, and how your body reacts and how much time it takes for a let down to happen or how much suction you need will vary. I found it easier to just manually hit the expression button when I felt a let down each time and to adjust the suction level as needed. An unnecessary feature that added to the increased cost I'm sure.

Bottom line - nice pump but the extra features are not necessary so not really worth the extra cost.

product_title: Skip Hop Dunck Stacking Bath Toys, Pink
review_headline: Great for baby, Great for mom
review_body:
I ordered this set for my 8 month old because I do not like the traditional bath toys that have the little holes in them. The bath ducky that is labelled as a "squirter" or "squeaker" toy can get water inside and then can grow mold. I do routinely clean the bath toys, but it seemed inevitable that after a while I would see little spots of mold forming inside the toy. I do not want to risk my baby sucking moldy water out of the little holes in those toys.

These ducks are bright and colorful, easy for little hands to play with and have many possible uses.

My baby likes to chew on them right now (at 10 months old everything still goes into the mouth) and they have the perfect rounded shape on the duck bill and tail for her to do that. There are no sharp or rough edges to worry about.

They are also nicely used as cups for rinsing her hair and water can be poured from the end (duck bill) or the side to give you either a narrow stream or wide stream of water. The shape also makes it easy to line it up keep it close to the forehead and pour without dumping water down her face (similar to the cups specifically designed for that purpose).

We often hold one duck higher than the others and make a flowing water fountain from one to the next and then into the water. She loves to try to "catch" the water as it is poured out.

They are easy to clean and stack nicely for saving space. I'm sure we will continue to play with this set for a very long time!!

product_title: Graco Silhouette Pack 'N Play Playard with Bassinet and Changer, Rittenhouse (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
We purchased this pack n' Play mainly for the time our son shares our room. A few people wanted to talk me out of buying this one since, as they said, we would not need the bassinet or changing table, but man are they wrong! We use the changing table all the time. it is of a great size, and it is higher than general changing tables, so for taller people much easier on the back.

The bassinet is a great addition and our son slept in it since the day we brought him home from the hospital. The 'mattress' is very hard, so in addition we purchased the Eddie Bauer Velboa Play Yard Sheet. It is a perfect fit and makes the mattress a lot softer and cozier. We also purchased the Waterproof portable crib utility pad 27x36 as a protection and this also is a great fit!!

Our son now sleeps in his own crib, but we still use the changing table all the time.

It is true that this model is on the bigger side and does not fit through regular doorways, but it is so easy to assemble and disassemble that this, in my opinion, should not be a reason not to purchase this Pack n' play.

- Sandra

product_title: The Door Guardian Childproofing Lock Colors: White
review_headline: Best Door Security for Your Grandma
review_body: Easy to install, easy to use.  Keeps little ones inside, keeps the bad guys outside.  I have installed this on my daughters doors and my mothers and on my daughters girlfriends house and apartment doors.  It has made every one of them feel more secure.  I would recommend these Door Gaurdians to every one.  ( Note install them above shoulder height and or below the door handle, it will make it harder for any potential intruder to put leverage on the door to break in.) Measure carefully. Dry fit them in the closed position so that the rubber door protector just closes on the door.  Carefully mark with a pencil the best fit location.  Open the door, place the Gaurdian in the jamb. Mark the holes that you are going to fasten it with.  Grab an drill and bore an 1/8\\" pilot hole for each screw about 1\\" in depth.  (The screws are about 3 1/2\\" long and you dont want to try to hand twist these screws in.  You could split the wood if the wood is old hardwoods.)  Also the screws are thick heavy duty and your wrist may not be that strong. Once they are installed you will sleep better at night.

product_title: Emily 2-in-1 Mini Crib and Twin Bed with Complete Mini Mattress with Hypoallergenic Waterproof Cover
review_body:
I bought this for my daughter, who has very limited space. The price is comparable to the mini cribs available locally. In my opinion the DaVinci crib seems to be better quality & looks a lot nicer! Shipping was quick (& free - THANK YOU AMAZON!!!) & assembly wasn't too bad - once we figured out which screws went where. The directions - not so great. We finally resorted to the 'whole' drawing on the last page & figured it out from there on our own. But there's not much to it & with a little common sense & patience I think anyone can handle the assembly.
The finished crib is super cute. The Espresso color perfectly matched my daughter's 'cherry' furniture. The mattress pad included, as many have stated, is NOT a real mattress. It is about a 1" foam pad that is covered in a waterproof plastic, but it works just fine for now. She may decide to purchase a regular mini crib mattress when baby gets larger.
All in all, we are very satisfied with the crib as well as the purchasing experience. I definitely recommend this crib!

product_title: Pognae 100% Cotton Soft Structured, Ergonomic Baby Carrier w/ Mesh Cooling Vent, Sleeping Hood and Headrest
review_body:
I have a moby and love it, but was looking for something more substantial as my little guy is 10 months and 20lbs now.
It is easy enough to get on and off by myself in the forward position, I needed assistance to get him off in the back carry position, though, I'm sure if I practice we can get it.

My baby loves to chew on the straps while seated in the carrier (I'll have to do somehting about that as they get soggy-gross!).
My baby loves being in it and it was a good price. It was between this, the ergo and the olives and applesauce carriers for us. This one won because the price was right! I'm glad we got it, and I would absolutely recomend it to a friend, infact, I already have.

product_title: Bumbleride Indie Stroller
review_body:
We had had our Bumbleride Indie for a few months now and am so far very impressed. I live very close to the beach, so wanted to get a stroller that I could take easily on the sand, and other similar terrain. After doing extensive research I decided to go with the Bumbleride Indie and am very happy I did!! For an all terrain, jogging stroller, the Indie is actually quiet light and SOOOO easy to maneuver. I can easily push the pram with one hand even with my toddler weighing almost 34 pounds in the seat. He loves riding in it and insists every time I say we are going for a walk that we take the stroller..lol...he jumps right in and doesn't budge. We recently went for a stroll along the beach and it handled very nicely on the compact sand nearer the water. The air filled tires are great and the suspension superb. The canopy is huge and offers more than substantial coverage from the elements. The adjustable handle is very nice and very comfortable. My 3 year old loves being able to move the handle down so he can push his brother. The foot break is very easy to put on and off and the stroller folds down very nicely. I can get it easily in and out of our Honda Odyssey and removing the back wheels makes it even more compact. Weighing only 20 pounds is awesome for such a full range stroller.

The ONLY complaint i have is the recline feature. The strap can get very sticky and makes it a pain sometimes to lower the seat back. I do however love how with adjustable foot rest and full recline of the seat, the stroller basically offers a bassinet environment without having to purchase additional items. I still give the stroller 5 stars though as all the other great feature outweigh this one downfall. It is definitely worth the price and the new changes that were made in the 2013 make it even better!!!

product_title: Bloom Alma Papa Modern Folding 3-in-1 Convertible Crib in Frosted Grey
review_body:
Following extensive research on cribs my husband and I decided to purchase 2 Alma Papa cribs. Our main concern was choosing a crib that would meet the highest safety qualifications, and we were hoping to also find a crib that would fit nicely into our home as well. The Alma Papa seemed to fit the bill. Bloom touts the safety of all of its cribs noting that they have low voc baby safe finishes, formaldehyde-free adhesives and are mdf-free as well. They offer an organic mattress as a separate purchase as well. The cribs are made in Vietnam, as opposed to China, also a plus in our book. Additionally, we were really impressed with the design, a crib that would work well in an environment with more limited space, and which had a low profile overall.

When we received the cribs my husband quickly set to work assembling them. And this is where our problems began.

The first thing my husband noticed was that the cribs are, as he described it, quickly slapped together with absolutely no attention to detail and a complete lack of consistency in product quality. We should know, we purchased TWO. One of the cribs was so poorly constructed that my husband had to force it to even get it together. The main problem was that there was paint globbed into the areas where the crib connects and the slots where the crib is supposed to come together were also misaligned. Both cribs had defects in workmanship. This included parts of the crib that the manufacturer did not even bother to paint. And on each crib there were differing parts which were lacking in paint. Some of the wooden pegs that attach various parts of the crib were flat, as opposed to rounded as they should have been, as though they had been sawed off. A bit hard to assemble a crib with sawed off bits. Additionally, once the cribs were assembled, they had a intense odor that was so strong it gave me an IMMEDIATE headache. I question the safety of any crib for any infant that causes an ADULT to get a headache of that magnitude. Low-VOC indeed.

When we complained about the smell we were told that it would go away within 48 hours. Not so. Within 48 hours the smell was just as strong. This was even after we moved the cribs into our home office and closed the doors and opened all the windows and turned on a fan. We have left the cribs in the aforementioned environment for almost a month now and guess what, they still stink!

We called a relative of mine who is a high end home builder who does all of the custom woodworking himself. He said that the cribs are definitely off-gassing and that they need to be put in a high temperature environment where they can off-gas more quickly. And this is a low-VOC product that is supposed to be safe?

We were told by the sales people where we purchased the crib that the fact that the cribs are low-VOC means that they are not coated in substances that hide the smells that off-gas over time. I really question this. There is no way that any rational, sane person would put their child in a crib that smells this horrible, for this length of time no matter what the claim about safety. As I said, a crib that induces a headache in an adult cannot be safe for a child. All this smell indicates is that Bloom's cribs off-gas just like nearly everyone else's apparently, except with Bloom you can actually smell it, and the smell is horrible!

We contacted the vendor from whom we purchased the cribs, as well as Bloom directly. Bloom scolded my husband for calling saying that they preferred not to speak with him and that he go through the vendor. He has called Bloom since and they reluctantly will allow him to bend their ear.

Since the cribs continued to smell horribly, we were told that 2 new cribs would be shipped to us and that before they were shipped they would be checked for any odor as well as to ensure there were no defects in workmanship as seen in the first 2 cribs.

Guess what? We received the 2nd two cribs, and they are WORSE than the first two. They smell just as horribly and they have worse defects in workmanship to boot. My husband said there is absolutely no way they checked on the product odor and quality before they shipped them out and I agree. You would think that a company with complaints like this would want to make sure that the next two cribs they sent would be double and triple checked to make sure they were up to snuff. Not only did Bloom not check the 2nd shipment over to make sure it was perfect, the 2 new cribs were from the EXACT SAME lot as the first two. As my husband says, how they thought they would achieve a different result is ridiculous.

Again we contacted our vendor who has has yet to hear from Bloom and it has been well over a week. So, here we sit, with 4 cribs that stink and have terrible workmanship, nearly 4 weeks after the first 2 arrived with no great solution in sight.

As an aside, we have a crib in our home that we love, but is colossal in size, and is the reason that we were looking for a more space saving alternative for other uses. We love that crib. We have never had any smell or workmanship issues with it either. It is made in the USA. Maybe that's the key!

It should be noted, we also purchased the Bloom Fresco high chair, which we actually love, but ultimately we find it difficult to endorse a company that has caused us so many headaches, literally and figuratively, in relation to the cribs. For cribs that are quite expensive, well over $1000 each, (if you purchase the crib, toddler rails, organic mattress, organic sheets, etc.) we expected better workmanship and attention to detail.s.
