product_title: Combi Cabria DX Lightweight Stroller, Flat Iron (Discontinued by Manufacturer) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Cons:
1. folding it down and carrying it is awkward if you don't have both hands available. Sure it has a carrying strap but it still super awkward.
2. Having to lock the front wheels before folding it down kind of sucks. But I just kind of got used to doing it. I tried just skipping that for a while and it kind of messed up one of the back wheels I think.
3. This might have just been mine, but the waist straps were put on backwards so they are nearly impossible to adjust.
4. EXTREMELY small basket. Like I can cram my sweater down there and not much else.
5. Probably the worst cupholder ever. I can't put any drinks in it because it hits the handle. Wth.

Pros:
1. It rolls pretty smoothly. Works best on sidewalks. Not so much on grass or super slick surfaces.
2. It's comfortable for my son, and he loves it much more than his other stroller (an umbrella)!
3. It takes up little room in my trunk.
4. I like the storage pockets and the oversized canopy is AWESOME. LOVE it. Biggest canopy I've ever seen on a stroller.

Overall, I don't think I'd go with this stroller again though. I'd look for something more versatile (like the city mini) and with a bigger basket.

product_title: Luna Bean Deluxe 3D Prints Baby Casting Kit
review_body:
This mold kit has an incredible ability to capture even finest details.
If you don't mind hunting for a perfect moment when your baby is very still, this mold can capture a truly phenomenal 3D memory that is absolutely adorable to see and have for years to come.

We did one pass at it with baby in not the calmest of the moods and some of the features we observed are truly amazingly accurate and extremely easy to mold. The actual kit and instructions are excellent overall.
Especially after doing a couple of samples, getting a hang of it takes no time.
The mold mixture is superb. It almost makes you want to play around capturing all kinds of stuff. It starts to harden in about 30 seconds and it takes about 1.5 minutes of waiting time before you can pull baby's hand or foot out of it.
It is definitely important for baby to be in deep sleep and quite knocked out so it's not moving its fingers or toes.

Overall the kit is excellent and I can't wait to give it another shot. The best time to do this is probably very late at night when the baby is exhausted or when it sleeps best/deepest. At that point it would be very easy to do.

I would highly recommend this kit and will definitely purchase one again for its completeness, ease of use and detail accuracy. It's so much fun to see the finished cast.
Way cool!

review_headline: Only need one for a Maclaren Twin Triumph
review_body:
I have a Maclaren Twin Triumph stroller and am very disappointed with the sunshade, which is small and extremely flimsy. We are going to Disney World and I needed something that would provide more coverage, especially for my infant daughter who is still too little for sunblock. This should fit the bill.

This sunshade needs to be tied to the stroller handles, so for the Twin Triumph it is really only possible to use one \\"Protect a Bub.\\" I think we will be fine with one since it is very large and seemed to provide good coverage when I tested it in my living room, but I wanted to point that out.

Note that the manufacturer says that the stroller will fold with the sunshade on. It will, but the Twin Triumph cannot be fully collapsed and secured in the \\"locked\\" position with the sunshade attached. That will mean a fair amount of tying and untying, which would be annoying to do on a regular basis but is fine for a vacation.

product_title: 4Moms Green Jack MamaRoo SILVER PLUSH Baby Bouncer Rocker Seat
review_headline: A Lot to Like, Falls Short in Some Areas
review_body:
~BACKGROUND~
I purchased the Classic Silver version of this "swing" as an open box for a really good price for my newborn. We have been using this now for 5 months.

~PROS~
- No batteries needed - just plug it in.
- Locking adjustable bar that allows the cradle to be positioned anywhere from laying down to sitting upright.
- Seating belt is adjustable and secure.
- 5 speeds.
- 5 motions - Car Ride, Kangaroo, Tree Swing, Rock-A-Bye, Ocean Wave
- 5 nature sounds and MP3 plug in capability.
- Easy to use LCD display and buttons.
- Unique and clean look.
- Removable and washable nylon seat.
- Mobile with 3 stuffed and designed balls.
- Solid, sturdy construction.
- Bottom heavy and solid which gives confidence in moving it from one area to another.
- Very easy to assemble.
- Fairly compact size, especially compared to larger swings.

~CONS~
- Pricey.
- The fully upright position is fairly upright and there is a danger of the baby falling forward.
- Due to the nylon material of the seat the upright positioning puts a lot of pressure on the groin area.
- Not a traditional swing. This swing is limited to left to right and up and down motions.
- Limited range of motion due to its design.
- Sound quality of speakers is not very good.
- The fastest speed is still fairly slow, particularly compared to the fastest setting on a traditional swing.

~TIPS~
Do not leave your child unattended with the swing in its most upright position. If your child were to lean forward I think he/she may remain stuck in that position.

~CONCLUSION~
Weighing all of the pros and cons it was worth it especially given the price we paid for it - open box plus 20% off coupon.

product_title: Graco DuoDiner 3-in-1 Infant Highchair to Booster Sprout Collection SweetPea
review_headline: Overall a great chair with a few minor flaws.
review_body:
I have used this high chair for 14 months now and have been very happy with it. We have used it in the first two positions: reclined and upright. I cannot speak to its use as a booster seat.

Pros:
- I used this chair in the reclined position quite a bit before my son was sitting upright. Rather than putting him in a bouncer on the floor I would put him in his high chair while I was cooking or getting ready in the morning. This let him be up at eye level so he could see me and what was going on.
- Very easy to put our little one in the high chair. I almost never take the tray off, rather I recline the seat back, slip my son in and then move the back to the upright position. I take him out of the high chair the same way. This is nice because the between the legs support is attached to the tray and keeps my son from sliding down while I am getting the harness connected.
- Easy to clean. While the tray is dishwasher safe it is easier to hand wash it. I love the the cover is machine washable, I have gotten carrot and beet stains out of it with no issue at all. I am not very diligent about following the wash instructions and have accidentally ran in through the drier more than once. No issues there.
- Having a two layer tray is great! We frequently use the bottom layer of the tray if the removable tray hasn't been cleaned yet :)Also, for finger painting or coloring I will take the removable tray off and use the bottom layer for those activities.
- Can be easily slide around the kitchen or house. Some may view this as a con as it could move if your little one were to try to pull themselves up with it. For us this hasn't been an issue.
- It has a five point harness. At this point I primarily use it as a 3 point harness but when my son starts trying to stand up in his high chair we will start using the shoulder straps.

Cons:
- I wish the tray could be snugged in closer. There is a large gap between the tray and my baby's stomach where crumbs get caught. His bib catches the mess but older high chairs I have used were able to be adjusted in closer. I found this preferable.
- I wish the seat could be set upright just a few more degrees. Until these last few months I would stick a folded towel behind him so he was closer to the tray.
- Not a space saver or easily stored between babies. While the legs fold up the seat itself does not and takes up a lot of storage space.

product_title: Valco Snap 3 Single Stroller
review_headline: Buy this instead of the City Mini
review_body:
Everyone in this area seems to have a City Mini -- and after trying out this stroller, I don't know why! I did extensive research online to compare sizes, weights, and features. I also test-drove a number of strollers in the store, and liked this quite a bit better than the other options. A few points:

1. It is noticeably lighter than the City Mini and other strollers I tried out. One of the lightest "featured" (i.e., non-umbrella) strollers on the market. As I recall, the only non-umbrella stroller that gave it a run for its money in this category was the much more expensive Bugaboo Bee.

2. Very easy to handle and maneuver.

3. Extremely important to me was the small footprint; I was on a mission to find a narrow stroller that I can fit in cramped store aisles and between cars in parking lots. On this front, once again, the Snap was the obvious choice, comparable only to the Bugaboo Bee. I think it was 3" narrower than the City Mini and also noticeably shorter, but the seat dimensions for the child were still comparable.

4. The basket below is not huge, but that is a necessary side effect of the smaller footprint that I wanted. I have been spoiled by the basket on my Chicco KeyFit Caddy, but this is totally serviceable. The City Mini basket is slightly larger due to the larger frame on the City Mini, but the Snap's basket actually seemed more functional: it is easier to access because it does not have a bar running across the back, which prevents bulky bags from fitting in the back easily. I've also been able to fold the stroller up with some items still stored in the basket (like my daughter's jacket and my carrier); this is really nice.

5. The folding mechanism is admittedly slightly less easy than that on the City Mini, but still very easy to do (no complaints on that front). I think this is a fair trade because it folds with the seat is on the inside, so and dirt, muck, and debrisis not going to get on the seat. Also, it means that I can leave a toy strapped onto the bar and folded inside, and items stored in the basket, when I fold it. These are real timesavers; I'm not sure this would be possible on all strollers.

6. It's very easy to recline or sit upright, allowing my daughter to sit up and look around or nap/get a diaper change.

7. I like the mesh viewing windows on the top and back to give airflow. Very important on hot, humid days.

I wish the handle were adjustable, and I had to buy an after-market "parent caddy." But I'm very happy with my choice! I'm on a proselytizing mission to get people to buy this stroller.

I also want to add that you can get this for 1/2 the cost on other websites. Just do a search, it's still not worth that price in my opinion.

product_title: Safety 1st Eco-Friendly Nature Next Bamboo Gate, Bamboo and Black, Fits Spaces between 28" and 42" Wide
review_body:
I was SO tired of my Great Dane and my Pomeranian getting into the cat litter box. Cat litter everywhere, the house smelled like poop, the dogs smelled like poop and the cat was not happy.

ENTER GATE! No more cat litter dragging over the floor! No more poop bits on the floor! No more smelly dogs or house. Best idea ever.

The gate itself is very nice and looks great between our dining room and laundry room. The latching gate was a little tricky at first (I actually had to read the directions), but fits nicely in place. And you can't beat the price.

The only downside I would say is that the grooves for the latch are wood and if you are in between sizes it might be difficult to get a \\"perfect\\" fit.

product_title: Summer Infant Keep Me Clean Disposable Potty Protectors
review_body:
Pros:
- Size is good - big enough to hang over the edges a few inches without being so large as to be wasteful.
- I like the weight, which is just a bit heavier and quite a bit softer than the freebie covers you find in some restrooms. Moderately substantial without taking up much space in a handbag, and they don't completely fill the personal hygiene bin in the ladies bathroom stall, which is where I'm tossing them once used.

Cons:
- I'm not a major germiphobe, but when my not yet three-year-old sits on split public toilets, one leg or the other falls into the split, which is often filthy. Even when clean, the awkward position makes her nervous and she wants to get off before she's done what we came to do. I thought these would keep her clean and keep her legs at the same level, but the little sticky tabs are close together on the bottom and they both land in the split, where there's nothing to stick them to! Without using the tabs, it's much harder than I antipated to keep the cover in place while I sit her down (too far forward and it doesn't cover the split, too far back and there's no clear shot into the toilet, too far to one side or the other and the cover falls in the toilet - and it's not flushable. Ick. The only thing I haven't tried yet is turning the cover around so the tabs stick to the back end of the toilet, but...
- Once so far I've been able to use the tabs and as others have said they were too sticky. I was actually trying to scrape the glue off with my fingernail. But really, that's kinda gross, so I gave up and left the sticky seat for the next user, which is kinda rude.

product_title: Medela Harmony Manual Breast Pump
review_headline: Works well and is easy to use
review_body:
I have two Medela pumps, this manual one and a Pump In Style. I actually seem to get more out of the manual than the PIS, but I double pump at work and think it would take too long to pump manually while there. This is nice to use at home and is convenient if you're on the go and don't want to lug around the electric pump. I originally thought there was something wrong with it, turned out to be a user error, but anyways, I contacted Medela's customer service and they're awesome.

If I had to do it again, I would just buy this manual pump and rent a hospital grade. Even though I own this and the PIS, I started to not get a lot out of the PIS and it would take forever to pump, so I rented the Medela Lactina. The Lactina is awesome, and to rent it would be just a little over what I would pay for the PIS. Plus it saves time and is faster. I'm still pumping at 8 months and I know your supply can diminish at that time, but with the Lactina it's thankfully coming back.

product_title: Graco NasalClear Nasal Aspirator, 1 Count
review_body:
This may be a bit pricey for a snot-sucker, but this was--dare I say--life-saving!

My son came down with RSV at two months old. It wasn't too bad to the point he was hospitalized, but the doctors said there was nothing they could do until he couldn't breathe. He was horribly congested, I felt so bad!! The blue bulb the hospital gave me when he was born wasn't working.

So I bought this on a whim, and used it right away when it arrived. He doesn't cry when I use it on him, and it cleared up a LOT of junk in his nose. I won't say the RSV went away because of this, but he could breathe a lot better because of it.

Can't compare it to the Swedish snot-sucking thing, I haven't used that one yet. But I LOVE this!!

One thing--it's been about a week since I used it, and when I used it yesterday, it stopped. Almost like it got stuck on something. I kept pressing the button for a minute until it seemed to get \\"unstuck\\" and start working again. Someone else in the house may have used it and not cleaned it, that's my guess. make sure you clean it.

UPDATE: I don't know if I'm cleaning this as well as I should have been. It's been about 6 months now, and the thing seems like it has stopped for good. It got stuck in the past, and i got it unstuck, except for this time. And right before it stopped working, it makes this awful burning smell when used. I clean it almost every time I use it, but maybe it's not good enough. It still gets krud stuck inside the machine that I have a hard time getting to.
I bought another one, because it really works better than the bulb, and since I'm by myself a lot, I just can't use the nose frida contraption, it requires at least two hands.
I read a suggestion to try and clean this by sucking in warm water, I'll try that on this new one to see if that's what I'm doing wrong.
I still like this, but the cleaning part of it is very frustrating...

product_title: Tommee Tippee Closer to Nature Newborn Starter Set
review_body: My great friend was starting to have her milk dry up so she made the hard choice to switch to formula. Her daughter had been purely breast fed for 3 months already. She tried both enfamil and similac without much change, so I suggested maybe it was the kind of bottle. She tried a couple different bottles she was given and still her daughter would be so angry at feeding times. As I was trying to feed her I noticed that she just seemed to not be able to suck appropriately on the bottle. We went to the store and got some Tommee Tippee bottles and instantly it was a difference! Instant latch on! Her daughter now has a bottle she will always take and the formula wasn't the problem at all. It made the emotionally hard transition much easier because of no more angry baby.

product_title: Munchkin Sesame Street Click Lock Insulated Straw Cup, 9 Ounce
review_headline: Just give your kid the regular bottle of juice/water - at least you know what to expect (spills)
review_body:
Like other reviewers, I can confirm, this cup is terrible. I reviewed the straws separately, so figured I'd add to the cup.

Our cups don't leak, it's the straw - so we've never had an entire cup leak, but small amounts everywhere.

The straw, when properly setup inside the lid, keeps liquid from coming out, but unfortunately, it also keeps liquid from returning to the cup. That means that as your child drinks from the straw, some liquid is left inside - and that liquid leaks, sprays, splatters and makes a mess. I have lost count of how many times I've been sprayed in the face because the straw gets bent and released.

Today was the last \\"straw,\\" I'm done being sprayed in the face and cleaning up spills and splatters off the floor. I will be throwing our 3 cups out tonight and am placing an order for something better, which will probably just be a simple sippy cup.

review_body:

review_headline: So beautiful and easy to put together.

But I don't always trusst what other people say and I am so glad I didn't. If you don't put the drawers in the right placement area then yes it will look bad and have openings that shouldn't be there (I noticed that on one review I had read). It is beautiful, sturdy, and even comes with a safetly bracket to attach to the wall, in case your child is a climber, so it will not fall on top of them. I recommend for everyone. product_title: Okkatots + Travel Baby Depot Bag + Travel Diaper Backpack + Navy + 19" x 15.5" x 8.5"
review_headline: why didn't I get this diaper bag backpack sooner?
review_body: As a new mom, you don't know what you're looking for in a diaper bag.  I went with a Coach one that I got at an outlet center.  It had two sides split with an inside zipper pocket, as well as two outside pockets and two specific spots for bottles.  I tried to keep it organized, but there was real no way since like your purse, things get thrown inside.  My husband always complained when I asked him to get something out of it.  It wasn't a doubt in my mind, I had to spend the money on this backpack.  And I am so glad I did.  It has so many pockets and departments, that it's almost impossible to not stay organized.  I have fit twenty to twenty-four size 3 diapers in the diaper spot. I don't use the provided changing pad, but rather pack a Kushies Deluxe Flannel Change Pad since I can fold it and it doesn't take as much room.  I comfortably fit three tall Dr. Brown bottles in the insulated bottle pocket.  And for now, I use the outside DVD player pocket for my wallet/change purse.  On the strap, it does have a cell phone mesh holder- I have the iPhone and it fits, but snuggly, so if you have a cell phone bigger than an iPhone, it won't work. I normally put my phone in one of the outside side mesh pockets.  I love that it's a backpack and put it on my back so I can have all available space in the shopping cart for a weeks worth of grocery shopping.  Or that I put it on my back and get my son out of his car seat without it falling off of my shoulder like my previous diaper bag would. When set down, the backpack keeps its form which I also like very much.  If you're a new mom trying to decide what type of diaper bag you want, or you're not happy with your current bag, then look no further and get this backpack.  You won't be disappointed.

product_title: The First Years Breastflow Starter Set
review_body:
I enjoy my sanity. Really, I do. If you, like me, enjoy your sanity, then I would recommend buying a different kind of bottle.

The bottle will leak. All over. Read other reviews - it happens to everyone. It will not leak all over on your best day. It will not leak all over when you're hanging out in the park, having a great time with your friends. It WILL leak all over:

(a) the day before you're leaving for a very long trip;

(b) the day before you're leaving for a very long trip and realize that you don't have enough clothes that actually fit;

(c) the day before you're leaving for a very long trip, you realize that you don't have enough clothes that actually fit, and your baby screams for most of the day because he's getting his first tooth;

(d) the day before you're leaving for a very long trip, you realize that you don't have enough clothes that actually fit, your baby screams for most of the day because he's getting his first tooth, AND your husband calls to tell you he has to work late.

On that day, my friend, is when this bottle will leak all over your last clean shirt.. It will also spray your screaming child in the face with milk. I don't know why.

Save your marriage. Save your sanity. Buy other bottles.

product_title: Diaper Genie Essentials Diaper Disposal Pail withStarter Refill, 100-Count
review_body:
Hi - let me just say that I do not write many reviews, but I had to about this product. I am writing as a parent that has been stuck, and I mean stuck, with this contraption for over 17 months now. I was warned by a patient that if you get this item, then get used to having to push the diapers down into it. I took that warning, but we received this at the baby shower, before I could update the list and remove it.

Ok so here it is. The concept is nice and if you only put a few in the genie by emptying it often, then you will probably be okay. If you have a busy lifestyle and do not have time to empty every day, then you might want to reconsider. I find that I have to repeatedly push the diapers down into the genie and whenever I step on the lever to make a deposit, I can smell the previous deposits. There are other disposal systems out there, and you should definitely consider them. This is popular and the refills are readily available, but I am not a fan of the Diaper Genie.

My wifes cousin had twins and purchased a diaper disposal unit that has a lever that turns the deposits. My wife and I were impressed by the lack of odor in the room and by how easy it was to dispose of the diapers. And there was definitely no need for touching the diapers or pushing them down after the deposit was made.

product_title: Badger Basket Baby Changing Table with Six Baskets
review_headline: Not as well structured as it looks in the product photo.
review_body:
I've never written a public, negative review of a product. There's a first time for everything...

Words cannot describe the seething, firey hatred I have for this item. I have hated it actively, several times a day, every day, since I brought my first baby home in January 2011. When I looked at the pic, I presumed that the \\"baskets\\" sat on full, shelf-like dividers, like soft-sided drawers that just aren't connected to the unit. I even figured you didn't have to use the baskets, you could just take them out and use the shelves instead. That's not at all how this piece is designed. The only \\"shelf\\" is the top, where you put the changing mattress. Below that is just what I'd call a \\"skeleton\\"--kind of like staging?--designed to hold the baskets in place. In other words, see those two horizontal black lines in the picture that appear to be pieces of wood that separate the three \\"drawers\\" from one another? They're just shadows. Seriously. If you enlarge the picture and strain your eyes, you'll see there is NO WOOD THERE. The picture is just taken to make it *look* like there's something there.

So fine, I misinterpreted the photo. My bad. But without these separations, the unit is more or less useless. Instead of sitting on platforms, the baskets hover over each other on these thin little runners--just one on each side. The problem is that the gap between the runners is prolly about 1/16\\" wider than the basket, tops. So if you don't balance the basket on the runners PERFECTLY, one side will collapse down into the drawer below it. This happens just about every time you open and close a drawer. And the issue gets worse as time goes on and the baskets start to warp a little bit from use. The 400th time you're struggling to yank open a misaligned basket with one hand while wrangling a crying baby with the other, you'll understand my ragey hate. Ragey, ragey, flaming, sparkly hate.

Do Not Buy This. If you insist on having one, please, for the love of all that's Holy, come take mine. Take it far, far away. You would be doing me a great service.love of all that's Holy, come take mine. Take it far, far away. You would be doing me a great service.

product_title: Angelcare 4 Piece Baby Video Sound and Movement Baby Monitor System Ac1100, Gray/White (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Video Quality is Very Subpar, Expected Better from Angelcare
review_body:
I had the audio Angelcare monitor with my first child and loved it! I decided I wanted video this time around and naturally went with the Angelcare Video Sound and Movement Baby Monitor. I am sorry to say that I am really not impressed.

Things I like:
The audio functionality is great, easily adjusted to eliminate secondary noise (like our Calm Baby CD), and comparable to the audio only version. The movement sensor is a nice option to give you a piece of mind (we have not hooked ours up yet, so I can't really speak to it). There is a timer option to keep track of how long your baby has been asleep (only goes as high as 5:59). I also like the room temperature being displayed.

Things I don't like:
Video quality is pretty bad. The screen is incredibly grainy and very difficult to see. It seems like everything is moving in slow motion. To give you a couple of examples: 1) I can tell my daughter has a binky in her mouth, but it's difficult to tell if she is sucking on her bink 2) depending on which way her head is positioned, I can't tell if her eyes are opened or closed. As others have mentioned, the infrared sensors get confused in low light situations (we have a blackout shade for naps) and the screen keeps flipping from day to night vision and vise versa. If it stays in day vision in low light, the video is essentially unusable. The sensors keep resetting every few seconds so the screen keeps going from red to sepia to black and white every 15-30 seconds or so.

There is zoom mode, 2X only, that makes the image in low light look honestly like something resembling ultrasound pictures. You can also move the camera slightly in all four directions.

The Vox option (Voice Activated Mode) does not work like I'd expect. I would expect that if my daughter starts making noise, depending on what the sensitivity is set to of course, the video screen would come on immediately if it was off. This is not the case.When the monitored is triggered and the screen is asleep, the sound comes on, but the screen remains off. So in the middle of the night you have to reach for the monitor, find the \\"on\\" button for video and turn it on. That's just silly.

Video sleep mode is aggravating to deal with. Sometimes you want the monitor on for an extended period of time and sometimes you don't. There are at least five touch screen buttons to press (a menu within a menu) to reset the time for sleep mode activation (0-20 seconds). I want to be able to override sleep mode from the front screen without having to jump through two menus.

This thing needs a tripod for mounting. I can't imagine placing it anywhere but really close to or on the crib. I think the video would be even worse. I know tripods are cheap, but at this price point I shouldn't have to deal with it.

Battery life is terrible. It does not last long the day without needing to be recharged, which means that the charger needs to be moved from my upstairs to mine downstairs daily, unless for a period of time I go without the monitor.

Very disappointed overall and will be returning it promptly. I was actually trying to figure out how this monitor has such glowing reviews and my thought is that most reviewers are so happy with the sensor function, that everything else doesn't matter. If you want a true video monitor, I would recommend getting one that actually has good video quality and buying a separate sensor pad to give you that extra piece of mind. Afterall, you'll be using the video aspect for much longer than the sensor pad.

product_title: Carter's 4 Pack Wrap Me Up Receiving Blanket
review_headline: Do you understand what you are ordering?
review_body:
I've read some comments about these receiving blankets which make me wonder whether the reviewers understand what a receiving blanket is.

A receiving blanket is a thin, lightweight, inexpensive piece of fabric which derives from the simple plain cloth once used to wrap newborn babies. Originally plain white, most are now printed on one side to make them "cute". It's actually a CLOTH, not a BLANKET. But the name is accurate, not misleading advertising. They've been called receiving blankets for decades.

If you think that a RECEIVING BLANKET is the same thing as a CRIB BLANKET, your confusion is probably going to create unrealistic expectations that will cause you to be unfair to Carters, a top-of-the-line provider of infant supplies.

A crib blanket is a much more substantial, much heavier, much thicker, much more elegant, and considerably more expensive critter. It is truly what we usually think of as a blanket.

Now, if you think that somebody is going to sell you 4 crib blankets for 10 or 15 bucks, you are hopelessly misled. For this kind of money, you are going to get exactly what you ordered -- 4 very nice quality receiving blankets.

Some of the comments are sadly clueless -- they read like "I ordered a subcompact and I'm angry that they didn't send me a luxury vehicle."

product_title: Baby Jogger POD Chassis
review_body:
I have three kids, ages 7, 5 and 2. The 7 and 5 year old are petite. My husband and I recently started a jogging program, and we needed a solution for bringing our kids for our assignments. We borrowed a single BOB and hoped we could have the big kids bike while we jogged, but that wasn't happening.

We purchased the double Croozer over the POD at first, for two main reasons, it was bigger (for our older kids comfort) and it was cheaper... but mostly because of it's giant size, that thing had to go back. We live in an apartment. Not going to happen.

So far, we've only bought the jogging kit. It fits in our van next to the BOB, which is great because we need both to fit in our van's trunk to go running. It's really easy to fold, which is big because we need to get it out of the car a lot. The seat and straps are well padded but it is bench seating and there is no suspension built into the chassis itself. We've seated our 7 year old an 2 year old in it several times, and although very snug, they do fine together. The 7 year old complains after about 30 minutes because her bottom hurts, though. The 5 and 2 year do well. The 5 year old falls asleep a lot and it stinks that there's not a recline or good head support.

Pushing it isn't terrible. Mostly my husband does it, but I've used it for some runs it's really not much worse than the single, even with 70 lbs of kids. I'm 5' 3" and would prefer the lower setting of the handlebar for normal strolling, but for jogging I like it higher. At it's high setting it's the same height as the BOB. The jogging wheel feels sturdy, but it's not quite as 'fixed' as the BOB. It actually is lot easy to do corners at a slow pace than the BOB, but when you go to a higher speed, it gets hard to keep straight. We're slow runners, so I like it :)

The size is really nice though for storing, maneuvering through doors and running. Really, I would call it about a 1.5 seater, but we make it work.. They really tried to maximize the cabin to frame size though, which is awesome. The wheels don't really extend past the cabin area, which is well designed.

Attaching the wheels is super easy, and I love that the brakes don't need to be set up everytime. The brakes work great for controlling the speed going downhill. The parking brake is fine, but setting it can be difficult. It pops up flush with the fabric when disengaged so not only is it hard to grab with my foot, but it make me drag my foot all over the fabric. I'm hoping it doesn't damage it with more use.

The front mesh panel zipper can be reached by my toddler, who sticks his finger in and unzips it while we're running. A little annoying but a safety pin fixed that.

My biggest complaint... for this price, it should come with the stroller kit. I understand not everyone will do both biking or jogging, so kits for those is reasonable... but everyone could find a use swiveling wheels if they were included. I'd love to have it as an option, but it's just not worth the cost of another stroller for wheels that should be included already. It just seems like a professional thing to do.

Overall, it's a good stroller and I hope to get many more years out of it, but there are enough complaints that I think it lands it in the 3 to 4 star range.

*** Update 4/4/16 *** So we've had this thing for 3 years now! Maybe it's the pain of the cost has wore off, but it seems so worth it now. We ended up buying the bike kit and stroller set when I saw them go on sale.

The bike attachment works well, and once assembled, it's easy to use. It's really great not to have to store both a jogger and trailer, and lately I've been switching between the two weekly. I've never used a trailer on a bike before, and I haven't had a problem using it. Actually I really love taking it on rides.

As much as I though I'd use the stroller kit... Istill haven't! For most "outings" it's a lot easier to take a sit and stand or regular stroller.

The jogging wheel is still working great and was pleased to find works well on snowy roads/trails. I've had no issues with the tires at all... and the fabric is still going strong with little wear.

But really, the reason I update... we had a baby recently. I was worried with no recline we would have to find a different jogger until she got older, but through some trial and error, I found a solution. I place her rearfacing in her bucket carseat in the pod. I tuck the seat handle down into the pod feet area, giving it support where there is no bench. The two outermost lap straps extend far enough that they can connect in the carseat brackets on top of the seat (normally used for base-less installs). Finally, I zip the mesh up around the seat. It's not the most glamorous install, but it gets the job done in a fairly safe manor. I can even see her face through the window while I'm running. I attached a few pictures of the setup. I also attached picture of the middle two when they were 3 and 6, a little snug, but still a good fit.oller. I simply adored cloth diapering my first two children; and after selling all my supplies, I find out I'm expecting #3! I love how easy and durable Thirsties wraps are. review_headline: Would have been wonderful had it not arrived with holes

On a quick wash cycle with nothing else in the washing machine. After putting it on the pillow, I discovered a tiny hole in the middle of the fabric (not on a seam)... I considered returning it but didn't because I really needed a cover on my pillow. Over the next week, I found three more holes (all small, but that's not the point) and a place at the seam that needs repairing. I wish now I would have returned it for the first small hole I found. Really unacceptable. Next time, I think I'll attempt to make my own cover.

product_title: BABYBJORN Potty Chair
review_headline: Not what it is cracked up to be
review_body: I bought this potty chair for my 15 month old little boy who has already started to potty in the big potty with help and loves it. I thought he would love his own potty, so I bought him this one based on the great reviews. Unfortunately he can't sit on it by himself because the splash guard is in the way. In addition his favorite thing about it is that he can remove the inner potty part and spill the contents all over the place. He figured that out right away and it has been a struggle to keep him from making a mess each time since. That may be fun for baby, but it's quite stressful for mommy!

product_title: 1 X Disney so Sweet Pooh Valance by KidsLine
review_body: I used this affordable valance (I bought two, as there is a VERY long window in my daughter's room) to accompany an unrelated bedding set (Jungle Jill) and the colors are a PERFECT match. I was not willing to pay the outrageous price for the valances that matched the bedding and this set is durable, it ironed beautifully, and looks playful and wonderful in her bedroom. For two valances on Amazon, I paid half of what I would have paid for one of the matching ones in the store. In addition, the center area between the bottom and top hemming of the valance is an open area that allows for stuffing if you'd like, so I've stuffed the area with tissue paper for a fun ballooned look that perfectly fits the motif of a young girl's nursery.

review_headline: Pretty, but not large enough for my needs
review_body: I ended up returning this and keeping the Skip Hop Grand Central, because I need a BIG bag.  The bag appeared to be well made and was very attractive, I just needed something a bit larger.

product_title: HALO Big Kids SleepSack Lightweight Knit Wearable Blanket
review_body: My kiddo has been wearing Halo SleepSacks since she was an infant. When she was little, getting into her SleepSack was a key part of our bedtime routine, and she loved to kick her little feet in it. I've purchased several SleepSacks and Swaddles as baby shower gifts. I really love them! But infants grow into toddlers, so when my girl started standing in her crib and taking her first steps, we graduated to an Early Walkers SleepSack. And of course, we are now on to the Big Kids size. Little Miss just graduated to a big girl bed (I'm so grateful that we got a convertible crib), which means all new bedding. But full size bedding is HUGE for this little person, so she gets all tangled in her sheet and kicks off her comforter. Though the weather has warmed up (it's April when I'm writing this), it's still chilly at night, so she needs SOMETHING to cover her up... the Big Kids SleepSack keeps her warm, but has feet holes so that she can walk around in it when she wakes in the morning. She has been requesting \\"no socks\\" lately at bedtime, so the holes are also great because her little feet don't get too hot. I got the 4-5T size because I'm frugal and I want her to be able to grow into it. She's 2 and is wearing 3T clothes for the most part. The sack is pretty big, but I was expecting that because I got the bigger size. She can still walk around in it, which is all I care about!

review_body: What can I say; this is a precious theme and just as beautiful out of the bag as it is in the picture. We liked the theme so much we remodeled the entire nursery to match the display room! The bedding is nicely made, no snags, and I can't wait to see my little girl in her crib!

product_title: Safety 1st Newborn Nasal Aspirator
review_body: this product is a waste of money.  It doesn't even suck back anything when you squeeze it.  Buy the hospital size/grade larger ones - those work.

product_title: Fisher-Price Discover 'n Grow Kick and Play Piano Gym (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: My daughter was 3 months when she got this for Christmas and she loves it! She is now 5 months old and still enjoys it quite a bit. It's wonderful in many ways -- 1) it encouraged her to reach for and grasp objects (the toy bar has nice sized toys for little hands); 2) it encourages activity with kicking the piano and rewarding that exercise; 3) you can put the toy bar down for tummy time and you can take the bar off and put it on a blanket; 4) you can sit the piano up once the child is sitting independently (which my daughter has almost mastered so we're switching the position of the piano soon). The toys easily come off the bar to take for traveling as well. The activity mat serves so many functions with only buying one thing. I'd highly recommend it - a great gift or a great toy to buy. I'm confident that my daughter will get many more months of use out of this product in one way or another.

product_title: Planet Wise Reusable Diaper Pail Liner
review_body: This was my first purchase and I loved it so much for my reusable diapers that I ordered a second for when one is int he wash. I use it in a medium sized trash can. review_body:

review_body: Goes great with the bedset and the baby loves watching it and listening to the music.  It was purchased to go along with the bed set and it looks good on the crib.

product_title: Gerber 2 Count Hooded Towel
review_body: Item delivered on time, was as described. LOVE IT!

product_title: Banana Fish Love Bird 4 pc Crib Set
review_body: I bought this for a friend for her baby shower.  It came very quickly and was just as described.  It is beautiful.

product_title: SwaddleDesigns Baby Lovie, Pastel Security Blanket with Chocolate Brown Trim
review_body: This is the second of these blankets that we've purchased for our son, who can not sleep without it!  It's super soft and really well made.

product_title: Bloomers Baby Diaper Cake
review_body: I purchased this diaper cake for my daughter in laws baby shower. It really was pretty and made a great center piece.  I guess I shouldn't have assumed that you could use the diapers once the baby was born. My grandson is now 7 months old and my daughter in law just now mentioned that when she tried to use the diapers, they were glued together so tightly that when she tried to gently pry them apart, the diapers would rip. review_body:
I received one of these as a baby shower gift and liked it so much I gave it as a gift to another expectant mom! There is a little nipple brush in the handle which comes in super handy! I had previously used a Dr Brown brush that started falling apart after a few uses. And constantly having to track down the little nipple brushes was a pain. This brush is wonderful! It fits perfectly into the Dr Brown bottles and the two sponges get everything clean.

My only complaint is that it topples over easily. It would be nice if there was a little weight added to the handle to help keep it upright.

review_body: Perfect for kiddo bath time. Keeps the water in, and is safe and soft in case it gets sat on or stepped on. Easy to clean. I only wish the little suction cup would stick to our tile wall so we could store it there when it's not in use, it'll only stick to the actual tub, not the tile.

product_title: Prince Lionheart Backseat Kick Mat
review_body:
This is by far the best kick mat out there. I did much research and picked this kick mat and was very pleased.
It is very durable and looks good too!

product_title: Delta Universal 6 Drawer Dresser
review_body: We bought this because it was the matching dresser for the Delta Canton Crib, which I give a definate 5 stars. This dresser was better than expected. Of course, I already had gotten the crib so I knew it would be just as nice, but it was still a surprise how much I love it! It was VERY easy to put together. product_title: Philips AVENT BPA Free Insulated Cup, 9 Ounce, Colors and Design May Vary (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
These are our favorite sippy cups. Our daughter loves them because they are brightly colored and have animals on them. We love them because they are insulated, break-proof, and for all intents and purposes, they don't leak.** The cap is very difficult to use, but fortunately unnecessary.

Pros:
* Very watertight.** We have thrown these in diaper bags willy nilly and never had a significant problem with them. My daughter is now almost 3 and has outgrown sippy cups for normal use, but these are so leak-proof** that we still use them for overnight. She takes the cup to bed with her and has cool water all night long. No other cup we've tried will not leak overnight.**
* Durable. My daughter had a single cup like this for over a year, and hauled it everywhere with her. It was practically a lovey. She dropped it countless times on the sidewalk. After over a year of abuse, it developed a small tear in the rubber of the mouthpiece, which she managed to peel away a bit more. At that point, we bought three more and put the original away. But we still use it as a backup. It's still working hard!
* The valve is simple, sturdy, and easy to clean. We've never had to replace the valve on our two year old abused cup.

Cons:
* The cap is stupid. It is extremely difficult for me to operate and impossible for a toddler to operate. We immediately removed the caps from all of the bottles and saved them for when we were packing spare water for a long trip (eg: car, plane, hiking backpack). When a cup is actively in use, the cap is a nuisance.
* With this listing, you have no idea what pattern you will get. Which seems a bit silly. But we ordered three at once and got three different patterns, all of them nice.

**Note: All sippy cups leak a little. It is the fact of sippy cups. Trying to find one that won't leak ever, yet will yield to a toddler is a lost cause. These will occasionally leak a few drops with normal use. We have foundthem more than leak-proof enough for our needs

product_title: Fisher-Price Apptivity Gym for iPhone & iPod Touch Devices
review_headline: Too light, too easy for baby to move
review_body:
This whole thing is so lightweight that a not yet 4-month-old baby was able to grab on to one of the legs and drag the structure closer so he could reach one of the toys. At 5 months, when kicking became popular, this toy was an utter pain because the baby would kick it out of reach (or worse, kick it at an angle until one of the legs bonked him in the face), and i'd have to straighten it out again, only for the whole routine to repeat endlessly. It's just too easy for even a very young baby to move around, and then get sad because they can't reach the toys. In this regard, it's vastly inferior to infant gyms with pads underneath that the baby lies on to hold the whole structure in place.

So let's say that you heed the American Academy of Pediatrics' recommendations to not give young children any 'screen time', and you're just using this as an activity center with a small, barely-reflective mirror which probably won't be lined up right for the child to actually see themselves. For that, this is a good toy, but not remarkable. The four hanging toys included in the box are nice - a rattle, a turning wheel, a spinning ball, and a keychain-type-toy. They're all animal themed, brightly colored, and so on. (Note: they're also made in China, so if product recalls make you nervous about owning anything from China that your child will almost certainly put in their mouth, you won't like this product.) You can take them off and use them independently, and if you clip them onto the side butterfly slots instead of the loops in the center, even the child can pull them off to play with them. Once your child can sit upright, the gym is still useful, unlike some other styles of infant gym. The arch is angled well for a seated child to swat at or grab the toys.

As for the apps, they're free to download, but not remarkable. They are more exciting if you tap the screen to make things happen, but for all but the largest babies the phone is just too far away for them to reach to tap when lying down. Otherwise, it's just colors and shapes and sounds in a small screen far away from baby's face.

It folds flat quite easily, if you need to put it away so you can use your floorspace for something else when baby's not using the gym. product_title: Graco Pack 'N Play Element with Stages, Oasis (Discontinued by Manufacturer) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
My granddaughter was too old for the bassinet in the highest position when I purchased this, but we are using it in the second position and she seems comfortable in it. She loves the mobile, which is really ugly plastic, with three little fabric star shapes. It would be easy enough to change out the shapes with new ones, and I plan to make a few so she doesn't get bored.

I bought the Graco because I wanted to take it down between visits and understood it to be quite portable, but it is not easy to fold up and put away, at least for this Grannie, so if you are looking for a supremely portable bed/play yard and haven't a lot of physical strength, keep looking.

We did not experience the off-gassing some others reported. I almost did not pick this one because of those reports, as I am very sensitive to plastic offgassing. I was prepared to return it, but none of us have experienced a whiff.

The changing unit definitely leans, and the baby rolls with the lean. We prop her in with a rolled blanket on that side while we're changing her. Graco needs to provide more support on that side.

Several people have mentioned getting an additional mattress pad to improve sleeping comfort. I expected to do that as well, if their concerns about comfort bore out--which they did--but Graco's safety instructions specifically tell us not to, without explaining why. It's too bad, because a thin sheet over the plastic and tubing is not at all comfortable for the child. I put a softer blanket under the fitted sheet, but only because I am always next to the crib while the baby is sleeping and can discover immediately if she is in danger of getting the sheet loose and pulling the blankets over her head.

For these reasons, I would not buy the Graco again, nor would I recommend it for someone who needs to put the baby down in one room and work in another. Nor would I recommend it for sleeping overnight, unless you follow their safety instructions to a T, which means no additional warmth or support under the baby.ions to a T, which means no additional warmth or support under the baby.

product_title: Graco Quattro Travel System with SnugRide 30 - Carlisle
review_headline: Overall, a good product with a few drawbacks
review_body:
For a newborn, this is a great product.

I am very pleased with the stroller. The car seat snaps into the stroller very easily, it looks great, the stroller is very easy to get out and put away, and the seat reclines easily for use with an older child. The only thing I would do differently is put some padding on the straps, which are kind of flimsy and uncomfortable for baby. You can buy pads so it's not a big issue.

The car seat has also been great. It was perfect for my newborn, it looks great, it is super easy to install in the car (once you figure out all the car seat latch system jargon for the first time), and it is really easy to adjust the straps to take the baby in and out. My biggest complaint is this - I specifically purchased the Snugride 30 for it's supposed ability to last longer in the baby's lifespan. What they don't advertise, though, is that it's really the baby's height, not their weight, that is going to mean they've outgrown the seat. My daughter is 10 months old and less than 20 pounds and she's at the height limits. Besides that, the seat may be rated so that it could hold a 30 pound baby, but I have no idea how you would get the straps over a 30 pound child because I can barely squeeze my 18lb daughter into them.

Overall, I still think it is a great stroller/car seat combo, but I think that advertising it for 30lb babies is a little misleading. I probably would have gone with the standard size seat instead of the big one if I had realized this ahead of time.

product_title: Leachco Back 'N Belly Chic - Taupe
review_body:
I bought this pregnancy pillow towards the end of the first trimester in my first pregnancy. I am primarily a back- and side-sleeper, so I was looking for a pillow that would encourage me not to roll over on my back. I read a lot of reviews to ensure that I bought the right pillow for such a steep price, and I have not been disappointed.

When I bought this pillow, I was having discomfort on the sides of my hips due to flipping back and forth all night, but since the pillow arrived, that has been alleviated. The sides of the pillow support my belly and back throughout the night.

At this review writing, I am at the end of my second trimester. I really love the pillow and have not slept without it since it arrived. Below I'll address some of the other concerns I read about when researching this product.

This "chic" pillow design (as opposed to the original Back 'N Belly pillow that Leachco put out) seems to have addressed the uncomfortable seam at the curve of the pillow. If I sleep too "high" in the bottom of the "U" shape, then it can put pressure on the top of my shoulder, but I adjust myself down an inch or two, and that solves the problem for me.

It is a large pillow, but my husband and I have been able to manage just fine in our queen size bed. He and I are both fairly tall (he is 6'2", and I am 5'10"), and the pillow takes up half the bed, but he reports that he still has enough room to be comfortable. When we have gone out of town, I pack it in a large duffel bag to bring it along. On the nights we have had to sleep in a double/full size bed, the squeeze with the pillow was much tighter. We have managed, but are always grateful to come back home to our larger, queen bed.

As I mentioned, I am tall, and I read that several women reported discomfort due to the "shortness" of the pillows "legs." They are indeed short; when I'm stretched out on my side,"inside" the pillow, the end of the pillow comes only just below my knees, but I have not been bothered at all by this. In fact, most times, I sleep with one of the pillow legs in between my knees for support; I find this very comfortable, and the length of the pillow's legs are not a concern then.

I somehow still manage to sleep on my back at some points in the night (I still find it very comfortable), but most of the time I am supported in a cocoon-like fashion by the pillow so that I am a little propped up instead of lying flat on my back.

product_title: Ubbi Diaper Pail
review_headline: New mom with immaculate house says...
review_body:
I received this diaper pail (in grey) as a shower gift, then I read many of the reviews on the product and started to be concerned that I may have made the wrong decision. I decided to be proactive with the following \\"issues\\" from other reviewers, and I must say, I have not had any problems with odor or bag removal. We have two dogs who are sniffers (Eng. Bulldogs) and miraculously they have not once been interested in the pail.

The first thing I did prior to the first diaper going in was drop an odor absorber in the bottom of the can (you can purchase at Bed Bath & Beyond or similar store) despite having to slide the opening to get a new diaper in, I have not have any issues with smell; I also am pretty religious about taking the bags out as not to have them overfill.

As far as the bag tearing, I've been using the white drawstring Costco trash bags and have not had any problem. When I change the bag, I air it open, push it to the bottom of the can, and then wrap it around the trash bag holder. Upon removal, I unwrap from the older, cinch the drawstring and voila! My husband nor I have not had one problem with tearing or removal.

Since I have not tried any other pail for comparison, I don't feel have the knowledge to give a perfect 5 stars, but I would certainly give it a 4 1/2! My more experienced mom friends are all impressed with this pail -- hope these tips help others!

UPDATE:
1) We have had the pail for over four months and there are two more things that I think would be helpful for those considering this pail. We have hardwood floors and the pail is all metal so it could slide on the floor - easy remedy - I had a bit of a sticky rug pad mat left and just cut a square to fit the bottom, works perfectly and pail does not slide.
2) My neighbor who has a 17mo old was so excited to see my Ubbi in person, (her son now loves to open up his Diaper Genie and stick his hand in it) so the locking feature on the Ubbi was something that she/we never considered to be a helpful feature, but it indeed is! Despite the expense, she purchased one and is very happy with the purchase. We also love the fact that you don't have to purchase special bags for the Ubbi, an expense that can get VERY costly as time goes by.

I'm now upgrading my review to 5 stars!

product_title: Eco Baba - Stainless Steel 12oz. Spout (Pink)
review_body:
Who doesn't want to limit their baby's exposure to harmful chemicals that plastic can release? Who wants to lug around heavy glass bottles and risk breakage? Who has searched in vain for the perfect silicone bottle? (Tried adiri too). Next best material for least potential of harmful chemical leaching is stainless steel. So I was excited to try this bottle. BUT:
1. VERY difficult to screw cap on properly. Sometimes it takes me 8 tries, sometimes just one. I used the advent nipples recommended, wet the plastic part that comes in contact with the base of the silicone nipple, tried very hard to line the threads up properly and ensured the cap was screwed evenly. Not easy in the middle of the night let me tell you!!
2. Fat bottle does not fit in conventional bottle warmers or normal sized mugs. You need a wide and deep bowl or huge mug.
Those two problems caused a lot of frustration, but I sucked it up and used it anyway b/c I don't want to use plastic. Hoping the designers can tweak it to make a perfect product.

Btw, pur bottles are also stainless steel and are slimmer so easier to warm, but even more difficult to screw top on properly. Leaked quite a bit even when it seemed perfectly screwed on. We used our eco baba for milk and pur for water only. The silicone adiri bottles that I used for my first born were great except difficult to fill without leakage, and difficult to warm even with the separate end caps. Company also not around anymore.

product_title: Samsung SEW-3036W BabyVIEW Baby Monitoring System IR Night Vision Zoom 3.5 inch
review_headline: Excellent features, expandable for multiple children
review_body:
I am a mother of two and this is my second video monitor. I had a Levana model previously that finally bit the dust and I was in need of a video monitor that could handle multiple cameras.

Major positives and perks to this monitor include:
- The audio can be muted while still viewing the video
- It has a VOX feature: the video and audio are shut off after 1 minute if there is no sound detected. (This feature is an absolute must! It allows you to sleep at night without a bright screen on or white noise from the audio portion but you are alerted if you are needed. I will never ever own a monitor without this feature)
- Video and audio quality are excellent
- Talk feature is handy especially with a toddler when you want to let them know you are coming to get them or tell them to settle down and go to sleep.
- It was incredibly easy to pair additional cameras and you can easily go from camera to camera or have it in scan mode where it will automatically switch between cameras every ten seconds.
- It has a zoom feature that I will probably never use but it is there if you care about it.

The only negatives I can say are:
- It is a pricey system especially when you add additional cameras at $99 each.
- The screen brightness doesn't dim much so when it comes on at night when in VOX mode it really lights up the room.
- A Samsung jingle plays when you turn it on. (a minor irritation)

All in all I am thrilled with the whole system and I would highly recommend it.

review_body:

product_title: Bright Starts Having a Ball Roll and Chase Bumble Bee
review_body:
My husband ordered this toy for our baby for Christmas. It looked like a cute toy that our child would have fun with. Everything was fine until we took the toy out of the box. As soon as the plastic tab was pulled from the battery compartment the toy promptly quit working. Thinking that perhaps the batteries chose that exact moment to go bad I got a screwdriver to attempt to replace them. The screw just turned and turned and would not come out. I worked on it quite a while before giving up and letting other people attempt to remove the screw. No such luck. Deciding that this toy was becoming more trouble than it was worth we contacted Amazon about returning this toy as defective. We were given instructions and a return label for returning the product. Just one more thing a parent that works full-time needs to deal with.

In the meantime a replacement Roll & Chase ball was shipped to us. My excitment about this quickly evaporated when I saw the condition of the replacement toy. The box was beat up and the ball was dirty and scuffed. Looked very much like a refurbished product. I was even more disappointed when I pushed the button to demonstrate the toy. It lit up and did what it was supposed to for about 2 seconds before cutting out. Ever the optimist, I thought maybe it would work once removed from the box. Once again as soon as the plastic tab was pulled out of the battery compartment this pile of junk stopped working. I wasn't even in the mood to try removing the screw to check the batteries. Once again we will have to go through the hassle of returning this product, only this time I DO NOT want another one.

We are extremely dissappointed with this product and the fact that one of the gifts that we got our baby for first Christmas turned out to be a complete dud. I'm just glad that our little one is too young to be dissappointed by this Christmas present. I would give this product zero stars if possible.

product_title: Bumbo Floor Seat
review_headline: 5 stars for the seat, 1 star for my daughter not liking it.
review_body:
When my daughter goes to daycare, she sometimes sits on the Bumbo seat they have. When I had the opportunity to order one for our own place, I jumped on it and couldn't wait for it to arrive. My daughter is about to hit 5 months, so I thought we may as well start having her sit up often. Plus, it'd be funny seeing such a tiny person sit in such a large living room.

When it arrived, I was taken aback by how heavy and sturdy it was. Indeed, the quality exceeded my expectations, and I was relieved to find it had the built-in seatbelt after meeting the recall corrections. However, when I put my daughter in, it took only a few minutes before she started squealing. I thought she was uncomfortable, so I shifted her around a bit, but she wouldn't be pacified. I tried again a few days later, but the same result. At the moment, it doesn't seem like she likes her own Bumbo very much. She currently has a diaper rash, so I'll try sitting her on the seat again once the rash's gone.

I looked again at the one at her daycare, and I realized it has the optional tray, which was used to prop up a mirror to keep her occupied while sitting. So I added the tray in my Amazon Registry and hope it'll distract her from concentrating on what she's sitting. I wish the seat actually came with it.

Otherwise, the seat itself seems great. It's built sturdily out of a foam material rather than a hard plastic as I initially thought, but is heavy enough with a seatbelt to keep my daughter from toppling over.

Hopefully she grows to like it, but not to the point where she no longer will fit in it.

Also, my son was not a real sweaty/leaky kind of baby, so I can't attest to how it holds up to those elements, but any sweat or leak stains that I did come across washed out no `problem & nothing ever got through to the mattress itself.

I have since purchased the full crib-size pad from this company for his toddler bed, & so far I am just as impressed with that one. It fits perfect & is a nice soft layer. It does have polyester backing under the organic cotton, so it's not 100% organic, but as far as I can read it doesn't have the polyethylene that most of the others have that is a concern to many parents.

product_title: Munchkin Nursery Projector and Sound System, White
review_body:
My daughter loves the Munchkin Nursery Projector and it does actually seem to help her sleep through the night. I have two complaints, both small and wouldn't stop me from recommending this to a friend.

1. When the voice activation sensor is turned on, the music and projector stay on all night, despite the timer being set and room quiet. If the voice activation sensor is off, the music and projector will turn off after the designated time.

2. The two sound options that play music, lullabies and Mozart, do not rotate to other songs automatically. The same song will continuously play over and over again unless you physically push the button, then the song will change. After 8 hours of "Hush Little Baby" it can get kinda old.

I have several positive things to say about this device. The volume control has a wide range, so you can set it to the perfect volume whether little one is awake or trying to fall asleep. The music/sounds are nice not irritating like some of my daughter's other toys. The projector works great, we have high vaulted ceilings and it reaches the ceiling without becoming distorted. It also creates a nice subtle glow in the room, functioning as a nightlight too. The device is small, lightweight and easy to move around. It plugs into the wall for power, so you don't have to change out batteries all the time or worry about it loosing power in the middle of the night. The power cord it comes with is a decent size too so you can place it in different spots around the room if necessary. Just be sure to keep the cord away from baby. I've accidentally stepped on the cord and the machine came tumbling to the ground a few times now and it still works.

He ended up using a knife to cut an odd piece of plastic off to get it to work. Then we put our 4 month old in the walker and noticed that her feet didn't touch. The final straw was when she was sitting in the walker this morning - the palm tree had fallen out AGAIN and so I pushed it down forcefully to get it to stay. I'm a woman, I didn't shove it with man strength, just pushed it hard to get it to stay in. When I pushed it the entire front part of the walker collapsed and scared my baby to death. Turns out the front bars that slide up and down to adjust the height came out of their track. She wasn't hurt, but it was enough to make me take her out of it and decide that we're NOT using it again.

product_title: THERMOS FOOGO Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel 10-Ounce Food Jar
review_headline: Ideal for keeping food warm, or cold, for several hours.
review_body:
First off, there are costlier variants of this model available, which seem to offer nothing more than some decorative stickers on the surface. We went for the basic, simple version, which does the job of keeping food warm. In my experience, if you pour hot food into this jar and then immediately close the lid, it will keep the food warm for at least six hours, in Bangalore weather. I say "warm" and not "hot" because after six hours when you open the lid, the food is still warm. I anyway do not expect it to be as hot as when the food was poured in six hours earlier, so no complaints here.

The jar is BPA free, as per the manufacturer, so that is a definite plus.
The mouth is wide enough for you to put your hand in to take out food from it without having to squish your hand to get to the bottom of the jar. The wide mouth is also a plus when it comes to cleaning, especially if you want to use cleaning pad and not a long-handle brush.
The jar's handle itself, I found, lends itself to easy gripping - what with its rubber grip - and opens without too much fuss. When handing it to kids, ease of opening is a definite issue to consider, both ways - how easy it is to close and how easy it is to close. Too difficult to open and the temptation to not close it tightly enough will result in either messy leaks or the food losing its temperature too quickly.

All in all, a most useful jar. Now it remains to be seen how long it lasts. Five years? Ten years? One year? It certainly looks solid and solidly designed to last five years, but let's wait and use and watch.

My husband has this idea that a well behaved Child doesn't need a leash and its a sign of bad parenting, blah blah. (He wasn't the one taking this journey to begin with) I happen to understand the attention span of a One Year old whom might I add, started walking on his actual Birthday (Yah! But Booo, lol in the travel department)

So there we (Little & I) are, in the airport, I also had the Go-Go Kidz car seat dolly thing (another lifesaver) and he (Little) was wanting to explore the spaces. A 0635 flight, I didn't want to stress too many people out if he started to freak out because I wouldn't let him out of his chair. So I did what any good momma would do, I hooked him into his Frog leash and we went for a walk as I gathered our bags he couldn't walk off. It gave me a peace of mind that the unthinkable wouldn't happen to my Sweet Little. It's a dumb little frog leash backpack but it worked for us.

product_title: Charlie Banana 2-in-1 6-Piece Reusable Diapers
review_body:
I would recommend these diapers to anyone with a new baby. I thought cloth diapering would be more annoying than it is. Charlie Bananas have proven to be better then other, cheaper brands; in regards to keeping leaks in and providing comfort. The materials are sooo super soft for the bum of my little one. I like how this brand has a little fold to keep the insert in place. I actually sometime reuse the outer cover and simply switch the insert/liner. I lay the insert/liner on top of the out cover and that way it can be interchangeable some of the time. You just have to make sure that the insert is tucked in to the diaper as your are snapping it up, otherwise the microfiber materials will work their best to pull the moisture to it. If it is tucked in the moisture stays in the diaper!

Also, on a side note... I have also been reusing wipes. I know that sounds sick, but it is not. Once I accidently washed a wipe because it got thrown into the diaper wash bag. When it came out of the drier it was like a thin cloth. We now we use all the wipes and use them not only as wipes, but inserts sometimes too. When the baby is old enought for solids we plan to use them as disposable inserts for certain diapering situations. It feels great to not have to spend oooodles of ooooodles of money each way on diapers and wipes. I am not stressed about loading my car and trash can up with tons of diapers. It never smells like poopy diapers in my house because I do laundry every other day. I am a real fan of cloth diapering :)

product_title: Angelcare Baby Sound Monitor, White
review_headline: Great monitor in a sea of mediocrity
review_body:
I just about threw in the towel trying to pick a baby monitor -- I read countless Amazon reviews and for every option, one review would say \\"This monitor is great!\\" and the next would say \\"This monitor is trash.\\" I was so frustrated that there wasn't a clear best. Well, I would argue this one is the best. I've used it in an urban townhome spanning three floors and a suburban environment with lots of baby monitor competition and this has performed flawlessly (I've actually used it in a home with another AngelCare monitor and they didn't interfere with each other).

My sister in law bought my second choice, the Sony Baby Call, and she had static and clicking problems from the start -- she finally gave in about a month ago and bought this AngelCare monitor.

The channel on mine will start to get a bit fuzzy after about a month or two requiring a channel change, but that has stopped the fuzziness every time. The channel changing process is a bit complex (requires button pressing on the base unit, so if we need to change after my child has gone to bed, we're out of luck unless we want to wake her).

Both units will take batteries, so we can easily pack it up and take it to grandma's or a friends house for the day without messing with cords. The temperature and nightlight on the base unit are also nice (we've found draft patterns in our house with the temperature indicator!)

We actually use the Snuza for breathing monitoring, but this is just a great basic monitor. Buy it.

product_title: Medela Lactina Select Hospital Grade Breast Pump - BPA Free #016SC01
review_body: I have breast fed two children to age 10 months so I know a thing or two about the absolute importance of a good pump if you are a working mom. My first child I used an Ameda Purely Yours double pumping system for awhile and it worked but took a long time and didn't seem to be doing a good job. I work in healthcare as a Physician Assistant and my employer had a hospital grade pump available for employee use. It was the Medela Classic. I was amazed by the performance and efficiency. I could get two 4-6 oz. bottles of milk out in 15 minutes (a necessity when you work in a fast paced career like mine). I used the Medela Classic through my first breastfeeding child. Then when I became pregnant with my son I was determined that I was not going to monkey around with a store bought pump and purchased a Medela Lactina with a car adapter and carry case. ( I had used one on occasion at the hospital that I work at and loved it as much as the Classic). I loved, loved, loved this pump. If you can afford to get a Medela Lactina pump, I strongly recommend it. It is a bit pricier than store bought but well worth it and you can always find a taker when you are done since there is no concern about contamination with hospital grade pumps. You will not be disappointed. This is the exact pump my employer (hospital) uses for lactation/nursing in postpartum women. Using a pump will free up your life considerably for when you want some Mommy time on the weekend. If you cannot afford to buy, I strongly suggest renting because this pump is so much better than anything available in stores. Good luck to all the breastfeeding mothers.

product_title: Britax B-Ready Stroller - Black - One Size
review_headline: Sighhh ... I want to love it but don't.
review_body:
I have a now 31 month old and a 4 month old. Upon purchasing this I truly believed I was buying something GREAT! Well ... I have been disappointed. We had a chicco with our first son and it was extremely easy to use. Easy to fold, easy to unfold, easy to lift the carrier, easy to place the carrier in the base. Within weeks, I was able to fold and toss in my SUV without a thought. EASY! It's been 4 months with this bohemith and I can't say I love it. We have a Toyota Highlander. I have the rear seats always folded flat so there is significant cargo room, yet, my interior is scratched up from taking this stroller in and out. I had the same car when using the Chicco. Chicco caused no damage. Further, opening and closing ... again, not easy. I'm not saying it's difficult, but with my Chicco, I never had to think about anything. I just did it. I can't do that with the Britax. Opening and closing it, the wheels sometime turn and get in the way.

Also, my 31 month old boy is not interested in the stroller at all. The attachments I purchased, wasted money. Not britax's fault, but I had hoped it would have worked out. The attachments are all solid and fantastic ideas. Oh well.

Further, the Britax Chaperone carrier I have is insanely heavy. I am 5'8 and consider myself strong, but, its just too much! Also, placing the carrier in the stroller isn't hassle free. you need two hands. It also won't fit into any of my local grocery stores shopping carts. Wal mart yes, Target barely; but nowhere else. But, it's one of the safest carriers so I put up with it.

The storage is wonderful! Which is great and necessary! It rides super smooth and is a breeze to push on any terrain.

I'm having a hard time rating this properly because in theory, this should be fantastic. However, after having the super easy Chicco I'm having a hard time loving this!

The cover does go over the stroller but with an effort, especially around the stroller's handles. Also, it should be a bit \\"taller\\", probably with an adjustable length via a string, so as to better cover the growing toddler's feet. My daughter will be two years old next month and her feet and ankles are exposed to the cold air.  Lastly, I hate the plastic, located in the front to allow the child to see ahead!!! review_headline: pretty cute but doesn't live up to the hype
review_body: I bought this for my one year old for Christmas after seeing this pop up on several award/top toy lists.  I was very interested in the singing and play aspects that were beyond what is offered with a traditional rocking horse.  My son liked it right away and wanted to ride it.  It is difficult for a child his age to get on and off on his own so I helped him.  He also had a tough time getting the \\"magical thingamabob\\" in and out of the mouth without help.  You have to push it in pretty far for George to recognize it is there and my son doesn't have the coordination or strength to do that.  The variety of songs is not what I expected.  There are two different modes and in each there are 4 songs about the same things. So it really feels like 4 songs total, not the 8 that were advertised.  And the biggest disappointment is how muffled the sound is.  It sounds like George is talking through a blanket, which obviously the sound box is inside but I think this could be improved upon.  All in all- it is very cute to look at, is a rocker with some extra features, but could be improved upon.
